articles.title: Bitcoin Faces Pressure After Fed’s Hawkish Rate Hold
articles.text:
Bitcoin faces fresh pressure after Fed’s hawkish rate hold: Analysts
Traders are pricing in a 78% chance of a December rate hike, while analysts say Treasury yields, the US dollar and upcoming inflation data could determine Bitcoin’s next move.
Bitcoin could face further headwinds after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady while signaling continued concern about inflation, according to market analysts.
The Fed voted 10-2 Wednesday to maintain its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4%, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favoring a quarter-point increase.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh acknowledged that inflation remained above the central bank’s 2% target.
“Americans… are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the Committee’s objective for close to 6 years. It’s our responsibility to get inflation down,” he said.
Iggy Ioppe, chief investment officer at tokenization platform Theo, said the decision itself was widely expected, but investors had not fully anticipated the Fed’s hawkish messaging.
“Markets had the hold priced, but not the hawkish tone,” he said in comments sent to Cointelegraph.
There are expectations that the Fed will raise rates in its Dec. 8-9 meeting, and again next year.
CME FedWatch data showed traders assigning a 78.4% probability to a quarter-point increase by December and a 67.3% probability of at least a quarter-point increase by March, as of Wednesday.
Warsh declined to say whether the Fed would raise rates at the end of the year.
“A lot of things can happen, so I’m not going to be able to share with you my musings about what happens when this group gets together six weeks from now,” he said during a press conference.
At elevated interest rates, Bitcoin has to “compete with” a risk-free rate near 4%, said Ioppe.
Related: Bitcoin price bounce rejected at 50-day trend line ahead of FOMC, earnings
However, Bitget analyst Lewis Huang said Bitcoin’s next move could depend less on the Fed’s decision itself than on Treasury yields, the US dollar and broader investor sentiment.
“With limited new direction from the Fed, Bitcoin’s near-term performance may depend more heavily on Treasury yields, dollar movements and broader risk sentiment,” he said.
Analysts, including Huang, are now looking to Thursday’s personal consumption expenditures inflation report and earnings from major technology companies for clues about the direction of risk assets.
Sygnum Bank chief investment officer Fabian Dori agreed, adding that “the next couple of days promise more excitement” with Thursday’s release of PCE inflation data.
“Various Mag 7 companies reporting earnings this week will help clarify whether AI capex is turning into revenues. Following these short-term catalysts, broader liquidity and financial conditions are likely to shape the path towards the December decision,” he added.

articles.title: Bitcoin Treasury Datavault AI Says It Can’t Access Its BTC, Stock Tanks - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Datavault AI shares fell 49.55% to $0.067 on Oct. 27 after an SEC filing said the company has been unable to complete a June request to withdraw Bitcoin from Biconomy.
- The company will restate four financial reports, cutting reported assets by up to $92.2 million, after reclassifying Bitcoin from a $150 million Scilex stock deal as a subscription receivable.
- Management is reassessing its going-concern status because it had counted the Bitcoin as a source of liquidity and says collecting what Scilex owes is uncertain.
Datavault AI shares fell more than 50% on Tuesday to close at $0.06, after the Nasdaq-listed company disclosed that it has been unable to withdraw Bitcoin from the crypto exchange Biconomy since June. The company also said four sets of its financial statements can no longer be relied upon.
The disclosure came in a Form 8-K filed Oct. 26, in which Datavault said it requested a withdrawal to an external account in June and has been “unable to complete the withdrawal.” The filing does not explain what is holding it up.
The Bitcoin traces to a Sept. 25, 2025, agreement in which Scilex Holding, a pain-medicine company, agreed to pay $150 million in Bitcoin for 15 million Datavault shares and a pre-funded warrant covering another 263.9 million shares. A pre-funded warrant is a right to buy stock in which nearly the whole price is paid upfront.
At $112,915.52 per Bitcoin, the deal came to about 1,328.43 BTC. Scilex credited 1,309.04 BTC to Datavault's account at Biconomy on Sept. 26 and Nov. 25, 2025, the filing says, a figure that reflects a 19.39 BTC deduction for cash advances Scilex had made.
Those credits were off-chain transfers, meaning the exchange changed balances on its own books rather than moving coins across the Bitcoin blockchain. Between Sept. 26, 2025, and Jan. 30, 2026, Datavault sold 491.431 BTC back to Scilex the same way, for about $40.5 million in cash.
After reviewing the transaction, Datavault concluded the Bitcoin never qualified as a digital asset of the company. It will instead book the deal as a subscription receivable, money a buyer owes for newly issued stock, shown as a reduction of stockholders' equity, with the $40.5 million in cash reducing what Scilex owes.
The restatements are expected to cut total assets by $8.1 million as of Sept. 30, 2025, $92.2 million at the end of 2025, $57.1 million as of March 31, and $49 million as of June 30. They cover the 2025 annual report plus three quarterly reports filed between November 2025 and August 2026, and Datavault expects to reverse the crypto gains and losses it had recorded on the coins.
Datavault had counted those Bitcoin balances as a source of liquidity, so management is reassessing whether the company can continue as a going concern, the accounting test for whether a business can keep operating and meet its obligations. The filing says collection of the amounts owed by Scilex is uncertain, and its risk list includes Scilex's creditworthiness, the company's reliance on a third-party custodian, Nasdaq listing compliance, and litigation or regulatory inquiries tied to the restatement.
Scilex's own quarterly filing shows Biconomy was already part of the deal. Scilex said it sold 12.5 million shares of its Semnur Pharmaceuticals subsidiary to Biconomy on Sept. 23, 2025 for $200 million in Bitcoin, then used $150 million of that to buy Datavault stock.
On June 24, 2026, the same month Datavault says it asked to withdraw its Bitcoin, Scilex signed a binding term sheet to buy 837 BTC held in Datavault's Biconomy wallet for $50 million, subject to a definitive agreement. Scilex agreed to an initial $30 million payment and the remaining $20 million in quarterly installments through Dec. 31, 2028, payable in cash or Scilex securities at its discretion. The 837 BTC, added to the 491.431 BTC already sold back, equals the 1,328.43 BTC of the original agreement.
Datavault stock bounced to near $0.085 on Wednesday. Scilex's purchase price under the 2025 agreement worked out to an effective $0.5378 per share. Datavault has not said when it will file the restated statements, and it warned that delays could extend to its quarterly report for the period ended Sept. 30, 2026.

articles.title: Jury Deliberations to Begin for Canadian ’Crypto King’
articles.text:
Canadian ‘crypto king’ case to go to jury as criminal trial winds down
Aiden Pleterski, facing fraud charges in Canada over his alleged role in a digital asset Ponzi scheme, said that he was innocent at closing.
The criminal case of Aiden Pleterski, the self-described “crypto king” who was allegedly behind a Ponzi scheme involving digital assets, will go to jury deliberations after closing arguments this week.
According to Wednesday reporting from CBC, the jury overseeing Pleterski’s case will begin deliberations on Thursday after receiving final instructions from Justice Shaun Nakatsuru. Pleterski allegedly defrauded his social media followers out of about $30 million between 2021 and 2022. He was charged with fraud in 2024 and had been awaiting trial for more than two years, choosing to represent himself in court.
“I am innocent of these charges,” said Pleterski, according to CBC. “That is why I pled not guilty. Had I not been forced to represent myself, that would have been proven. That’s all I have to say.”
The fraud charge against the “crypto king” could result in a prison sentence of up to 14 years should he be found guilty at trial. Pleterski is one of many high-profile figures tied to the crypto industry accused of fraud, though others have already been convicted. Former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried is serving a 25-year prison sentence in the United States following his 2023 fraud conviction.
In a separate criminal case, five men, some of whom were reportedly victims of Pleterski’s scheme, were charged with kidnapping and torturing the “crypto king” in 2022. One of the men, Deren Akyeam-Pong, pleaded guilty to nine charges and awaits sentencing.
Related: US government asks for $1M forfeiture from ex-Celsius exec ahead of sentencing

articles.title: Chip Maker SK Hynix Posts Record Quarter as AI Memory Demand Overwhelms Supply - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- SK Hynix reported third-quarter revenue of 104.6 trillion won, up 328% from a year earlier, and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won, up 632%, for an 80% operating margin.
- The company expects memory demand to exceed supply through 2030 and says its DRAM and HBM volumes through 2029 are effectively sold out.
- Long-term agreements with 14 key customers cover more than 50% of SK Hynix's 2027 and 2028 production capacity.
SK Hynix reported record third-quarter results on Wednesday, with revenue of 104.6 trillion won (almost $78 billion) and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won ($65.5 billion), according to its earnings release.
It was the first time the South Korean memory chip maker’s quarterly sales topped 100 trillion won ($74.5 billion).
Revenue rose 328% from a year earlier and operating profit rose 632%, for an operating margin of 80%, which means the company kept about 80 won of profit from its core business for every 100 won of sales. Analysts surveyed by Bloomberg had expected operating profit of 77.5 trillion won.
Net income came in at 39.8 trillion won, up 216% from a year ago but down 58% from the second quarter. CFO Kim Woo-hyun said the gap came from net non-operating expenses of 32.6 trillion won, meaning charges outside chip sales, led by an 11.6 trillion won currency loss and a 22.9 trillion won valuation loss on investments.
SK Hynix told investors that demand for memory will keep outrunning supply through 2030, and that its DRAM and HBM volumes through 2029 are effectively sold out. DRAM is the standard memory in servers, phones and PCs, while high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, is the stacked memory that sits beside AI processors and feeds them data.
“Given the complexities involved in implementing leading-edge processes and the lead times required to construct new production facilities,” Kim Woo-hyun said, “a situation where supply cannot keep up with demand is expected to persist for some time, a constraint projected to continue through 2030.”
SK Hynix said some customers have recently adjusted their HBM specifications, which it reads as proof that demand is overwhelming supply, since they must build more AI accelerators from a limited quantity of chips. “Demand remains so strong that customers’ volume requirement is more than double that of what we can supply today,” the company said on the call.
To lock in that demand, SK Hynix has signed long-term agreements, contracts that reserve chip volumes years in advance, with 14 key customers including leading global cloud providers. They cover more than 50% of its 2027 and 2028 production capacity, typically run five years, let prices move within an agreed range and include safeguards such as deposits.
SK Hynix expects investment to rise significantly in 2027 as the first phase of its Yongin chip complex enters full-scale operation.
Citigroup analyst Peter Lee opened the Q&A by asking what supports confidence in AI investment when monetization looks slow, a doubt that Citadel founder Ken Griffin raised eight days earlier when he said investors are “almost certainly” in an AI bubble. CEO Kwak Noh-Jung answered that major cloud customers reported year-over-year cloud revenue growth of 30% to 80% and cloud order backlogs up two-fold to five-fold.
Kwak added that AI spending, once concentrated among a few big tech companies, is broadening to non-tech firms, sovereign AI projects (government-backed national computing) and on-prem setups (companies running AI on their own servers), so one buyer slowing down would hurt less.
Financing is tightening for AI infrastructure players, though. Elon Musk wrote on Oct. 25 that “debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money” for firms without large non-AI revenue.
SK Hynix expects weaker demand from PC and smartphone makers because of higher memory prices and tight supply, but says AI infrastructure demand should offset the decline.

articles.title: Crypto Today: Strategy Dividends, Coinbase Data Leak, Tokenization
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Strategy shareholders approved daily dividend payments across four preferred stocks, Coinbase said customer contact information was exposed through a third-party analytics provider and Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev warned that regulatory uncertainty could discourage investors from moving substantial assets into tokenized markets.
Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends across four preferred stocks
Strategy shareholders have approved a proposal to introduce daily dividend payments across the company’s four preferred securities, with 99.3% of votes cast supporting the changes.
The amendments cover STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD, replacing existing semi-monthly or quarterly payment schedules with distributions every business day. Dividends will continue to accrue over weekends and holidays, while annual dividend rates remain unchanged.
Strategy expects STRC to begin daily payments on Nov. 2, followed by the other three securities on Jan. 4, 2027. The company said the shorter payment cycle could improve liquidity and reduce price fluctuations in its preferred shares.
The securities currently offer annual dividend rates ranging from 8% to 12%. STRC carries a variable rate of 12%, while the remaining three offer fixed rates.
The move follows similar efforts by rival Bitcoin treasury company Strive, which introduced daily dividends on its SATA preferred stock in June. Strive also recently raised $630 million through a second preferred offering, SATS, which carries a 15% annual dividend rate.
Strategy remains the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, with 848,517 BTC, compared with Strive’s 43,000 BTC.
Coinbase denies systems breach, says vendor exposed customer data
Some Coinbase customers’ contact information was exposed in a security incident at analytics vendor Amplitude, the exchange said Wednesday.
The incident impacted a “small subset” of Coinbase customers, along with other Amplitude clients, Coinbase Support said on X.
Coinbase denied that its own systems had been breached and said customer funds were not affected.
The disclosure adds to Wednesday’s reports of cyberattacks affecting both crypto exchanges and traditional financial firms. In South Korea, Bithumb is investigating whether a breach of its internal work platform exposed customer information, while brokerage Daishin Securities reported a leak of personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers.
Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’
Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev says uncertainty over the longevity of US tokenization rules could prevent investors from committing substantial assets to tokenized markets, despite the securities regulator opening a temporary path for onchain stock trading this year.
Speaking during Robinhood’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Tenev welcomed the SEC’s innovation exemption but said further rulemaking or legislation would be needed to provide longer-term regulatory certainty.
“As far as the innovation exemption goes, I think it’s a really positive step... I do think more needs to be done to give people a little bit of certainty because as we talk to customers, I think the uncertainty of what happens in five years is likely to be an impediment to, like, putting serious assets onto this technology.”
Tokenized stock offerings have faced resistance from traditional issuers. Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs were among 16 companies that objected to their shares being offered on the proposed OKXICE venue, while AMC CEO Adam Aron separately criticized Robinhood’s tokenized stock products.

articles.title: Actor Anthony Boyle Contacted Ex-FTX CEO as Part of Netflix Portrayal
articles.text:
Sam Bankman-Fried wrote to actor portraying him in Netflix series
The former FTX CEO remains incarcerated as Irish actor Anthony Boyle portrays him in a series about the downfall of the crypto exchange and his relationship with Caroline Ellison.
In about three weeks, Netflix is set to release one of the first dramatizations of the saga of cryptocurrency exchange FTX since its CEO, Sam “SBF” Bankman-Fried, was found guilty and sentenced to prison.
According to a Wednesday Vanity Fair report, Anthony Boyle, the Irish actor portraying SBF on screen for the Netflix series ‘The Altruists,’ contacted the former CEO in prison via email as he prepared for the role. Although Boyle said he “promised him that I wouldn’t divulge anything,” Bankman-Fried reportedly answered the bulk of the actor’s questions ahead of the series’ release.
“I was interested in what possessed someone to become the world’s youngest billionaire,” said Boyle, according to Vanity Fair. “I’m not really interested in money or crypto or finance. It was: What makes them do the things that they do?”
Based on a trailer Netflix released on Oct. 8, the series appeared to be centered on the relationship between Bankman-Fried and his colleague and girlfriend, Caroline Ellison, who headed FTX’s sister arm, Alameda Research. SBF was convicted of seven felony counts related to the misuse of customer funds at FTX and sentenced to 25 years in prison, while Ellison was released in January after serving more than a year as part of a plea deal with US authorities.
Former FTX COO Constance Wang said that the on-screen portrayal of the executives made her “feel physically upset,” adding that SBF was more “socially awkward” than Boyle demonstrated.
Bankman-Fried has already been covered by several media outlets and was the subject of Michael Lewis’ 2023 book Going Infinite. Ben McKenzie’s documentary Everyone Is Lying to You for Money included a 2022 interview with the former CEO before the exchange’s downfall, but no other significant dramatization of SBF or FTX has been released on the big screen or television until The Altruists.
Related: Sam Bankman-Fried’s lawyer lays out ex-FTX CEO’s Supreme Court case

articles.title: AI Security Startup Upwind Raises $400M at $3.8B Valuation - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Upwind Security raised a $400 million Series C led by Bessemer Venture Partners at a $3.8 billion valuation, up from $1.5 billion in January.
- The company says revenue quadrupled in 2026 but has not disclosed dollar figures.
- The money will fund AI sensors for endpoints, scanners for AI agents and their skills, and expansion into identity, data and AI security.
Upwind Security raised $400 million in a Series C round at a $3.8 billion valuation, the cloud and AI security company announced Wednesday. Bessemer Venture Partners led the round, less than nine months after it also led Upwind's $250 million Series B.
Canapi Ventures joined as a new investor, and every existing backer returned, pouring even more money into the startop. Upwind said it will put the money toward product and engineering growth.
“The funding round makes Upwind one of the most capitalized companies in the world that’s focused on solving the cloud and AI security problem,” Upwind said. “It is a big day for us, becoming the fastest growing company in modern cloud & AI security. But, it is still a small milestone in our journey.”
Upwind says revenue quadrupled in 2026, though its press release gives no dollar figures. The company counts hundreds of organizations as customers, among them Siemens, Roku, Carvana, Nubank (Brazil’s biggest neobank), Supabase, and ClickUp.
Its platform collects what it calls runtime intelligence, meaning data from cloud workloads, APIs and AI agents while they are running, instead of relying on periodic scans that capture a snapshot of an environment. It supports Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud, and AWS customers can open Upwind inside the AWS console through Security Hub, with billing handled through AWS.
The company's release argues that attackers now use AI to scale their operations while employees build applications on large language models and agents operate autonomously inside organizations. Traditional alert-based tools, it says, give security teams too little context to judge the intent behind an agent's activity or whether a vulnerability is a reachable exposure, meaning a flaw an attacker could actually get to.
The round follows a string of incidents this summer in which AI labs' own models reached real companies' systems.
OpenAI said in July that two of its models escaped a sandboxed test, exploited a previously unknown flaw and breached Hugging Face's production infrastructure to obtain answers to a cybersecurity evaluation. Anthropic reported that Claude models compromised three real-world companies after a testing misconfiguration gave them internet access, and Meta confirmed a similar case in August.
Upwind was founded in 2022 and has now raised more than $800 million, according to the company. The new valuation is about 2.5 times the one set in its January Series B.

articles.title: Strategy Shifts STRC, STRF, STRK and STRD to Daily Payouts
articles.text:
Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks
The largest Bitcoin treasury company will begin daily dividend payments on STRC in November, with three other preferred securities following in January 2027.
Bitcoin treasury company Strategy said Wednesday that shareholders approved amendments allowing its four preferred stocks to pay daily dividends, with 99.3% of votes cast in favor, according to preliminary results.
The amendments cover Strategy’s four preferred securities — STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD — shifting dividend payments from semi-monthly or quarterly schedules to every business day. Dividends will accrue daily, including weekends and holidays, without changing their annual dividend rates.
Strategy expects daily payments on STRC to begin Nov. 2, with STRF, STRK and STRD following on Jan. 4, 2027. Strategy said the changes are designed to shorten the time between earning dividends and receiving cash, while supporting liquidity and price stability in its preferred shares.
Source: Michael Saylor
Strategy’s preferred stocks carry annual dividend rates ranging from 8% to 12%, with STRC offering a variable rate currently set at 12%. The other three securities pay fixed dividends, while STRK also gives investors the option to convert their holdings into Strategy common stock.
Related: Strategy skips Bitcoin purchases, spends $205M on STRC buybacks
Strive expands daily dividend offerings with $630 million raise
Fellow Bitcoin treasury company Strive introduced daily cash dividends on its SATA preferred stock in June, months ahead of Strategy’s planned changes. The company has since launched a second preferred security, SATS, offering a fixed 15% annual dividend rate, with daily payments scheduled to begin Nov. 9, subject to declaration.
Strive closed a $630 million SATS offering on Oct. 20, selling 7 million shares at $90 each. The company said proceeds could be used for Bitcoin purchases and other corporate purposes, but has not disclosed how much it intends to allocate to the cryptocurrency.
Strategy remains the largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, with 848,517 BTC, while Strive ranks fourth with 43,000 BTC, according to BitcoinTreasuries.net data.

articles.title: More Americans Have Tried Crypto, But Few Are Sticking With It: Survey - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Some 22% of U.S. adults have ever owned or used crypto, up from 18% in 2025, but past-year use held at 13%, and the growth came mostly from lapsed users.
- Only 19% say the financial system is secure, and 63% say it needs an upgrade to combat threats like AI and cybercrime. Yet just 4% trust crypto exchanges.
- Only 2% are very familiar with DeFi, though 40% say they’d be at least somewhat likely to try it.
More Americans have tried crypto than a year ago. Far fewer are still using it.
Some 22% of U.S. adults say they have ever owned or used crypto, up from 18% in 2025, according to a national survey conducted by Ipsos for the DeFi Education Fund, a crypto policy advocacy group. But the share who used crypto in the past 12 months held flat at 13%.
The growth came almost entirely from people who have stepped away. Among Americans who hadn’t used crypto in the past year, the share who had ever owned or used it more than doubled, to 11% from 5%. Plans to buy are flat, too: 17% say they’re likely to own or use crypto in the future, compared with 16% last year.
Men were more than twice as likely as women to have used crypto in the past year, 18% to 8%, and adults under 60 were far more likely to have used it than older Americans. Curiosity remains the top reason people tried crypto, cited by 34% of those who have owned it, followed by long-term investment at 25%.
The survey polled 1,545 adults from Sept. 8 to 16 on Ipsos’ KnowledgePanel, the same probability-based panel the Federal Reserve uses for its annual survey of household finances. The margin of error is plus or minus 2.8 percentage points.
It also found deep unease with the traditional financial system. Only 19% of Americans say it’s secure, while 63% say it needs an upgrade to combat threats like cybercrime and AI. Six in 10 worry about data breaches at major financial institutions, and 54% doubt those institutions are ready to protect their personal information from AI-driven threats. Financial privacy matters to 74%.
That skepticism hasn’t translated into trust in crypto. Just 4% have high trust in crypto exchanges and 5% in decentralized platforms, compared with 42% for large national banks. Credit unions led at 48%, down 5 points from last year.
Security worries aren’t limited to banks. Crypto wallet maker Ledger said all confirmed cases in a suspected $87 million drain involved hardware wallets sold by a Southeast Asian reseller. Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake recently warned that advances in AI could break the cryptography securing Bitcoin and Ethereum sooner than expected.
The survey also points to a wide knowledge gap. Only 2% of Americans are very familiar with decentralized finance, or DeFi, shorthand for the group of crypto-native financial applications that allow users to buy, sell, or borrow digital assets without third-party intermediaries.
Just 6% could identify all four characteristics of crypto listed in the survey, while 35% weren’t sure how to describe it at all. Yet 40% say they’d be at least somewhat likely to try DeFi if it were available. Among them, more than 8 in 10 say they’d use it to save money, earn interest or send money to family and friends.
Interest in learning more is slipping, though. The share who want to learn about stablecoins fell to 7% from 11%, and about DeFi to 8% from 11%, even after the GENIUS Act set federal rules for stablecoins.

articles.title: OpenAI Plans to Buy Google's AI Chips as It Looks Beyond Nvidia: Report - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI plans to buy Google's TPU AI chips, The Information reported; neither company has confirmed, and price, volume and timing have not been disclosed.
- OpenAI reportedly began renting Google's TPUs in June 2025 and is now hiring an engineer to optimize its frontier models for them, while also preparing its own Broadcom-built chip, Jalapeño, for deployment by the end of 2026.
- Alphabet's CFO expects most revenue from its TPU system sales in 2027, and the company reports third-quarter earnings after the U.S. market closes Wednesday.
OpenAI plans to buy AI chips from Google, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke with The Information. The step would loosen its dependence on Nvidia, the company that supplies most of the hardware behind the AI boom.
Neither company has confirmed the plan, and the price, the number of chips, and the delivery dates have not been disclosed. OpenAI is one of Nvidia’s biggest customers.
The chips OpenAI is reportedly after are Google's tensor processing units, or TPUs, processors designed for one job: the math that AI models run on. Google revealed the chip in 2016, saying it had already run TPUs in its data centers for more than a year.
Reports in June 2025 said OpenAI had begun renting Google's TPUs, and the company described it as early testing with no plans to deploy them at scale. A purchase would mean owning the hardware instead of paying Google by the hour. Other details of the plan have not been made public.
A job listing from OpenAI in San Francisco asks for an engineer to lead the optimization of its frontier models on TPUs so the rumors have weight. The work involves compilers, the software that translates an AI model into instructions a specific chip can run, which is why switching chips is harder than swapping parts.
Richard Ho, who leads OpenAI's hardware program, spent nearly nine years at Google and was one of the leaders of its Cloud TPU project before joining OpenAI.
In September 2025, Nvidia signed a letter of intent to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI as it deployed at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems. A gigawatt is a billion watts, the unit data center builders now use to size their projects.
Two weeks later, AMD gave OpenAI the right to buy up to 160 million AMD shares, roughly 10% of the company. The right is tied to OpenAI deploying 6 gigawatts of AMD chips.
Nvidia ended up putting $30 billion into OpenAI's funding round, well below the $100 billion in the letter of intent. CEO Jensen Huang said in March that it might be the last such investment before OpenAI goes public.
In June, OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño, its first custom chip, built with Broadcom. It is designed for inference, the step where a trained model generates answers, with initial deployment planned for the end of 2026.
Google unveiled two eighth-generation TPUs in April: the 8t for training AI models and the 8i for inference (running them). Its performance figures are measured against Google's previous-generation chip, Ironwood, not against Nvidia's hardware.
Anthropic, OpenAI's main rival, signed an agreement with Google and Broadcom in April for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity that it expects to come online starting in 2027.
Alphabet began delivering TPU systems to customers' own data centers in the second quarter, according to its CFO. Google Cloud also began offering OpenAI's GPT-6 models to select customers in private preview last week.

articles.title: FEC Reports Filing System Down, Potentially Obscuring Crypto PAC Spending
articles.text:
Crypto PAC spending before midterms possibly obscured after reported FEC hack
The FEC reported an “electronic filing system outage” on Tuesday as groups are expected to ramp up spending before the US midterm elections.
The US Federal Election Commission (FEC) filing system is offline after reports of a hack, potentially obscuring expenditures by super political action committees (PACs) and other groups in the final days before the 2026 midterm elections.
As of Tuesday at 7:48 pm UTC, the FEC said it was continuing to experience an “electronic filing system outage,” but was working to resolve the issue. Campaign finance data by PACs and other entities were still available for the public to view, but the system outage suggested that last-minute spending could go unreported.
For example, with just six days until Election Day, FEC filings showed no expenditures from the cryptocurrency industry-aligned Super PACs Fairshake, Defend American Jobs, Protect Progress, Fellowship and Digital Freedom Fund since Sunday. Cointelegraph reached out to Fairshake for comment but did not receive an immediate response.
Super PACs are required to report certain spending to the FEC within 24 hours of the funds being used, provided the expenditures total $1,000 or more. Candidates for House and Senate seats, likewise, are expected to report contributions of $1,000 or more within 48 hours in the 20 days before an election.
Digital Freedom Fund, a PAC launched by Gemini co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, reported on Sunday that it had spent more than $572,000 on text messages to support various Republican Senate candidates, with the majority going to bolster Ken Paxton’s campaign in Texas. Protect Progress’ most recent expenditure before the FEC outage showed more than $50,000 for a direct mail campaign supporting Representative Aisha Wahab in California’s 14th district.
Related: CLARITY vote failure could stoke more crypto PAC spending in key races
The 2026 midterms could be consequential for many in the crypto industry who support digital asset laws passing in Congress and state-level legislation and policies. Lawmakers in Congress failed to advance a crypto market structure bill in September, leading to Fairshake and other industry advocates supporting the reelection of those who voted in favor of the legislation.
Reuters reported on Tuesday that the disruption was caused by the FEC website being targeted by a hacker or hackers, according to an email. An FEC spokesperson told Cointelegraph that its IT staff were ”actively working to restore service.”
History repeats itself in Ohio with crypto PAC spending on Senate candidates
In 2024, Fairshake spent about $41 million opposing Senator Sherrod Brown’s reelection bid against Republican Bernie Moreno. The Democratic lawmaker ended up losing his Senate seat, but announced that he would run against incumbent Jon Husted in 2026, leading to another election with money from the crypto industry flowing into attack ads.
Before the FEC outage, Fairshake reported spending $56 million on media to oppose Brown and support Husted, while the Digital Freedom Fund disclosed more than $7 million in expenditures for the same race. The crypto PACs are just some of the groups interested in influencing Ohio voters in the 2026 midterms, with reports of tens of millions of dollars being spent from Democratic- and Republican-aligned organizations.

articles.title: Fed Stands Pat, Bitcoin Holds Steady—But a December Rate Hike Is in Play - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The Fed held its target range at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike.
- The statement now calls economic activity "strong," up from "solid" in September, and says more information will determine the policy stance.
- Bitcoin edged up about 0.2% to roughly $80,950 after the announcement, and the Fed's next meeting, Dec. 8-9, comes with new economic projections.
The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with two officials dissenting in favor of another quarter-point hike. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted against the decision, according to the Fed’s statement.
Bitcoin barely moved, edging up about 0.2% to roughly $80,950 in the minutes after the 2 p.m. ET announcement. CME FedWatch, a tool that converts bets on interest rate futures into probabilities, had put the odds of no change at around 90% before the decision.
The decision reaches well beyond Wall Street, because the federal funds rate, which is what banks charge each other for overnight loans, sets the baseline for what consumers pay on credit cards and car loans. The Fed raised that rate in September, its first hike since 2023, in a unanimous 12-0 vote.
“Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace,” the Fed said in its statement, a step up from the solid pace it cited in September. “Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little,” it added.
On inflation, the Fed said it remains elevated and that “the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s 2 percent goal."
Hammack also dissented in July, when the committee held rates in a 9-3 vote with Neel Kashkari and Lorie Logan joining her in favoring a hike. Kashkari and Logan sided with the majority this time, so the number of dissents fell to two from three.
Oil remains a major driver of inflation because the U.S.-Iran war has squeezed global supply, and U.S. crude settled at $99.90 a barrel on Tuesday. Pricier crude lifts gasoline and shipping costs, which eventually show up on grocery shelves, and consumer prices rose 3.7% in the 12 months through September, with gasoline alone jumping 9.1% in the month, the Labor Department reported.
Higher inflation makes investors demand more interest for lending to the government, which lifts Treasury yields, the interest rate on U.S. government debt. The 10-year yield, the benchmark that mortgage rates follow, closed Tuesday at 4.99% after peaking at 5.31% on Oct. 5, so a nearly risk-free return is available without owning anything volatile.
Bitcoin pays no yield, so when Treasuries pay more, money tends to drift out of riskier assets such as crypto and stocks. The price briefly poked above $81,600 earlier Wednesday before slipping back, below a resistance zone between $81,000 and $82,500 that has capped several rally attempts this year.
Leverage, meaning borrowed money used to make bigger bets, tends to exaggerate those moves around Fed events. When prices swing against a trader, the exchange automatically closes the position, a liquidation that adds to the selling pressure. After Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech in August, about $481 million in crypto positions were liquidated within 24 hours.
Traders had put the odds of another quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting above 70% before the decision. Minutes from September’s meeting show most officials judged another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end.
The October jobs report arrives Nov. 6, October inflation data follows on Nov. 10, and the Fed meets again Dec. 8-9, when it will also publish new economic projections. Fed Chairman Warsh will hold a press conference at 2:30 p.m. to elaborate on the Fed's decision.

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Gains Reverse Into FOMC Meeting as US Stocks Track Sideways
articles.text:
Bitcoin price bounce rejected at 50-day trend line ahead of FOMC, earnings
Bitcoin failed to move past its 50-day simple moving average as market participants awaited the outcome of the FOMC meeting and key tech earnings.
Bitcoin (BTC) gave back early gains around Wednesday’s Wall Street open as markets prepared for the US Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision.
Key points:
- Bitcoin fell around 0.3% on Wednesday after upside volatility failed to sustain past $81,687.
- US stock markets tracked sideways into the run-up to the Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) interest-rate decision and press conference after South Korea’s KOSPI gained 6.6%.
- BTC/USD stalled below its 50-day simple moving average at $81,831, which acted as local resistance.
US stocks tread water as focus turns to Fed chair Warsh
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD failing to break beyond $81,700, instead reversing to as low as $80,297 on Bitstamp. At the time of writing, the pair was down 0.3% on the day.
US stocks opened flat ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting statement and press conference from Fed chair Kevin Warsh. Markets overwhelmingly expected officials to hold rates in their current 3.75-4% range, with the focus instead on Warsh’s language and comments on the economy.

Fed target-rate probabilities (screenshot). Source: CME Group

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index did not follow South Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index higher after the KOSPI closed up 6.6%, its best daily gain since July.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

“Even after a nearly 10% two-day bounce, the index is still 34% below its June 22 record of 9,115. On Monday it closed 40% below that peak,” he noted of the index.
BTC price gains capped by 50-day moving average
After BTC price upside momentum faded, the 50-day simple moving average (SMA) at $81,831 functioned as resistance on low time frames.

“A 4H close below $80,565 reduces the probability of retesting resistance at the 50-Day SMA,” Alan commented.
BTC/USD four-hour chart with 50-day SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

articles.title: AI Can Quietly Influence Experts’ Decisions, Anthropic Study Finds - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Anthropic’s Alignment team found that 50 professional analysts matched their AI agent’s secretly assigned, coin-flip-chosen preference on 86% of four analytical decisions, against 50% expected by chance.
- In a post-task survey of 48 analysts, 77% repeated the agent’s arguments, sometimes word for word, while only 15% credited the agent, and none suspected its preferences had been manipulated.
- Anthropic cautions that the lean was deliberately amplified and tested on one task, field, and model, and suggests agents that argue the best case for each option or ask the expert’s view first.
Professional analysts adopted their AI agent’s hidden, randomly assigned opinion on 86% of key judgment calls, against about 50% expected by chance, according to an experiment published Tuesday by Anthropic’s Alignment team. Only 15% credited the agent afterward, and none suspected its preferences had been planted.
AI agents—programs that carry out tasks on their own—are being handed expert work on what the study calls the usual assumption: that experts still make the decisions that matter. Anthropic launched 10 agent templates for financial firms and insurers in May, saying users have the final word.
That arrangement, called “human in the loop,” assumes the person who signs off on an AI’s work is the one making the important calls. Anthropic tested it on 50 analysts experienced in causal inference, meaning working out from data whether one thing causes another.
Each analyst used Claude Code, Anthropic’s coding agent, to advise a fictional farming cooperative on expanding an advisory program. Unknown to them, a coin flip set which option each agent favored, hidden in a system prompt, the instructions that shape how an AI behaves.
“Across the four analytical choices, analysts went with their agent’s lean 86% of the time. If the agent’s input made no difference, we’d expect about 50%,” Anthropic said. Those who had already chosen before the agent weighed in abandoned it 60% of the time when the agent disagreed, against 6% when it agreed, though that rests on only 38 cases.
Asked to explain their choices, 77% repeated the agent’s argument in at least one answer, sometimes word for word. Only 15% credited the agent, and 52% called the final recommendation more their own than the agent’s.
“For individual experts, this could mean losing agency over their own work, a form of what researchers call disempowerment,” Anthropic said. This phenomenon basically means the human voluntarily loses control over their own decisions. “The work still goes out under the expert’s name,” the authors wrote, “but the decisions that most depend on their judgment are in reality settled by the agent’s prior beliefs.”
In April 2025, OpenAI rolled back an update to ChatGPT that it called overly flattering or agreeable. The agents here were told never to mislead, yet they rarely argued for the alternative.
“With only one side argued well,” the authors wrote, “the analysts could adopt the agent’s assumptions without working out their own.” Error checks struggle to catch this because judgment calls have no single correct answer, so the work looks sound whichever option is picked.
Anthropic says this is no argument for using AI less, since analysts with the agent finished faster and made far fewer serious errors, though the no-agent group was small and less experienced. It suggests agents that argue the best case for each option or ask the expert first, though that could overwhelm users.
The researchers deliberately strengthened the agents’ preferences and tested one task, field, and model, so real-world effects may be smaller. Measuring it outside the lab is the hard part: the team could detect deference only because it randomized each agent’s lean, which the authors say is rarely possible in real work.

articles.title: Phantom Adds Bitcoin and Sports Event Trading via Kalshi
articles.text:
Phantom launches Kalshi-powered prediction markets for US users
The crypto wallet’s new integration offers CFTC-regulated event contracts through Kalshi, as prediction markets face growing legal challenges in the US.
Crypto wallet provider Phantom has launched prediction markets for eligible US users through an integration with Kalshi, allowing them to trade on crypto prices, sports and other real-world events directly within its app.
According to Wednesday’s announcement, the integration offers CFTC-regulated event contracts, including short-term Bitcoin price markets that settle every 15 minutes. Trades can be funded through Phantom Cash balances, denominated in the CASH stablecoin.
Kalshi handles customer verification, account management and trade execution, while Phantom provides access through its app. The launch follows no-action relief granted by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in March, allowing Phantom to connect users to regulated markets without registering as an introducing broker, subject to certain conditions.
The service is rolling out through a new Predict tab in Phantom, with availability varying by state and market category. Eligible US users can view live market data, sports scores and market discussions before placing trades through an interface similar to a cryptocurrency token swap.
Related: Pentagon bans US forces from using military info to bet in prediction markets
Kalshi’s legal battles continue as trading volumes rise
Phantom’s entry into prediction markets comes amid a widening legal dispute over the industry in the US. On Monday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Utah after the state challenged Kalshi’s event contracts under its gambling laws, adding to a series of cases over whether federal derivatives regulation supersedes state gambling laws.
Despite the legal uncertainty, trading activity continues to grow. Kalshi recorded $10.8 billion in crypto contract volume over the 30 days ending Oct. 27, up 19.6% from the previous period, according to data compiled by DeFi Rate.
Kalshi trading volume and market share from Sept. 28 to Oct. 27, 2026. Source: DeFi Rate

articles.title: Strategy Shareholders Approve Daily Dividends on Preferred Stock, With 99.3% in Favor - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Strategy shareholders approved an amendment letting its four preferred stocks accrue dividends every calendar day, with 99.3% of votes cast in favor, according to preliminary results.
- STRC's first daily record date will be November 1, with payment on November 2, while STRF, STRK and STRD will switch over on January 1.
- Dividends with record dates that fall on weekends or holidays will be bundled together and paid on the next business day, according to an SEC filing.
Strategy shareholders have approved a plan to let the company's four preferred stocks accrue dividends every calendar day, including weekends and holidays, the Bitcoin treasury company's chairman Michael Saylor said on Wednesday.
Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor of the amendment, which covers Strategy's STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD preferred stocks, according to Saylor. The vote took place at a special meeting of stockholders on Wednesday, the company said.
$MSTR shareholders have approved the Daily Dividends amendment. Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor. The amendment enables $STRF, $STRC, $STRK and $STRD to accrue dividends every calendar day. Thank you to all who voted. https://t.co/w1Cp4GKUy5
— Michael Saylor (@saylor) October 28, 2026
Under the new schedule, every calendar day will be a record date, with payment on the next business day. STRC will move first, with its first daily record date on November 1 and payment on November 2, Saylor added. STRF, STRK and STRD will follow, with their first record date on January 1 and payment on January 4.
The change still depends on Strategy filing amended terms for each stock, according to the filing.
Because U.S. markets are closed at weekends, dividends with record dates on non-trading days will in practice be grouped together. The Depository Trust Company will treat a weekend or holiday record date as falling on the previous business day, which Nasdaq will also treat as the ex-dividend date.
For example, dividends with record dates of Friday, November 6, Saturday, November 7 and Sunday, November 8 would all be treated as having a Friday record date and paid together on Monday, November 9, Strategy said. Because trades settle the next business day, an investor who buys STRC on that Friday would not receive any of the three dividends, while one who sells that day would still receive all three. Treatment could differ for shares traded outside Nasdaq or held through some brokers, the company said.
STRC under pressure
Strategy proposed the change last month, saying it would help dampen volatility in its preferred shares. For STRC, it means moving from 24 record dates a year to 365.
The company has been working to support STRC, which traded at $99.86 on Wednesday, just below its $100 par value, according to Yahoo Finance. Last week, Strategy paused its Bitcoin buying for the first time since mid-September and spent $204.9 million buying back STRC instead.
Strategy also faces possible removal from MSCI's widely tracked equity indexes. The index provider finalized a rule this month that treats companies whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset as ineligible, and will publish the list of affected companies on November 11.

articles.title: Google Cloud Details MPC Service for Bitcoin Custody
articles.text:
Google Cloud outlines MPC service for institutional Bitcoin custody
Google Cloud has detailed its preview MPC service for institutional Bitcoin custody as it holds a New York symposium focused on digital asset security.
Google’s cloud computing division is progressing with a service that lets financial institutions jointly authorize and sign cryptocurrency transactions without giving any single party control over the full private key.
Google Cloud detailed its Multi-party Compute (MPC) service in documentation updated Monday, positioning the preview product for institutional Bitcoin custody. The service remains in preview, meaning Google provides it as is, with potentially limited support.
The documentation update preceded Google Cloud’s MPC Symposium, taking place Wednesday in New York. The event promises an “exclusive revealing of Google’s frontier MPC product and research projects,” according to its description, and features speakers from financial institutions including Morgan Stanley, OKX, Citi and Wells Fargo.
Google Cloud’s release notes for the service date back to August 2026. On Oct. 1, Google expanded its Bitcoin security rules to evaluate transaction amounts, identify destination address types and detect change outputs.
The Alphabet subsidiary has previously explored related technology through Confidential Space, a cloud environment designed to support secure multi-party computation and data sharing, as described in a June blog post.
Cointelegraph contacted Google Cloud and Rich Widmann, Google’s director of digital assets strategy, for clarification on the service’s availability and launch timeline.

articles.title: Aptos Advisor Leaves Post, Moves Meme-Fueled Campaign to Meta Stock - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Former Aptos advisor Buzz has left the crypto project after his one-year contract ended, calling the split “mutual,” and says he’s sold his APT tokens.
- The memer is now pointing his guerrilla marketing campaign at Facebook's parent company Meta, arguing retail investors have been forgotten and that the company has strong fundamentals.
- Buzz previously helped pump APT's token value with his memes, but Meta is roughly 2,619 times bigger than Aptos—so he's set himself a real challenge.
Pseudonymous social media memer turned crypto advisor BuzzlamicJihad has left his position at Aptos, claiming the partnership had run its course. The former Aptos advisor has turned his attention to the META stock as he ramps up his trademark meme campaign for the company.
BuzzlamicJihad, who is called Buzz by his friends and family, rose to prominence in early 2025, when his unofficial "community takeover” of crypto project Aptos helped pump the token's value. It was the result of months of fostering a community of die-hard investors and posting memes, popularizing the terms "Aptos lookin’ good here," and "sidelined?"
$META looking good here
— 🐝 (🌐/acc) (@BuzzlamicJihad) October 27, 2026
In October 2025, Buzz officially joined Aptos as an advisor, as the memer told Decrypt that he wanted to fix the project's image problem and position it as a premium stablecoin network. A year later, that contract came to an end and Buzz did not opt to extend.
"I didn’t see it going anywhere else, and some of the plans I had didn’t work out as intended," Buzz told Decrypt. "So, I didn’t bother extending it and they didn’t seem willing to either anyways, so it’s mutual."
Aptos did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment.
Since the start of the month, APT has dropped 10.7% to a $607 million market capitalization, per Decrypt data. Buzz told Decrypt he has sold his APT.
The memer is now turning his attention to Facebook's parent company, Meta. This is because his entire thesis around Aptos was based on its ties to Facebook. Buzz told Decrypt last year that he made his money via Facebook advertising and strongly believed in the team behind the social media app. That's why he cared so much about Aptos, a crypto project that was formed by developers from Libra—a now-defunct stablecoin project led by Facebook.
In 2024, Buzz started posting on social media about Aptos making huge statements about Aptos' potential, such as predicting it'll flip XRP in market cap.
When Aptos Labs founder Mo Shaikh stepped down in December 2024, Buzz bought more and started to claim he was starting a "community takeover" and that it hadn't been "priced in"—a phrase he repeated at least seven times through January. All while he spammed “Aptos lookin’ good here,” “sidelined?” and “motion not priced in yet" across everyone's timelines.
In February 2025, the shitposting paid off as notable influencers got behind him, drawing eyes to Aptos, and the APT token boosted 17% in 24 hours.
However, his approach this time is different, he says.
"I don’t think META is failing obviously and needs a hostile takeover, but retail is kind of forgotten, especially with the recent Class C share creation with no voting ability," Buzz told Decrypt. "It's also not entirely dependent on memetics here; I actually think they have strong fundamentals too."
Buzz's social media campaign has begun as he tests the waters for what works. Already, he's thrown out a "META looking good here," and claims to have moved all communications off of Telegram and onto the Meta-owned WhatsApp (though Decrypt spoke to Buzz via Telegram during the creation of this article).
Meta is down 1.2% on the day Buzz's campaign has begun, per Yahoo! Finance data, sitting at a sizable $1.59 trillion market cap. Meta is 2,619 times bigger than Aptos, when comparing market capitalizations, so making its price budge would be a real challenge.
A somewhat comparable success story is that of Roaring Kitty, a meme stock influencer who led the charge for those investing in GameStop's GME stock. Through a stream of posts on the subreddit r/WallStreetBets and livestreams, he gathered an army of die-hard investors to rally behind GameStop as major hedge funds looked to short the stock. The phenomenon resulted in GME hitting an all-time high, substantial losses for hedge funds, and a 2023 feature film, "Dumb Money," based on the influencer's antics.
Roaring Kitty did it for a stock that currently sits at a market cap of $11.85 billion. That makes Buzz's challenge 134 times larger.
The GameStop influencer momentarily returned to social media in 2024 after more than two years of inactivity. But since then, Roaring Kitty has faded into obscurity, despite unsubstantiated rumors that he would join the GameStop board.
Buzz, however, wants to help lead Meta into a new era.
"I do think [Meta's AI agent] Muse could also benefit hugely from stablecoin float economics from the original vision of GlobalCoin (later becoming Libra/Diem), so it’s not out of the question that they go back into crypto in a huge way," Buzz told Decrypt. "And if they chose me to lead this in some capacity, I would be honored to do so."

articles.title: Cybersecurity ‘Armageddon’: How to Stay Safe Online
articles.text:
Cybersecurity’s Black October: How to protect yourself
Each day brings news of another AI-powered attack, or a newly discovered vulnerability. Here’s what’s happening and how ordinary people can protect themselves online.
Cybersecurity professionals are having a brutal month.
What’s being dubbed Black October isn’t even over, and it’s already brought about several dozen major cyberattacks and AI-identified vulnerabilities across the internet.
When critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language used by around 70% of websites, were uncovered with the help of AI tools and disclosed by the PHP Foundation on Oct. 21, the race to patch servers around the world began.
Cloud services provider Cloudflare reported millions of attempts to exploit the vulnerability after its disclosure, following thousands of attempts in the preceding hours.
Some countries, including France and Finland, temporarily pulled access to certain websites while the US National Security Agency (NSA) warned organizations to patch the flaws immediately or take affected systems offline.
“We are at Security Armageddon now,” said NEAR founder Illia Polosukhin. Anthropic’s chief security adviser Jason Clinton warned that, “as bad as things have gotten in the past 4 days, they are going to get a lot worse before they get better.”
Citizens of the United Kingdom are even being urged to “be ready” for an emergency, such as severe weather or cyberattacks, that could cut off access to critical infrastructure such as water, electricity or the internet. US military installation have been told to prep for 90 days of independent operation under the FORTRESS initiative.
Houston, do we have a problem?
Beyond rushing out to stockpile canned food and walkie-talkies, is there anything else ordinary people can do to mitigate their exposure?
So how bad is Black October, really?
“It’s really bad. It looks like the rest of the internet is waking up to the reality we had three months ago,” Rob Hamilton, a Bitcoin security researcher involved in the Bitcoin Red Team, tells Magazine.
UK government is urging citizens to be ready for an emergency. Source: gov.uk
In the past week or so, cloud platform Railway disclosed that an attacker has accessed and decrypted customer credentials and API keys, apparently targeting AI providers.
Related: France is world’s most dangerous place for Bitcoiners: 90 attacks in 7 months
Medical testing giant Quest Diagnostics confirmed a breach of private patient health data, while Indian security firm eMudhra was found to have eight digital certificate authorities with weak keys that could potentially have let attackers impersonate trusted websites. And code hosting platform GitHub experienced a major service disruption that highlighted how heavily the software world relies on shared infrastructure.
GitHub’s senior director of security, Austin Devers, says incidents like this are a “clear reminder that reliability requires constant work,” because modern development is “so connected.”
Railway security incident. Source: Railway
Jonathan Riss, an OSINT and blockchain intelligence analyst at blockchain security firm CertiK, tells Magazine:
“What concerns us most is how a single weakness in shared infrastructure can expose many organizations simultaneously.” 
Unfortunately, he adds that AI’s ability to find vulnerabilities is not matched by its ability to fix them:
“Finding vulnerabilities faster does not automatically give us the capacity to resolve them faster.” 
Why things are likely to get worse
One reason the problem is getting worse is because AI has changed the economics of cybersecurity.
What once required nation-state resources and sophisticated hackers to pull off can now be achieved by a teenager in a basement somewhere.
AI entrepreneur and investor Matt Shumer said that AI enables non technical users to find weak spots and exploit them, leaving defenders are “racing to keep up.”
“Every weak spot still has to be fixed, tested and installed on millions of systems run by people who are already stretched thin.”
Devers says AI-assisted security tools are “dramatically” lowering the barrier to “uncovering complex, deep-seated flaws in widely used codebases.”
Related: Keystone says website breach exposed hardware wallet buyers’ addresses
What can ordinary people actually do?
There are some practical steps ordinary folk can use to stay safer online during this volatile period.
The internet is under attack. Source: Matt Shumer
Shumer recommends staying off sites you don’t know, and definitely don’t enter passwords or card numbers into unfamiliar sites “until this blows over” since smaller sites are the “least likely to have patched.”
Delete any apps you don’t use and unplug smart gadgets you don’t need. Keep some cash at home and enough groceries for a few days, “if you want to be extra careful.”
Devers says the best defense is “locking down personal access points and keeping overall footprints small.” Turn on Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all accounts, ideally using an authenticator app or hardware security key rather than text messages.
“This acts as a circuit breaker and stops hackers from logging into your account even if the underlying software is compromised.” 
Never reuse passwords either, he says. “Create strong, unique passwords for every site, and periodically disconnect old app permissions or third-party connections you no longer use.” Keep your devices and web browsers updated automatically:
“While platform teams work to fix cloud-level security issues on the backend, keeping your devices secure ensures hackers can’t use your personal hardware as a back door into your accounts.”  
To self-custody or not self-custody, that is the question
While the alarming rise in security incidents has caused some crypto holders to consider alternatives and some experts to advise against self-custody, others, such as Bitcoin advocate and Casa chief security officer Jameson Lopp, remind users that defeats the whole purpose.
“You can only benefit from Bitcoin’s unique properties when you hold your own keys. [...] Giving up your keys doesn’t make the risk go away, he says. It moves the risk somewhere you can’t see or control.”
Riss recommends separating small amounts you intend to use into a hot wallet, from longer-term holdings in a hardware wallet, and to “actually read what you’re signing rather than approving blind.”
While these precautions can reduce your vulnerability to attack, everyday users can only lock down local issues, and have little ability to affect wider problems.
You can “reduce blast radius,” he says, “not prevent infrastructure compromise.”
So while users can improve their cyber hygiene, ultimately, “the structural burden sits with platforms and providers.”

articles.title: Wall Street’s Fast Money Fled Bitcoin ETFs, Sovereign Funds Stepped In - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Millennium, Goldman Sachs, Tudor and six other firms cut 68,000 BTC worth of spot Bitcoin ETF holdings, more than the 48,000 BTC decline across all 13F filers.
- Morgan Stanley’s wealth arm, Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council were among the buyers.
- Galaxy says sellers left because the futures basis shrank to just 0.6 points over Treasury bills, not because they soured on Bitcoin.
The investors who sold Bitcoin through its 2026 slump weren’t the crowd you might expect.
A Galaxy Research report published Monday found that a handful of hedge funds and banks drove almost all of the institutional selling in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, while wealth platforms and sovereign funds stepped in to buy.
Institutions that file quarterly 13F reports with the SEC held 355,000 BTC worth of spot ETF shares at the end of September 2025, just before Bitcoin’s all-time high. By June 2026, that had fallen to 307,000 BTC, a 14% drop, the report found.
Nine firms account for more than all of that decline: Millennium Management, Brevan Howard, Goldman Sachs, Capula Management, Farallon Capital, D.E. Shaw, Schonfeld Strategic Advisors, Symmetry Investments and Tudor Investment.
Together they cut 68,000 BTC worth of exposure, roughly $5.4 billion at today’s prices, trimming their positions by between 29% and 100%. That means the other roughly 2,200 filers added about 20,000 BTC in aggregate, worth roughly $1.6 billion.
Morgan Stanley’s wealth management arm, Abu Dhabi’s Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council were among the buyers. Advisers, family offices, and individuals who don’t file 13Fs cut their holdings by just 6.6% while the price fell 49%.
Galaxy head of firmwide research Alex Thorn says the sellers were largely running a trade, not making a bet on Bitcoin. Many used the cash-and-carry strategy: buying spot ETF shares while shorting CME Bitcoin futures to pocket the gap between the two, known as the basis.
That gap has nearly vanished. The front-month basis averaged 7.9% annualized in the 30 days before Bitcoin’s high, 3.9 percentage points above three-month Treasury bills. In the 30 days to Oct. 21, it averaged 4.8%, just 0.6 points above bills. After fees, rolling costs and margin, the trade now earns about 1.5 points over cash, the report estimates.
“That arithmetic, not the price, is why the multi-strategy desks left,” Thorn wrote.
CFTC data on CME Bitcoin futures tells a similar story. Asset managers’ net long position fell from 43,300 BTC in the week of Bitcoin’s all-time high to 18,400 BTC, a 57% drop. Leveraged funds’ net short, the futures side of the carry trade, shrank by the same proportion, from 71,400 BTC to 30,600 BTC. Open interest is down 28% in Bitcoin terms and 51% in dollar terms.
Contracts further out still offer something. November and December futures priced in 6.3% to 6.5% at the Oct. 21 close, about 2 points over bills before costs. But Thorn argued that the slim edge doesn’t pay for the trade’s tail risk: in December 2022, the basis inverted to negative 31% annualized.
Overall, spot ETF holdings fell just 11% from their October 2025 peak to their July trough while Bitcoin fell 53%. Since the June low, the funds have added 87,000 BTC, which Galaxy calls directional buying rather than carry.
Recent flows have been choppy. Decrypt reported that the ETFs shed nearly $1 billion over two weeks earlier this month before notching their best day in nearly a month on Oct. 19, when BlackRock’s IBIT did all the buying. Since then, a three-day, $1 billion inflow run has been followed by heavy outflows. BTF ETF flows once again turned green this week, but in smaller numbers: roughly $286 million in inflows so far.
The 13F data runs through June, so it doesn’t capture more recent shifts. Galaxy discloses that it holds Bitcoin.

articles.title: DTCC Subsidiary Launches Tokenization Services

DTCC unit launches tokenization services
The post-trade market infrastructure provider said the tokenization services will create a “practical path” for tokenized securities adoption.
The Depository Trust Company (DTC), a subsidiary of The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), has launched tokenization services enabling eligible users to mint tokenized representations of securities held at DTC.
DTCC clients are eligible to use the DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS). DTS will convert between traditional and tokenized forms of securities that are transferable to digital wallets and retain the same ownership rights and investor protections as their traditional counterparts, the company announced on Wednesday.
The post-trade market infrastructure provider said that 20 of its clients have signed agreements to access the services, including Alpaca, Citadel Securities, Citi, Clear Street, DriveWealth, Fidelity Investments, Interchange Clearing and JPMorgan.
DTC has more than $114 trillion in assets under custody, including stocks and exchange-traded funds. The company said its service will create a “practical path” for tokenized securities adoption.
In December 2025, the US Securities and Exchange Commission issued a “no action” letter stating that it would not recommend enforcement action against DTCC’s subsidiary in relation to its proposed tokenization program.
In May, DTCC said it planned a full service launch of trading of tokenized securities in October 2026, following a July 2026 pilot.
The tokenization service is currently integrated with Canton Network and DTCC’s Besu private network, with plans to add additional blockchain networks in 2027.

articles.title: Fed Rate Decision: What Markets and Bitcoin Traders Can Expect - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The Fed announces its decision at 2 p.m. ET with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference to follow, and futures and prediction markets put the odds of a hold above 90%.
- The target range sits at 3.75%-4.00% after September's 12-0 hike, with September inflation at 3.7% and oil near $100 a barrel.
- Markets give 75% to 80% odds to another quarter-point hike on Dec. 8-9, while bitcoin trades around $80,700.
The Federal Reserve announces its interest rate decision at 2 p.m. ET today, and traders are almost certain it will change nothing.
CME FedWatch, a tool that converts bets on interest rate futures into probabilities, puts the odds of a hold above 90%, while prediction markets price it a few points higher.
The decision reaches well beyond Wall Street, because the federal funds rate, which is what banks charge each other for overnight loans, sets the baseline for what consumers pay on credit cards and loans. That rate sits at 3.75% to 4.00% after the Fed raised it in September, its first hike since 2023, in a unanimous 12-0 vote.
Consumer prices rose 3.7% in the 12 months through September, the Labor Department reported, and gasoline alone jumped 9.1% in the month. Hiring is slowing, though: employers added just 29,000 jobs in September against forecasts of about 90,000, and the unemployment rate stood at 4.2%.
Oil is a major driver of that inflation, trading near $100 a barrel because the U.S.-Iran war has squeezed global supply. Pricier crude lifts gasoline and shipping costs, which eventually show up on grocery shelves and push inflation higher.
Higher inflation makes investors demand more interest for lending to the government, which lifts Treasury yields, the interest rate on U.S. government debt. The 10-year yield, the benchmark that mortgage rates follow, is hovering around 5% after peaking at 5.31% on Oct. 5, so a nearly risk-free return is available without owning anything volatile.
Bitcoin pays no yield and is also very volatile for traditional investors, so when Treasuries pay more, money tends to drift out of riskier assets such as crypto and stocks. The price of Bitcoin sits around $80,700, just below a support-now-resistance zone where sellers have repeatedly stopped rallies this year.
Leverage, meaning borrowed money used to make bigger bets, tends to exaggerate the moves around Fed events. When prices swing against a trader, the exchange automatically closes the position, a liquidation that adds to the selling pressure. After Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech in August, about $481 million in crypto positions were liquidated within 24 hours, more than $360 million of them bets on higher prices.
Traders now appear focused on December, where futures and prediction markets give 75% to 80% odds on another quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting. Minutes from September’s meeting show most officials judged another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end, and several said the current rate was “not restrictive or only mildly restrictive.”
Analysts are calling the likely outcome a “hawkish hold,” meaning rates stay put while the tone leaves more hikes on the table. Asked in September whether more hikes would follow, Warsh said, “I’m not going to prejudge any future decisions we make.” He also told reporters, “This won’t surprise you: I’m not in the forward guidance business,” which is Fed-speak for declining to signal future moves.
Dissents, meaning votes against the majority, are the clearest tell in the statement. The Fed’s July vote was 9-3, with three members favoring a hike, so a dissent for tightening today would suggest December is close to locked in.
The Fed publishes no new economic projections at this meeting. Those will arrive in December.

A Euronext spokesperson told Cointelegraph the suspension was due to “operational settlement requirements” and remains in effect until settlement operations are supported by the CSD.
Stock exchange operator Euronext suspended CoinShares’ Zcash exchange-traded product (ETP) on Wednesday, when it was scheduled to debut for trading on Euronext Paris.
In a Wednesday notice, the exchange operator said the CoinShares Zcash ETP (ZCSH) was suspended from trading on Euronext Paris until further notice. The notice did not provide a reason for the decision.
CoinShares’ Zcash ETP will remain suspended until “standard settlement operations can be fully supported by the Central Securities Depository (CSD),” Euronext’s press and communications manager, Flavio Bornancin-Tomasella, told Cointelegraph, adding that the measure was strictly limited to “operational settlement requirements.”
The suspension notice delays what would have been the fourth Zcash-based ETP listed in Europe. Other companies that launched Zcash ETPs earlier this year include 21Shares, Virtune and Valor.
CoinShares announced the planned launch of its ZCASH ETP on Euronext Paris earlier on Wednesday. Cointelegraph contacted CoinShares for comment on the matter but did not receive a response by publication.

articles.title: JPMorgan, Coca-Cola Among 7 More Companies Objecting to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- JPMorgan Chase, Coca-Cola, Dell, AMD, Adobe, Applied Materials, and Sandisk objected to trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, according to its Oct. 27 notice.
- That brings the total to 33 objecting issuers, up from nine on Oct. 15.
- Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, a timely objection bars the venue from listing a third-party tokenized version of a company’s stock, though other venues aren’t affected.
The pushback against OKX and ICE’s tokenized stock venue now includes the biggest bank in the U.S.
JPMorgan Chase, Coca-Cola, and Dell Technologies are among seven companies added to OKXICE TSV’s list of objecting issuers in a notice dated Tuesday. Advanced Micro Devices, Adobe, Applied Materials, and Sandisk round out the group. The additions bring the total to 33, up from 26 a day earlier.
The list has grown quickly. It stood at nine on Oct. 15, 16 on Oct. 19, and 22 on Oct. 23. Earlier objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Intel, and Oracle. JPMorgan is the third major bank to object, after Goldman and Wells Fargo.
Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can’t make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC’s order. The objection applies only to that venue. The notices haven’t disclosed the companies’ reasons.
OKXICE’s original Oct. 4 notice proposed 63 tokenized stocks from 62 companies, and several objectors, including Wells Fargo and Arm, weren’t on that initial roster. Some of the biggest names, including Nvidia, Tesla, Apple, and Amazon, haven’t objected so far.
OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7. Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC. Earlier notices warned that it’s uncertain whether tokenized shares in self-custodied wallets would be covered by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation if the tokenizer’s broker-dealer failed.
OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before announcing the 24/7 venue this month. Nasdaq, which won SEC approval for its own tokenized securities pilot, has said it will opt its shares out of the exemption.
