articles.title: Amazon's new Echo Dot now works as an eero Wi-Fi extender and smart home hub - Engadget
articles.text:
Amazon's new Echo Dot now works as an eero Wi-Fi extender and smart home hub
It has a new onboard AI processor that allows for more natural Alexa+ conversations.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
As part of its big Echo refresh, Amazon just unveiled a new Echo Dot with some useful updates. The tiny globular speaker can now serve as a smart home hub with support for multiple protocols and thousands of devices, for one. And the new Dot now works as an eero Wi-Fi extender to stretch your in-home wireless internet range.
The new Echo Dot is the first to be equipped with Amazon's custom-designed AZ3 chip for on-device AI voice processing. That, the company says, will allow for more natural conversations with Alexa+ since your voice commands won't need to make a round-trip to a data center. Amazon also added a fourth microphone so the Dot can hear you better as you move around a room. The extra mic will also help Amazon's Voice ID identify who's speaking, so it can pull up your playlists instead of your partner's.
The Dot's new built-in smart home hub will give users a relatively inexpensive way to connect smart home devices. It works with the Zigbee, Matter and Thread protocols, giving you control of "thousands" of compatible devices right out of the box, according to Amazon.
The other primary new feature makes a lot of sense. The new Echo Dot speakers will work as eero Wi-Fi extenders, adding up to 1,000 feet of coverage to an existing eero network to eliminate dead zones and improve internet connectivity. Judging by Amazon's "existing" wording, though, this may only work if you already have an eero router.
Amazon also improved the Echo Dot's audio quality by adding a full-range driver into the housing to create "more back volume for crisp vocals and 50 percent more bass than the last generation," the company said. It also offers features from previous models like Omnisense that can detect things like room temperature and human presence, allowing it to automatically turn up the thermostat or turn on the lights when you walk in.
Amazon also introduced an Amazon Kids Echo Dot model that offers the same features as the regular Echo Dot, but includes a year of the company's Kids+ subscription. That offers access to age-appropriate Audible audiobooks, ad-free music and kid-friendly podcasts, along with Stories from Alexa and the curated wind-down app, Sleep Studio. Amazon's Echo Dot is now available in four colors (Graphite, Glacier White, Agave Green, and Coral Pink) for $100. The Amazon Kids Echo Dot comes in Penguin and Octopus designs starting at $110.

articles.title: Xreal Aura is a new wired headset powered by Android XR | TechCrunch
articles.text:
At the Android Dev Summit on Wednesday, Google’s smart glasses partner Xreal launched its new Xreal Aura wired smart glasses, powered by the Android XR and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite platforms. The companies had teased the glasses earlier in the year at Google’s I/O developer conference.
As Meta expands its push into smart glasses, competitors like Apple and Google are keen to release their own devices. Much like it did with Android smartphones, Google is relying on an assortment of partners, including Samsung and Xreal, to bring devices powered by its Android XR platform to consumers.
The new Xreal Aura smart glasses are tethered to a smartphone-like device for processing power, rather than handling all the computing themselves. The glasses then display the content in the wearer’s field of view.
The device’s design, meanwhile, is closer to Meta’s smart glasses than Apple’s Vision Pro, which is a larger headset.
Xreal Aura uses Sony’s Micro-OLED display with 1200p resolution at 120 Hz and a 95-degree field of view — screen specs that put the glasses above the Ray-Ban Meta Display on paper. However, Xreal’s smart glasses are heavier at 95 grams compared to Meta’s 69 grams, and you have to carry the puck.
At launch, the Aura supports many popular Google Play apps and games along with specific XR experiences, including the NBA App for Android XR; Nevatars; Fallout: Factions; Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars; the NASCAR XR App; and the San Francisco Ballet Company’s “The Nutcracker.”
Users can opt to plug a computer or handheld gaming console directly into the Xreal Aura via USB-C to make it an augmented display. The device can also allow for various entertainment and productivity use cases by spinning up a multimonitor setup or a big virtual screen.
For audio, the Xreal Aura uses Bose’s tech to power its sound while watching videos or listening to music.
Given that the new smart glasses are powered by Android XR, Gemini is available to users as a Q&A assistant and can help them understand on-screen context.
The Xreal Aura is available to order starting today in the United States, Canada, Japan, and
South Korea. The 12GB + 256GB version costs $1,279 with a limited launch price of $1,099 through December, and the 16GB + 512GB version is priced at $1,499 with a launch price of $1,299 through December. The company said it will start shipping by mid-November.
In May, Xreal CEO Chi Xu told TechCrunch that building a smart glass business is hard and everyone is losing money. He also said that the Aura glasses will have a wide range of use cases, and the industry has reached an inflection point of having the right hardware, software, and design smart glasses to reach scale.
“You need all the key pieces ready — you need the hardware ready, the operating system needs to be ready, and then you need a great user interface,” Xu said at that time.

articles.title: Samsung's Galaxy Buds On are its first clip-on, open-ear wireless earbuds - Engadget
articles.text:
Samsung's Galaxy Buds On are its first clip-on, open-ear wireless earbuds
It's got a clip-on design to keep them in place.
As competitors like Sony, Bose and Sennheiser reveal their takes on open-ear wireless earbuds, Samsung is taking another stab with the Galaxy Buds On, featuring a clip-on design for a more secure fit. While they don't pack high-level noise cancellation like the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, the company claims its new Audio Leakage Reduction tech reduces sound leakage by protecting reversed sound waves at the rear of each bud, ostensibly canceling it out. The company says it pulled data from over 119 million ear scans to help the Buds On fit across a range of ear shapes and sizes and have IP54 water resistance.
They're also designed to ensure a low-pressure fit around the ear, something many of us crave from open-ear buds, avoiding the discomfort from typical wireless headphones that form a seal around the ear canal. As mentioned, these aren't Samsung's first open-type design; you might recall the underwhelming Galaxy Buds Live. The more recent (and better) Galaxy Buds 4 launched earlier this year and also have an open-type, semi-in-ear profile like recent AirPods.
The Galaxy Buds On pack a new high-efficiency Class-D amplifier designed to balance power consumption and punchy sound. Battery life also looks solid, with an estimated 9.5 hours of music playback on a single charge. With the charging case, that should stretch to 38 hours.
Samsung's newest buds pack three mics and a voice pickup unit (VPU) that detects speech vibrations, which work together to isolate the caller's voice and cut out noise. Algorithms have been trained on a range of ambient sounds, including construction noises and car horns (is that a regular occurrence on your calls?). The Buds On also pack in head-gesture controls: nod or shake your head to accept or decline calls, and even dismiss alarms and notification readouts. The buds will also work with Galaxy smartphone features, including access to Gemini Live, Quick Voice Memo recordings and will connect to Galaxy phones as soon as you open the case.
The Galaxy Buds On will launch in early November 2026 and will be priced at $229.

articles.title: Anthropic weighs up to 20% of IPO for retail as Warren demands answers
articles.text:
Anthropic is weighing setting aside 15% to 20% of the shares in its IPO for retail investors, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg on Wednesday, 28 October. JPMorgan will lead the US retail offering, they said. TNW has not independently verified the report.
The S-1 prospectus only says the banks may set aside shares for their online brokerage customers. SpaceX set aside about 20% for retail investors at its June listing, after first planning 30%, as Samuel O’Brient reported for Business Insider.
“Individual money is less sensitive to price, and a book that leans on it lets the banks price the deal higher than institutions alone would support,” Harrison Rolfes, a senior research analyst at PitchBook, told Business Insider.
Warren wants answers by 3 November
Senator Elizabeth Warren has told Anthropic to answer four pages of questions about its IPO filing by 3 November. Corrie Driebusch reported the letter for The Wall Street Journal, which saw a copy. The Massachusetts Democrat sent it to chief executive Dario Amodei on Tuesday.
She asked how Anthropic can ensure its technology will not become an existential threat to humanity. She also asked about its ties to Amazon and Broadcom, and how it will justify a valuation that could approach $2tn. Anthropic did not immediately respond to the Journal.
The risks “demand greater scrutiny before they become intertwined with the public capital markets,” Warren wrote, according to the Journal.
The risks in the filing
The filing notes concerns, inside Anthropic and outside it, about where advanced AI could lead. It sits alongside the warning that Anthropic could become a political target.
Sufficiently advanced AI systems “could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” the filing says.
It notes that proposed US laws contemplate the nationalisation or mandatory shutdown of frontier AI systems. The rules Anthropic itself argues for could slow its growth, it adds. Government contracts make up about 1% of its revenue.
The same document sizes the prize. Anthropic says knowledge work was worth more than $40tn globally in 2025, which tops SpaceX’s $28.5tn market estimate, as the Journal noted.
More compute deals
TNW has reported the Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Broadcom deals. Anthropic also agreed to spend up to $120.5bn with SpaceXAI, the SpaceX unit formerly known as xAI. That reaches about $3.1bn a month from December. After early 2027, either side can cancel on 90 days’ notice.
It also agreed to spend up to $44.6bn with Nscale and about $41.3bn with Lambda. It expects to pay $125bn to $150bn for more TPU chip capacity from 2028 to 2031, outside its commitments table. Since 30 June, it has signed deals with about $245bn in minimum payments. The total is still blank. The Journal had reported that Anthropic could spend $750bn on compute.
Margins and who pays
Cost of revenue, mostly compute that serves customers, was $2.38bn in the first half, against $16.3bn of revenue. That is a gross margin of about 85%, the figure Semafor called Anthropic’s key number, citing The Information. It leaves out training. Total compute spending was $8.95bn.
“We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all,” the filing says.
Margins may also shrink as new compute arrives before the revenue it supports. Models released in the six months to 30 September made up over 80% of third-quarter revenue.
Sales through Amazon, Google and Microsoft’s cloud marketplaces were 48% of first-half revenue, up from 11% in 2023. Google has an option to buy up to $10bn of stock at the IPO price. Anthropic values the convertible notes Amazon holds at $108.6bn; Amazon puts them at $97.9bn, Equibles Research found.
When insiders can sell
Some shares can be sold from the first trading day. Co-founders and holders of more than 0.5% must wait until after third-quarter 2027 results, or 365 days. Most others are free after first-quarter 2027 results, or 180 days.
In his newsletter, critic Ed Zitron wrote that the company the S-1 describes “no longer exists”. He pointed to the blank third-quarter figures. MBI Deep Dives called Anthropic “a much, much better business” than it had expected, but said it would not yet buy.

articles.title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google is making it easier for businesses to connect their apps to its AI experiences across Search and Gemini with the debut of its Connected Apps Platform.
Introduced in Gemini and Google Search earlier this year, connected apps let users securely link and interact with popular third-party services, then use them to take specific actions. For instance, you could connect to Canva to design a flyer, or to YouTube Music to build a playlist.
We’ve seen varying takes on the idea by other consumer-facing AI services like ChatGPT and Meta’s Muse. The premise is that such integrations could ultimately shift consumer behavior away from launching and using individual apps to instead using their favorite services through their preferred AI provider.
However, to successfully capture and retain consumers’ attention, there have to actually be a wide range of connected apps to explore.
Google’s idea is to open its doors to any business or developer that wants to reach users through Search or Gemini by allowing them to submit their own connected apps and monitor their performance.
The platform preview is currently available in beta to developers in the U.S., and will allow developers to build and submit apps that can be used across Google’s products.
To get started, developers would integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app, Google explains.
Essentially, this process lets devs connect their app to Google’s services so it can be used with the search giant’s AI features. Developers can also choose whether they want their app to be available via Search, the Gemini app, or both.
After the app is live, developers can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and maintain control over their brand identity, such as their verified logos and authenticated accounts.
Similar to how SEO allowed companies and websites to show search engine rankings, this could well be one of the initial steps for businesses that want their services to be more visible to users on the agentic web.
Google already has over 50 Connected Apps available in Gemini, including from partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, Peloton, and others, in addition to its own expansive set of services, from Workplace and Photos to YouTube Music and Google Home.
These apps will now come to Google Search over the next few weeks. Search today has fewer integrations, featuring apps like Instacart, Canva, YouTube Music, Yahoo Fantasy Football, and others.
Google said meditation app Calm is another new partner on this effort, and that its app will soon launch on both Gemini and Search.
The new Connected Apps platform is in public preview for U.S. developers who sign up for the waitlist. Google did not share when it would become more broadly available.

articles.title: Vietravel Airlines đón tàu bay mới, mở rộng mạng bay quốc tế
articles.text:
Tăng quy mô đội tàu, thêm đường bay mới
Việc bổ sung tàu bay giúp Vietravel Airlines tăng cường năng lực khai thác cho giai đoạn cao điểm cuối năm 2026 và dịp Tết Nguyên đán Đinh Mùi 2027. Đây cũng là nền tảng để hãng mở rộng các đường bay trọng điểm.
Cụ thể, đường bay Hà Nội - Thâm Quyến (Trung Quốc) sẽ được đưa vào khai thác từ ngày 14/11/2026, ngay trước thềm Hội nghị cấp cao APEC diễn ra tại Thâm Quyến. Tiếp đó, đường bay thẳng thường lệ Hà Nội - Ma Cao (Trung Quốc) dự kiến khai thác từ ngày 29/11/2026. Bên cạnh đó, hãng đang xúc tiến làm việc với các đối tác liên quan để thực hiện kế hoạch mở bán các đường bay Hà Nội - Đài Bắc (Đài Loan, Trung Quốc) và Đà Nẵng - Cao Hùng (Đài Loan, Trung Quốc) trong tháng 11/2026.
Đại diện Ban Lãnh đạo Vietravel Airlines chia sẻ: “Việc tiếp tục đón thêm tàu bay mới giúp Vietravel Airlines chủ động hơn về nguồn lực khai thác trong giai đoạn cao điểm cuối năm, đồng thời tạo điều kiện để hãng mở rộng mạng đường bay, đặc biệt là các tuyến quốc tế trọng điểm. Cùng với việc đầu tư đội tàu bay, Vietravel Airlines cũng đang triển khai các chương trình ưu đãi để hành khách có thêm nhiều lựa chọn di chuyển với chi phí hợp lý”.
Nhân dịp mở đường bay mới, Vietravel Airlines triển khai chương trình ưu đãi giảm 50% giá vé chặng Hà Nội - Thâm Quyến, áp dụng đến hết ngày 13/11/2026. Đây là cơ hội để hành khách khám phá thành phố công nghệ năng động của Trung Quốc, đồng thời thuận tiện hơn trong việc kết nối thương mại, công tác và du lịch giữa hai quốc gia.
Song song đó, hãng triển khai chương trình miễn phí hành lý cho hành khách bay trên đường bay Hà Nội - Bangkok, giúp hành khách tiết kiệm chi phí và thoải mái hơn trong hành trình khám phá thủ đô của Thái Lan. Thông tin chi tiết được cập nhật trên website chính thức của Vietravel Airlines (vietravelairlines.com).
Nền tảng vững chắc cho chiến lược tăng trưởng dài hạn
Kể từ khi gia nhập hệ sinh thái T&T Group vào cuối năm 2024, Vietravel Airlines đã từng bước đẩy mạnh tái cơ cấu, bổ sung đội tàu bay và mở rộng hoạt động khai thác. Việc tiếp nhận thêm tàu bay VN-A295 là một bước tiến trong kế hoạch phát triển đội bay của hãng trong năm 2026, nhằm nâng cao năng lực vận chuyển, tăng tính chủ động và chuẩn bị cho kế hoạch tăng trưởng ở quy mô lớn hơn.
Song song với đó, Vietravel Airlines cũng đang chuẩn bị cho chiến lược phát triển dài hạn. Vừa qua, hãng và Airbus đã trao thỏa thuận mua 50 máy bay thế hệ mới, gồm 20 chiếc A220 và 30 chiếc thuộc dòng A321. Hai bên dự kiến ký kết các hợp đồng mua máy bay trong thời gian tới, với kế hoạch bắt đầu bàn giao từ năm 2029.
Việc tăng cường năng lực khai thác, mở rộng mạng bay quốc tế cùng các chương trình ưu đãi thiết thực thể hiện định hướng của Vietravel Airlines trong việc mang đến cho hành khách nhiều lựa chọn hơn, đi cùng những chuyến bay an toàn và trải nghiệm dịch vụ ngày một tốt hơn.
Hiện Vietravel Airlines đang khai thác các mạng bay kết nối các trung tâm kinh tế và du lịch trọng điểm trong nước như TP. HCM - Phú Quốc, Đà Nẵng, Hải Phòng, Thanh Hóa, Vinh, Hà Nội - TP. HCM, Buôn Ma Thuột, Cam Ranh, Đà Lạt, Đà Nẵng. Đồng thời, hãng cũng đang từng bước mở rộng hiện diện tại các thị trường quốc tế với các đường bay thường lệ kết nối Hà Nội, TP. HCM với Bangkok (Thái Lan), TP.HCM - Thâm Quyến (Trung Quốc).

articles.title: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
articles.text:
Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don’t like AI, and it’s not just young people and creatives. Appearing on the Colin and Samir podcast to talk about the launch of widescreen and long-form video for Instagram, Mosseri said he thinks there’s a trend of “more anxiety and more frustration and more anger about AI,” particularly in creative industries:
Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
The Instagram boss said that worries about AI come down to ‘a fear of being left behind in some way.’
It’s not only getting worse, it’s going to continue to get worse. I think we’re going to see more frustration and anger, some of it founded, some of it unfounded, over the next couple of years, and that’s going to make it hard for a lot of people, not just in the industry.
Mosseri claimed Instagram doesn’t rank AI creators differently, but raised the question of ranking quality, saying, “There’s a lot of great AI content out there, there’s also a lot of AI slop. Do we rank AI content as well as we rank non-AI content? Probably not.” Talking about AI slop again after previously bringing it up in a New Year’s slideshow dump, he said he thinks the term AI “slop” is used “too liberally.”
Instagram began cracking down on AI-generated profiles in August, after launching a label for AI accounts earlier this year, but misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes remains an issue. Earlier this month, Mosseri said Instagram is “actively working out what to do” about AI fakes, but he noted, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.”
Mosseri said Instagram is “now starting to require AI accounts to label themselves, because we think it’s important that people know if what they’re looking at is real or not real.” He also acknowledged there are fears around AI, including from creators:
I think people are concerned about a lot of things. I think they’re concerned about owning their content and models getting trained on their content. I think they’re concerned— there’s people who are concerned about safety. They’re concerned about job displacement, having AI displace whatever it is they do, if you’re a content creator or an engineer or a mathematician. I think there’s concerns about— I mean, fundamentally what I think it comes down to when you really have, like, a heart-to-heart with someone is a fear of being left behind in some way.

articles.title: Chrome's AI-powered Autofill can now dig through your Gmail to fill out forms | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s Chrome browser is getting an update that will improve its autofill capabilities using AI. On Wednesday, the company said that Chrome will get an advanced version of autofill that will help users fill out online forms with suggestions pulled from their Gmail.
That means Chrome could suggest things you might need to know, like a flight confirmation number, membership ID, tracking information, order number, address, phone number, or credit card number by referencing your email.
The update is an expansion of Google’s Personal Intelligence, which already allows users to connect their Google Apps to its AI assistant, Gemini, to retrieve certain details and then use them to answer complex questions.
Though seemingly minor, the update could make Chrome easier to use, which could give users another reason to continue to use Google’s browser and stay in its AI ecosystem. It’s reminiscent of one of Apple’s most appreciated features: the ability to automatically detect verification codes sent via text and display them above the keyboard, allowing users to enter them with a single tap.
As with other Personalized Intelligence features, users can decide whether or not to enable enhanced autofill from their Chrome settings. Sensitive data is encrypted, Google notes.
The feature is rolling out to U.S. users on the desktop, and in the iOS and Android apps for Gemini in Chrome.

articles.title: The Alexa Home Map is a visual way to see and control your smart home - Engadget
articles.text:
The Alexa Home Map is a visual way to see and control your smart home
In case you're sick of remembering what you named your thirteenth lamp.
Alongside a slew of Echo devices, Amazon also introduced a new smart home interface today. It's called the Alexa Home Map, and the company describes it as "an interactive 3D map that lets you see and control your home."
Most modern control panels from the likes of Google and Apple display your collection of connected home devices as tiles on a page. You open an app, whether it's Google Home or Apple Home, and you're presented with rows and columns of these cards. Depending on the type of device represented, you can either tap on a card to turn a light on, or drag a slider on it to adjust things like volume or brightness. But this setup requires you to either scroll through a list of rooms in your home or sort by type of device or pin your most commonly used items to the dashboard.
It's something we've gotten used to, but is not necessarily the most intuitive. With the Alexa Home Map, you can get a digital blueprint of your home, and it will feature animated icons for things you can control. Light bulbs and speakers appear on the map where they're located, which is handy if you've forgotten what you've named a specific fixture and only remember where they're placed.
The Alexa Home Map also works with outdoor security cameras to show you what's around your house, including passing vehicles and pedestrians. But rather than present photorealistic representations of individuals, the map uses a visualization that to me was initially reminiscent of scenes from The Sims. I almost expected some of the faux people to randomly spasm like my Sims characters. I later found out that the visual identity was more inspired by the likes of Tesla's Driving Visualization, which made sense.
According to Amazon, the map "updates dynamically in real time, showing the colorful glow of your smart lights and animations of cars and people moving around your yard." In a demo I saw at the company's briefing event this week, the Home Map even showed precipitation like snow and rain, when it was reflective of the local weather.
The company added that lights on the map will glow "in the same color and brightness they're set to, so a blue-lit living room or a dimmed bedroom looks that way on screen." A speaker that's actively playing will show music notes dancing around it. "These touches make the map feel less like a diagram and more like a living picture of your home, and it'll continue to get even better over time," Amazon said in its press release.
To set up your Alexa Home Map when it's available later this year, you'll start by entering your address. Amazon says "the exterior of your home appears automatically" once you do. Then, you'll have to take your compatible iPhone (or Android when it rolls out there) and walk through your home to scan the interior. This uses LIDAR, so it's likely that there won't be a lot of non-iPhone devices that will be compatible with it.
Once you're done with the scan, you'll need to "place your devices on the map right where they sit in your home." I can't tell how involved this process is – I can only imagine that sitting down and drawing up where all 120 of the lights in your massive mansion would take hours. But that's probably a problem that someone that can afford a mansion would not deign to worry about.
Amazon said that "once your map is built, you can move around it however you like, zooming into individual rooms and switching between floors." You can also filter out the devices you're seeing on the map by their type, so you can quickly get a view of just the lights or plugs in your home. You can also use light mode or dark mode, depending on your preferences.
Alexa Home Map "will start to roll out in preview later this year on the Alexa Home Map app on iOS," and it'll also arrive on the Alexa and Ring apps. In addition, larger Echo Show devices like the Ember Artline Fire TV, as well as the new Alexa Tablets and Echo Show 16. A spokesperson at the event told me that Android support will be coming in early 2027.

articles.title: Meta shareholders sue Zuckerberg to block his non-voting share plan
articles.text:
Meta shareholders have sued Mark Zuckerberg and the rest of Meta’s board to stop a plan for a new class of non-voting shares. They filed the class action in the Delaware Court of Chancery on Tuesday, 27 October. Ryan Knappenberger reported it for Courthouse News.
The plaintiffs are two Steamfitters Local 449 funds and two individual investors, Bruce Taylor and Ronald Mumme. They sue on behalf of Meta’s Class A stockholders. They want the court to block the plan before it takes effect on 19 January 2027, when more than 2.5 billion Class C shares would start trading.
“Zuckerberg has always been fixated with his control over Meta,” the plaintiffs wrote in the complaint.
What the shareholders claim
Under the plan, every shareholder gets one non-voting Class C share for each share they own. Zuckerberg can sell his new shares to pay California’s proposed wealth tax. He controls 60.6% of Meta’s votes through his ten-vote Class B shares.
The complaint accuses Zuckerberg of breaching his duties as Meta’s controlling shareholder, and all 12 directors of approving unfair terms. Directors Robert Kimmitt, Charlie Songhurst and Tony Xu formed the special committee that negotiated the deal. The complaint says they lacked independence from him. Xu has given at least $2m to a political committee fighting the tax, it adds.
According to the complaint, Zuckerberg “bullied” the committee. It says he threatened to block any issue of new voting shares to fund Meta’s plans, and to move out of California. The plaintiffs call the move threat empty, because the tax applies to people who lived in California on 1 January 2026.
From 20 shares to one, and back up
The complaint, which draws on Meta’s own filing, sets out how the talks went. In August, Zuckerberg asked for 20 new Class C shares for every existing share, plus a pay package. The committee called that “excessive”. It offered a dividend that would be paid only if the tax passed, sized to cover the bill.
On 1 September, the committee said a dividend of about one share for every nine was “the limit” of what it could offer. That would have been worth roughly $20bn to Zuckerberg. Its members discussed dissolving the committee or resigning from the board. At a board dinner on 9 September, Zuckerberg said he would list his Palo Alto home for sale on 13 September. On 14 September, the committee agreed to one share for one, nine times its limit.
The $700bn alternative
The plaintiffs say Meta did not need the new shares to raise money. The committee’s banker, Moelis, told it that Meta could sell about $700bn of ordinary voting stock over several years, the complaint says. Zuckerberg’s voting power would still stay above 50%. The committee never asked Moelis for a fairness opinion, the complaint says.
Zuckerberg’s lawyers argued that sovereign investors could not buy voting stock. The complaint calls that “spurious”, noting that Norway’s sovereign wealth fund already holds about 1.5% of Meta’s Class A shares.
A $23.8bn sale, no vote
Zuckerberg can sell 20% of his new Class C shares straight away without giving up any votes. Those shares are worth about $23.8bn, the plaintiffs say. He can sell the rest in quarterly batches over eight years.
He also gets more Class C shares each time the stock doubles. The plaintiffs say that target is “spring-loaded”. It is measured from $580.60, an average of prices from 29 July to 9 September. Most of that period came before Meta launched its Muse AI agent. By 24 September, Meta’s shares were 33.9% above that price.
Class A shareholders got no vote. Zuckerberg approved the plan himself by written consent. Since 2014, a majority of independent shareholders has backed each of 13 proposals for one vote per share, and his votes defeated them all, the complaint says. Meta’s shares fell more than 9.6% in the three trading days after the plan was announced, it adds.
“Zuckerberg receives immediate and continuing opportunities to monetize his Meta equity while retaining majority voting control,” the complaint says.
Meta’s position
No court has ruled on the plaintiffs’ claims. Meta defended the plan when it announced it, in a statement to CNBC.
“There were many driving factors that led the board and special committee to approve the Class C shares, and it would be misleading to attribute it to any single reason,” Meta said.
Meta’s filing said the new shares let the company raise money without diluting Zuckerberg’s control. On Monday, Meta launched a $35bn share sale to fund its AI spending.
The plaintiffs point to a ruling by the same court on 16 October, which blocked a similar share plan at Cloudflare. Californians vote on the tax, Proposition 40, on 3 November. By July, tech billionaires had put $120m into defeating the tax.

articles.title: A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
articles.text:
A hacker stole a trove of personal information from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The breach exposes the names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses, and office locations of more than 41,000 employees, including those in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), according to TechCrunch and Wired. The data also linked the agencies to specific surveillance tools.
A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
The names, job titles, phone numbers, and emails of thousands of ICE, CBP, and other DHS employees were compromised in a massive hack.
As reported by TechCrunch, a hacker known as “Department of Peace” gained access to the data through Okta, an identity and access management service used by the DHS. Around 21,000 records pertain to CBP employees, and nearly 7,000 belong to staff at ICE. The data also includes records from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI).
The DHS has worked to conceal the identities of CBP and ICE agents, who have carried out anti-immigration raids around the US, while also tracking down online critics. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” the “Department of Peace” hacker said, according to TechCrunch. This leak comes just weeks after hackers stole data from the FBI on its employees and job applicants.
The leaked DHS information was reportedly given to cybersecurity researcher maia arson crimew, who shared it with Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), a nonprofit organization that’s now hosting the leaked “Icepick” dataset. The leak also reportedly includes information about DHS groups that have access to tools that can be used for surveillance, such as the facial recognition app Mobile Fortify and PenLink, which can collect and analyze data from phones and online services.
The DHS didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

articles.title: CXMT to start AI memory production as only 20% to 30% of chips work
articles.text:
China’s biggest memory chipmaker, CXMT, plans to start making HBM3E, an advanced memory used in AI chips, even though only 20% to 30% of the chips it makes are usable. Two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, which reported the details on Wednesday, 28 October. TNW has not independently verified the report.
CXMT has sent HBM3E samples to several Chinese AI chip designers, the people said. It expects to begin limited production within the next two months, one of them said. The Information first reported CXMT’s HBM3E plans; the yield figures and timeline are new from Reuters.
A yield of 20% to 30%
High-bandwidth memory (HBM) stacks memory chips on top of each other so they can pass data quickly to AI processors. It is a key part of the chips that train and run large language models.
Yield is the share of chips from a production line that meet specifications. CXMT’s is about 20% to 30%, the people told Reuters. SK Hynix, the market leader, gets around 70%. Low yields make production expensive, because the company must throw away or rework many chips.
In testing, CXMT’s HBM3E performed closer to SK Hynix’s older HBM3 than to its HBM3E, one of the people said. CXMT has sent customers two versions: a standard design and an update meant to improve yields. Its chip will likely cost more than comparable foreign products, one of the people said.
Why China is pressing ahead
Chinese AI chipmakers cannot get enough advanced memory to raise output, the people said. The US tightened export controls on some advanced HBM products bound for China in December 2024. Chinese firms have since sought the memory through unofficial channels, where it can cost several times more, according to the people.
Last month, Huawei, Cambricon, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX raised prices for their AI chips by 20% to 50% as memory costs rose, Reuters reported earlier. Cambricon’s latest sales missed expectations as chip supply tightened.
At least a generation behind
SK Hynix held 50% of global HBM revenue in the second quarter, according to Counterpoint Research. Samsung had 33% and Micron 18%. CXMT held 10% of global DRAM revenue, making it the fourth-largest supplier of conventional memory, Counterpoint said.
CXMT said in September that it had caught up with Samsung and Micron in conventional memory. It also swung to a profit of nearly $20bn this year as memory prices soared.
In HBM, its rivals have moved on. SK Hynix said on Wednesday that HBM4 had beaten its target yield and would pass HBM3E in shipments and revenue in the fourth quarter. It posted record profit in the same results. Samsung said in July that it had expanded HBM4 sales and shipped HBM4E samples.

articles.title: Meta's Waddle World is a Tamagotchi-like AI pet app - Engadget
articles.text:
Meta's Waddle World is a Tamagotchi-like AI pet app
But it's only available in the Philippines for now.
Looks like a big part of Meta's AI strategy is to rely on "uwu" and cuteness as a way to get people to use and train its models and agents. The company has released a new Tamagotchi-like AI-powered pet-rearing game called Waddle World, but it's only available in the Philippines for now. If you've ever played Tamagotchi or any other virtual pet game, Waddle World will feel very familiar. You hatch an egg to get a pet, then you have to play with it and feed it to keep you happy. This virtual pet, however, can chat with you and even create illustrated journal entries to illustrate your conversations.
Social media consultant Matt Navarra has posted links to its Apple App Store and Google Play store listings on X. Based on those listings, the game first became available in late September. Waddle World is a 16-bit game that Meta describes as a "daily journal disguised as a pet." You'll be able to write or dictate a journal entry, which the game presents as a way to communicate with your pet. Every time you write in your diary, your pet writes back and draws a little doodle to go with the entry. The responses are, of course, powered by Meta's AI. As Navarra noted, this is basically "Tamagotchi meets ChatGPT."
In addition to the app's journaling features, you can play mini-games to collect points that you can use to buy food and toys for your pet. One mini-game will have you stacking grocery items on top of your pet's head. Another will have you catching falling stars and dodging bombs. The third game will have you spelling words using the jumbled letters on the screen. It's not clear why it has such limited availability at the moment, but it's possible that the company is testing it in the Philippines before giving it a wider release.
Meta already lets you design cute avatars and designate a personality for your Muse agent. It also revealed the "Muse Charm" at its Connect event in September. The Muse Charm, designed to be an AI companion, is an egg-shaped physical device like the Tamagotchi that contains your Muse avatar. It's small enough to be a keychain, created so that you'll have constant access to Muse — or for Muse to have constant access to your environments and experiences. Meta is aiming to release the device in time for the holidays this December.

articles.title: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the 'For You' feed | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Reddit is the latest social platform to adopt the “For You” feed popularized by TikTok. The company announced on Wednesday that users will now see two options when opening the platform: “For You” and “Following.”
The “For You” feed combines posts from communities users have joined with recommendations tailored to their interests. Reddit says the feature will help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not have otherwise come across. The “Following” feed only displays posts from communities they have joined.
The company says the change is designed to foster connection, participation, and belonging.
Reddit is likely hoping that the redesigned feed experience will nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow. It also brings Reddit more in line with the recommendation-driven experience that’s become standard across social media, where algorithms play a significant role in shaping what users see.
With the launch, Reddit joins a number of popular platforms that have adopted “For You”-style feeds, including Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook.
Of course, not everyone will welcome the change, as some users may prefer the more focused feed experience of only seeing posts from communities they’ve joined, rather than having recommended content mixed into their home feed. Some users who encountered the new feed during its initial testing phase have already expressed their frustration with the change.
Reddit says users can switch between feeds and return to the one they last viewed the next time they open the platform.
It’s worth noting that although Reddit has long recommended posts from outside users’ subscribed communities, the new layout gives those recommendations their own feed on the homepage.
“This new feed experience is a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant – an idea, a connection, a unique perspective, or even a new interest,” the company wrote in a blog post. “A more human internet is not just something you sit back and watch, it is something you find value in and want to participate in.”
The new feed experience is rolling out globally over the next few weeks, the company says.

articles.title: Sắp hết hạn nộp thuế đất, dân chung cư vội vã nghỉ việc để kê khai
articles.text:
Theo quy định, ngày 31/10 hàng năm là thời hạn nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp đối với các tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân có quyền sử dụng đất thuộc diện chịu thuế.
Theo Điều 4 Luật Thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp năm 2010 và Điều 3 Thông tư 153/2011 của Bộ Tài chính, người được Nhà nước giao hoặc cho thuê đất để xây dựng nhà ở bán, cho thuê là người nộp thuế. Khi quyền sử dụng đất được chuyển nhượng, nghĩa vụ thuế thuộc về bên nhận chuyển nhượng.
Thuế TP Hà Nội cho biết, đất ở đô thị, nông thôn, bao gồm đất xây dựng chung cư, thuộc diện chịu thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp. Thuế đối với căn hộ được tính dựa trên phần diện tích đất phân bổ cho từng căn hộ.
Như vậy, theo cơ quan thuế, thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp đối với nhà chung cư là nghĩa vụ tài chính bắt buộc của tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân có quyền sử dụng đất gắn với căn hộ chung cư.
Thực tế, không ít cư dân chưa nắm rõ quy định nên dù mua căn hộ và sinh sống tại chung cư nhiều năm vẫn chưa thực hiện thủ tục kê khai, nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp.
Chị Bảo Hân ở phường Định Công (Hà Nội) mua căn hộ chung cư từ năm 2019. Do không để ý đến nghĩa vụ thuế, đến nay chị mới đến cơ quan thuế làm thủ tục kê khai.
Lo lắng chậm thủ tục, chậm nộp lại bị phạt, chị xin nghỉ việc 1 ngày để mang hồ sơ ra trụ sở Thuế cơ sở 13 Hà Nội theo hướng dẫn của tổ dân phố.
Chị Hân là một trong những trường hợp không nhận được thông báo thuế hoặc không có thông tin về thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp trên ứng dụng eTax Mobile, có thể trực tiếp đến Thuế cơ sở 13 TP Hà Nội để được hướng dẫn kê khai để nộp thuế.
Khi đi, người dân cần mang theo căn cước công dân và bản sao giấy chứng nhận quyền sử dụng đất, quyền sở hữu tài sản gắn liền với đất để phục vụ việc kê khai.
Chị Hân cho biết, khi đến Thuế cơ sở 13, chị thấy nhiều người cũng đang chờ được hướng dẫn về kê khai thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp. Đến lượt, chị Hân cũng được cán bộ thuế hỗ trợ hoàn thiện thủ tục.
Sau khoảng 30 phút, số tiền thuế và tiền chậm nộp đối với căn hộ rộng 76m2 của gia đình đã hiển thị trên ứng dụng eTax Mobile. Chị thực hiện nộp thuế trực tiếp qua ứng dụng, với tổng số tiền hơn 155.000 đồng.
Tương tự như chị Hân, nhiều người dân ở chung cư hiện cũng đang gấp rút thực hiện kê khai, nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp trong những ngày này để kịp hoàn tất đúng hạn theo quy định.
Có nơi, tổ trưởng dân phố nhiệt tình nhận 'vác tù và hàng tổng", tin nhắn được gửi vào nhóm cư dân "ai bận cần em hỗ trợ nộp hồ sơ kê khai thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp thì mang bản photo sổ đỏ và CCCD nộp cho em nhé. Em sẽ hướng dẫn khai hoặc khai giúp cho từng nhà có nhu cầu và nộp hộ luôn".
Theo tìm hiểu, việc triển khai đợt cao điểm hỗ trợ người nộp thuế cài đặt và nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp năm 2026 qua ứng dụng eTax Mobile đã và đang được các phường ở Hà Nội tổ chức trong thời gian này.
Chẳng hạn, tại UBND phường Hoàng Liệt, đợt cao điểm được triển khai trong giờ hành chính, từ ngày 27/10 đến ngày 31/10 để hỗ trợ người nộp thuế hoàn thành nghĩa vụ nộp thuế đất.
Thuế TP Hà Nội lưu ý, việc không kê khai, nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp có thể dẫn đến nguy cơ bị truy thu thuế, tính tiền chậm nộp và xử phạt vi phạm hành chính theo quy định.
Ngoài nghĩa vụ tài chính phát sinh, người dân cũng có thể gặp vướng mắc khi thực hiện các thủ tục liên quan đến nhà đất. Khi chuyển nhượng, tặng cho, thừa kế hoặc làm thủ tục cấp, sang tên giấy chứng nhận quyền sử dụng đất, quyền sở hữu tài sản gắn liền với đất (sổ hồng), cơ quan chức năng có thể yêu cầu hoàn thành các nghĩa vụ tài chính liên quan.
Một vấn đề khác là việc đối soát nghĩa vụ thuế có thể mất nhiều thời gian nếu căn hộ đã được mua bán từ lâu nhưng chưa kê khai hoặc thông tin chủ sở hữu chưa được cập nhật đầy đủ. Khi rà soát lại, số tiền thuế còn thiếu có thể cộng dồn qua nhiều năm, khiến người dân phải giải trình và hoàn thiện hồ sơ.
Vì vậy, người sở hữu căn hộ chung cư nên chủ động kiểm tra thông tin thuế trên eTax Mobile. Nếu chưa có dữ liệu hoặc chưa rõ tình trạng nghĩa vụ thuế, người dân cần liên hệ cơ quan thuế hoặc UBND phường để được hướng dẫn kê khai, nộp thuế theo quy định.
| Theo điểm a khoản 1 Điều 21 Nghị định số 252/2026/NĐ-CP của Chính phủ, thời hạn nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp lần đầu là chậm nhất 30 ngày kể từ ngày cơ quan thuế ban hành thông báo nộp thuế. Từ năm thứ hai trở đi, người nộp thuế thực hiện nộp thuế một lần trong năm, chậm nhất vào ngày 31/10. Riêng năm 2026, do ngày 31/10 rơi vào thứ Bảy, hạn nộp được xác định là ngày làm việc tiếp theo, tức ngày 2/11/2026. |

articles.title: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
articles.text:
The MPC Sample Key isn’t even formally announced yet, but Akai is already showing off what the modding community is cooking up through vibe coding. Akai has decided to embrace the explosion of hackers and custom firmware developers by giving them early access to the device, which will have open-source firmware.
Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
The MPC Sample Key will be an open-source 37-key take on its budget-friendly MPC Sample.
It will likely run some version of the same software found on the MPC Sample, but with tweaks to accommodate the traditional keyboard, pitch, and mod wheels. Unlike the higher-end MPC Key 37, however, the Sample Key doesn’t have pads. Instead, you play back samples with the keys.
In the short Instagram Reels posted last night and today, Akai shows a number of vibe-coded mods that add synths, including Native Instruments Massive, to the device, as well as virtual analog and FM synths. One is even shown running a completely custom OS, with “several different synths in it.”
According to the clips, the same “community” features will come to the regular MPC Sample, which is also shown running a few vibe-coded synths built by Claude. That could mean Akai plans to open-source the entire MPC Sample platform.
CEO Jack O’Donnell told The Verge that inMusic brands, especially Akai, would be looking to embrace the modding community by seeding early devices to developers. These efforts will also include open-sourcing some software and providing an SDK.

articles.title: iOS 27.2 brings two new features to Apple's CarPlay - Engadget
articles.text:
iOS 27.2 brings two new features to Apple's CarPlay
Apple has redesigned the Podcasts app and upgraded Siri AI.
Apple has officially released iOS 27.2, bringing more Siri and AI functions to iPhone users. And since CarPlay is powered by iOS running directly from a connected iPhone, the rollout introduces some changes to it, as well. As 9to5Mac reports, you can expect two big changes coming to CarPlay with the new mobile OS.
First, the company has updated its Podcasts' app Home tab to add a New Episodes and a Continue Playing section. It removed Up Next altogether and replaced it with those two. So, if you want to find the latest installments for the shows you're watching, you have to go to the New Episodes section. And if you want to pick up watching a show from where you left off, you'll find it in — you guessed it — the Continue Playing section.
In addition, iOS 27.2 brings a couple of Siri AI upgrades to CarPlay. Like Siri on mobile, the assistant on CarPlay can now recall past conversations, allowing you to ask it to recall previous chats. You can ask it to repeat its previous cafe recommendations, for instance, if you couldn't find your chat from last week. Siri AI on CarPlay can now also draw from more sources for more detailed responses, including your voicemails, your Safari history and Reading List, the attendees in your Calendar events and even photos attached in Messages.
The update comes with a few minor changes, as well, including a new Music app icon. Apple has transformed its recognizable red color into something monochromatic. The app is now white with a black music note, unless you're on dark mode, in which case it's black with a white note. Users on the CarPlay subreddit are also reporting that their infotainment system doesn't support the APTV, which lets them play videos on their car screen, anymore after updating to iOS 27.2

articles.title: DOJ looks into Nvidia's $12.9B Hugging Face deal, Reuters reports
articles.text:
The US Justice Department is asking how Nvidia’s $12.9B purchase of Hugging Face would affect competition in AI, including whether it would hand Nvidia a key distribution point for models. The questions run alongside a years-long probe into Nvidia’s conduct.
The US Justice Department is asking how Nvidia’s $12.9B purchase of Hugging Face would affect competition in AI, Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing two people familiar with the matter.
Officials want to know whether the deal would let Nvidia “capture a fundamental distribution point for AI,” Reuters said. They also want to know if Nvidia could use Hugging Face to hurt rivals.
Hugging Face is where developers share open AI models and data for anyone to use. Nvidia agreed to buy it in September, promising to keep the platform open. It expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027.
The DOJ declined to comment, citing long-standing policy. But it said it “will continue to prioritize advancement of Super Intelligence,” the White House’s term for AI. Nvidia declined to comment, and Hugging Face did not respond.
The questions run alongside a years-long DOJ probe into Nvidia’s conduct, which began under President Joe Biden. It covers the chipmaker’s deals, its stakes in other firms and how it sells chips, including whether it put pressure on buyers. Nvidia also faces an antitrust probe in France.
Last month, the DOJ was reported to be examining whether Nvidia set up its $20B Groq deal to avoid a merger review. Nvidia licensed Groq’s technology and hired its top executives rather than buying the company.
Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, has used its grip on AI chips to move into software and models. It is also in talks with Reflection AI, a maker of open AI models it already backs, about a takeover or a bigger investment.

articles.title: AI execs may be too out of touch to build for the general public | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Former Yahoo CEO and early Google engineer Marissa Mayer is catching a lot of flak for how she uses AI. In an interview about her new app Dazzle, an AI assistant that learns from your camera roll, Mayer poses what she believes is an impressive flex for the product: It helped her come up with three bullet points about her 10-year-old daughter for a birthday presentation at school, describing her as “empathetic, creative, and an animal lover.”
It’s a vague description, like a generic horoscope — it could probably describe a lot of 10-year-olds.
Some onlookers, like progressive activist Leah Greenberg, marveled that “the fact that Marissa Mayer would voluntarily disclose this to a reporter is a pretty good demonstration of how deeply the culture of Silicon Valley has diverged from the rest of humanity.”
Perhaps Mayer drew so much backlash because we have repeatedly observed sheltered billionaires suggest that we outsource child-rearing — one of life’s greatest tests of patience, humility, and kindness — to a computer that is incapable of understanding human emotion.
We’ve been primed for this frustration. Last year, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Bored Ape owner and late night host Jimmy Fallon on national television, “I cannot imagine … figuring out how to raise a newborn without ChatGPT.” The public didn’t love that comment, either, but Altman wasn’t fazed by the negative feedback. A few months ago, he said on X that a “cool use case” of ChatGPT Work would be creating a podcast that talks about your kids’ upcoming birthdays or soccer games and “explain[s] your kids’ interests.” (He was brutally ratioed with comments like, “What if you just talked to your children?”)
After publication, Mayer defended herself in a long X post. She claims she was not relying on Dazzle to explain her child to her, but rather, she was testing what her prototype could do — it resurfaced photos of “forgotten kindergarten projects,” like a “snake devenomer” or “sandcat playground,” illustrating her daughter’s creativity and care for animals.
Fair enough. But Mayer remarks in the same interview that people could also use her AI to outsource the mental load of “figuring out the theme for your child’s birthday party.” She says she’s used her app to plan a playdate for her daughter, book family activities on vacation, and decide what to be for Halloween. She even proposes that her AI assistant could coordinate plans with her husband’s AI assistant. When the reporter asks her if it’s depressing to imagine this “frictionless future … planned by AI,” Mayer replies, “I haven’t really thought that through.”
These leaders seem to write off the naysayers as part of a small, angry fringe group. Yet a Pew Research Center study reports that 50% of U.S. adults think that AI will reduce people’s ability to form meaningful relationships. Only 5% of respondents said AI would make it easier to build these connections.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, however, joins his Silicon Valley kin in envisioning a world where our social needs are met via AI.
“The average American I think has, it’s fewer than three friends, three people they’d consider friends, and the average person has demand for meaningfully more, I think it’s like 15 friends,” Zuckerberg said last year on a podcast. “The average person wants more connectivity, connection than they have.”
Zuckerberg predicts that it will become more socially acceptable to outsource our emotional needs to AI therapists or even AI romantic partners. “There are all these things that are better about physical connections when you can have them,” he added. “But the reality is that people … feel more alone a lot of the time than they would like.”
Zuckerberg goes on to explain how virtual-reality embodiments of AI avatars are only growing more realistic. Meta seems to be more keen on improving our relationships with these approximations of humans, rather than between the actual billions of humans who use its platforms each day.
Maybe part of this stems from the culture of the tech industry, which prizes efficiency. People try to biohack their own bodies by optimizing their sleep schedules with health trackers or injecting unregulated “peptide stacks” to maximize their productivity.
If you’re building electric vehicles or computer chips, then sure, efficiency is a clear north star. But our relationships with other people are not a tech product that we’ve been challenged to ship with as little capital as possible. Human relationships are inherently messy, but our connections with one another can be what gives our lives meaning. When we delegate those interactions to computers, we surrender the difficult, yet fulfilling experience of being people.

articles.title: Readwise is taking on Kindle and Kobo for ebook supremacy
articles.text:
For the last several years, Readwise has been building tools for power readers. There’s the eponymous product, Readwise, which stores and categorizes your Kindle highlights to help you remember what you’ve read. There’s Readwise Reader, an app for reading newsletters, PDFs, and web articles you’ve saved for later. And now there’s Readwise Books, a full-fledged platform for buying, reading, and talking about books.
Readwise is taking on Kindle and Kobo for ebook supremacy
Taking on Kindle is hard. Beating Goodreads might be really easy.
Readwise Books is currently in beta, available through invite or to existing Readwise subscribers. I’ve been testing the app for a few days, and it’s a much bigger take on reading than most. Tristan Homsi and Daniel Doyon, Readwise’s cofounders, like to call the platform “Strava for reading” because it can track how long, how much, and how fast you read, and it can show that information to friends you make in the Readwise Books app. The app’s homepage is a feed of what other people are reading, with comments and recommendations laced throughout.
“Strava for reading” wasn’t the original goal of Readwise Books, which has been part of the Readwise plan since the beginning. “Literally, Dan and I talked about this when we first met,” Homsi says. “We feel like Kindle could be so much better. We really didn’t think it would take nine-plus years to be able to get to this point.” But it turns out, Doyon adds, that for all their ideas about innovation in books, “no one sits around wanting a better Kindle.” But there is one thing they do wish for: a better Goodreads. “Everybody hates Goodreads.”
In a sense, then, the plan for Readwise Books is to take on Kindle by first taking on Goodreads. The Readwise Books app offers a nice way to track books you want to read, are reading, and have read; it even syncs with your Kindle account to let you track books you’ve bought from Amazon by taking pictures of your starting and ending pages. You can rate and review books and see what others have said. It’s a little Strava, a little Letterboxd, and a lot nicer to look at than Goodreads.
The long-term goal, of course, is to get people to stop buying Kindle books and start buying from Readwise. Homsi and Doyon have spent the last several years working to reach deals with all five of the major US publishers in order to have a competitive library of books available. That meant endless negotiations, security reviews, DRM debates, and more — both cofounders seem exhausted just talking about the process. But eventually, by several small miracles, they got the deals done. And since those deals govern the price of books, and many things about how they’re sold and presented, they bring Readwise to a nearly even playing field almost immediately.
It all took a lot longer than expected, but Doyon and Homsi think their timing might actually be pretty good. Digital book reading continues to grow, particularly among young people; a huge amount of that reading happens on phones and tablets. Meanwhile, a new crop of E Ink devices like the tiny Xteink and the Boox Palma line have expanded the universe of available hardware for a company like Readwise.
Not long ago, Doyon says, they would have had no choice but to build an e-reader of their own. (And he says they still might.) Now, they can just make sure it runs on an E Ink-friendly flavor of Android.
After a couple of days using Readwise Books, I can say confidently I already like it better than practically all of its competition. It’s a much nicer-looking app than anything you’ll get from Kindle or Kobo; it has lots of ways to customize how books look; and at least for now, I’m finding the tracking features compel me to read more instead of annoying me. (Homsi says some early versions of the gamification features were substantially more annoying.) I’ve found a few bugs, and the half-integration with Kindle is a little confusing in spots, but it’s already a really nice place to read.
Of course, I, like millions of other people, already own a Kindle and lots of Kindle books. Switching ebook platforms is hard, and Doyon says he’s not counting on everyone to do it right away. He says he’s hopeful Readwise can persuade existing users to switch, in order to sync their notes and progress more seamlessly. He’s also hoping that the advent of AI, and the ways in which AI reliance may rot our brains, will get a lot of people back into the idea of reading more deeply again. And that a bunch of those people might be looking for a nicer, more social place to do so.

articles.title: Discord messages in public servers will show up in Google search
articles.text:
Messages posted in Discord’s largest public communities will start appearing in Google and other search engines from mid-December. Discord announced the change in a blog post on Tuesday, 27 October. It covers more than 63,000 Discoverable Servers. It is on by default for adults in most countries, though not in Europe.
Discoverable Servers are the communities that anyone can join without an invite. They need at least 1,000 members and must be at least eight weeks old. They must also meet Discord’s activity and safety rules. Their admins chose to list them in Discord’s Server Discovery. The changes leave private servers, direct messages and group chats untouched.
“This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this,” wrote Kelsey Duncombe-Smith, a group product manager at Discord.
Two stages, both on by default
From 16 November, every Discoverable Server gets a Server Web Page, a public page that describes the community. If admins have not made one, Discord publishes a default page. The pages may also show automated summaries of conversations in public channels.
From mid-December, some messages from public channels can appear on those pages and in web search. They appear in the posters’ own words. Discord will not show usernames or avatars next to them. Discord won’t include messages sent before mid-December. It will label the channels that can appear on the web.
Discord has already tested the messages with game communities including NBA 2K, Rust and Dead by Daylight. During that pilot, all the published posts came from admins and moderators.
How to opt out
Users can turn their messages off in User Settings, under Data and Privacy. One switch covers every Discoverable Server they are in. Messages sent while the setting was on stay on the web unless the user deletes them. Users cannot opt out of the channel summaries, which only admins can switch off.
Admins can choose which channels take part, or opt them all out, in Server Settings under Web Presence. If they change nothing, public channels stay in. A server that does not want a web page at all has to stop being Discoverable.
The message setting is off by default in the EU, the UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia and South Korea. Discord put that down to “legal restrictions”. Users there have to opt in. Discord excludes teen accounts entirely. Discord sorts users by age with checks it rolled out last month.
The privacy backlash
The plan drew criticism from users over privacy, as Lauren Forristal reported for TechCrunch. Some argued that posting in a public server does not mean they want their messages found across the internet. Others asked whether AI companies could train models on the messages. Reddit users have raised the same worry about AI scraping, TechCrunch noted.
Discord says the goal is to bring back what forums offered: answers anyone can find. Earlier this month, it also opened its ad business to smaller brands.
