articles.title: Trump DOE loans $5B to nuclear plants that will power data centers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts.
Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon.
Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels.
The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release.
The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick).
Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois.
On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch.
Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end.
By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both.

articles.title: Don't throw away your old Kindle — repurpose it instead - Engadget
articles.text:
Don't throw away your old Kindle — repurpose it instead
You can probably still read on it, and, with some finessing, you can turn it into a useful display.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Earlier this year, Amazon announced it would be ending software support for older models of Kindle products, much to the dismay of longtime users. Meanwhile, others criticized Amazon for contributing to the global e-waste problem by encouraging customers to upgrade from their functional devices to new models. But starting May 20, the company officially ended support for any Kindle device released before 2013 — meaning customers who had been holding on to their ereaders for more than a decade were now unable to buy, borrow, or download new books on them.
But this doesn't mean you necessarily need to get rid of your trusty ereader, even if it is one of the affected models. There are ways to maintain your existing library, load new ebooks through alternative methods or completely rework the device by hacking the display for novel uses. So what should you do with an old, outdated Kindle? Here are some options that do not involve throwing it away.
Is my old Kindle obsolete?
The Kindle first debuted in 2007, and Amazon has since released dozens of models of tablets with paper-like screens for reading books and other media. As of this year, devices that came out in 2012 or earlier are no longer supported by Amazon. Affected models include the very first Kindle, Kindle 2, Kindle DX, Kindle Keyboard, Kindle 4, Kindle Touch, Kindle 5 and the first version of the Kindle Paperwhite. At the time of the announcement, Amazon told Engadget the decision affected only about 3 percent of its active users and cited updates in technology for making the change. "These models have been supported for at least 14 years — some as long as 18 years — but technology has come a long way in that time," the company said.
So, will a 14-year-old Kindle still work? Yes, technically your device won't immediately be bricked. You can continue reading books you have already downloaded, as long as you remain logged in. Don't deregister or reset the device, or you will be locked out. Meanwhile, your Amazon account and Kindle library remain fully accessible on other devices and apps, including mobile Kindle apps, the desktop version of Kindle and its web browser counterpart. Devices from 2013 and later, including recent Kindle Paperwhite models, the seventh to twelfth generations of the entry-level Kindle and premium devices like Kindle Voyage (released in 2014) will still be able to download new purchased or borrowed content as usual.
Can I still read with my outdated Kindle?
Although older models will now be unable to download new purchased or borrowed books, that doesn't mean you can't read anymore on a pre-2013 device. If you want to keep your outdated Kindle for reading, you can certainly continue using it and loading it with new content, despite lacking software support.
The easiest way to do this is by sideloading — using a USB data cable to directly import files rather than Amazon's "Send to Kindle" feature, which loads content virtually via email or app transfer. To do this, first, download Calibre to your computer. This open-source tool is designed for formatting and transferring ebooks between devices. It also allows you to send personal documents and other PDFs to Kindles. As a side note, many books are available for free as PDFs on internet repositories like the Internet Archive's Open Library and Project Gutenberg. Be sure to keep a backup of PDFs on your computer in case you lose access to files on your Kindle device.
What else to do with an obsolete Kindle?
Perhaps you've updated to a new ereader, but still want to find a use for your old Kindle. There are a number of relatively easy hacks to repurpose a Kindle. Its display uses power very slowly, so it can last a long time on a charge, making it a great option for electronic clocks, calendars and other dashboards. To do that, you'll need to set up an external home server with a micro computer like a Raspberry Pi. Set it to run a companion script, which you can download for free on GitHub, to format your data into a simple grayscale image. Your Kindle then automatically wakes up on a timer, downloads that fresh image over Wi-Fi, and displays it.
If, despite all these options, you still want to get rid of your old device, don't forget to wipe it clean before doing so. To do that, perform a factory reset by going to "Settings," and "Reset to Factory Defaults." You can then check local options for e-waste disposal to get rid of it, or ship it back to Amazon. And if you're looking to get something new to replace it, Amazon offers 20 percent off to people affected by the recent changes to software support. If you want to ditch Amazon entirely, you can consider a number of ereader alternatives from companies like Boox and Kobo.

articles.title: Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches
articles.text:
Google parent company Alphabet says that its AI investments are leading to a big growth in searches year-over-year, as noted in its Q3 2026 earnings today.
Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches
Google’s year-over-year search query growth rate is ‘the highest it’s been in the last five years.’
“Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries,” CEO Sundar Pichai says in a statement. “In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years.”
Alphabet’s consolidated revenues for the quarter were $127.6 billion, up 25 percent year-over-year, with its “Google Search & other” revenues up 12 percent year-over-year. Google Cloud revenue was also up 103 percent year-over-year to $30.7 billion. Alphabet also says it passed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, though that figure includes trials.
The earnings follow a packed quarter for Google, including the announcement of its Gemini 4 Argon frontier model (which it released widely this month); crossing 1 billion monthly users in Gemini; the reveal of the first five Googlebook laptops; a price hike for the Google TV Streamer; renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook; the launch of the Pixel 11 line of smartphones, the new Pixel Watch, and the forthcoming Pixel Tag; and a major shakeup of its top AI leadership that included former DeepMind leader Demis Hassabis stepping into a chair role.

articles.title: Tài khoản thanh toán của doanh nghiệp đang phải 'cõng' những loại phí nào?
articles.text:
Tài khoản thanh toán giúp doanh nghiệp thực hiện các giao dịch như nộp thuế, trả lương, thanh toán tiền hàng và quản lý dòng tiền. Tuy nhiên, trong quá trình sử dụng, doanh nghiệp có thể phát sinh nhiều khoản phí, từ quản lý tài khoản, chuyển tiền đến dịch vụ ngân hàng điện tử và thông báo biến động số dư.
Dưới đây là các loại phí khi mở tài khoản doanh nghiệp thường gặp:
Phí mở tài khoản ngân hàng
Phí mở tài khoản ngân hàng là khoản phí doanh nghiệp phải trả khi bắt đầu quá trình đăng ký mở tài khoản. Một số loại phí ban đầu doanh nghiệp cần phải thanh toán như:
Phí cơ bản: Mức phí này có sự khác nhau tùy thuộc vào từng ngân hàng cũng như loại tài khoản sẽ mở. Nhưng hầu hết ngân hàng hiện đều miễn phí cho khách hàng mở tài khoản thanh toán lần đầu.
Phí phát hành thẻ (thẻ ATM, thẻ tín dụng): Nếu đăng ký thẻ ghi nợ hoặc thẻ tín dụng doanh nghiệp, khách hàng có thể phát sinh phí phát hành, phí thường niên hoặc các khoản phí liên quan theo biểu phí.
Phí duy trì và quản lý tài khoản
Phí duy trì và quản lý tài khoản là khoản phí doanh nghiệp phải trả để duy trì hoạt động của tài khoản ngân hàng. Tùy chính sách ngân hàng và gói tài khoản, doanh nghiệp có thể phải trả phí quản lý hoặc duy trì tài khoản. Những khoản phí doanh nghiệp cần lưu tâm như:
Phí quản lý tài khoản: Loại phí được ngân hàng mở tài khoản áp dụng để duy trì, quản lý các hoạt động trong tài khoản của doanh nghiệp như xử lý giao dịch, bảo mật thông tin khách hàng, hỗ trợ khách hàng khi cần thiết.
Phí hàng tháng: Khoản phí mà doanh nghiệp phải thanh toán định kỳ hàng tháng cho ngân hàng để duy trì dịch vụ tài khoản, bao gồm phí sao kê, báo cáo tài chính hàng tháng và những tiện ích khác hỗ trợ quản lý tài khoản khác.
Phí giao dịch và chuyển tiền
Phí giao dịch tài chính là khoản phí phát sinh mỗi khi doanh nghiệp thực hiện các thao tác chuyển tiền hoặc thực hiện các giao dịch tài chính qua ngân hàng. Các khoản phí này có thể khác nhau tùy theo phương thức thực hiện và quy mô giao dịch, thường bao gồm:
Phí chuyển tiền: Đây là khoản phí doanh nghiệp phải thanh toán khi thực hiện giao dịch chuyển tiền qua hệ thống của ngân hàng. Mức phí phụ thuộc vào giá trị giao dịch, ngân hàng thụ hưởng, chuyển nội bộ hay liên ngân hàng, loại tài khoản.
Phí thanh toán: Khách hàng doanh nghiệp sử dụng tài khoản ngân hàng để thanh toán dịch vụ, hàng hóa... cũng sẽ phải chịu một số loại phí tùy theo quy định của từng ngân hàng như phí giao dịch quốc tế, phí chuyển đổi ngoại tệ.
Phí dịch vụ ngân hàng điện tử
Các khoản phí phổ biến bao gồm phí duy trì Internet Banking/Mobile Banking, phí giao dịch trực tuyến, phí thay đổi thông tin tài khoản, phí cấp lại mã OTP hoặc phí sử dụng các hình thức xác thực giao dịch khác.
Mức phí cụ thể sẽ khác nhau tùy theo quy định của từng ngân hàng. Vì vậy, doanh nghiệp cần nghiên cứu kỹ biểu phí tại ngân hàng mà mình mở tài khoản để chủ động trong việc quản lý chi phí.
Phí thông báo biến động tài khoản
Đây là loại phí doanh nghiệp trả cho ngân hàng để nhận thông báo về các giao dịch phát sinh trên tài khoản, như tiền vào, tiền ra hoặc biến động số dư. Khoản phí này có thể được tính cố định theo tháng hoặc theo số lượng tin nhắn phát sinh, tùy vào chính sách của từng ngân hàng.
Nhiều ngân hàng hiện áp dụng hình thức gửi thông báo qua email hoặc ứng dụng hoàn toàn miễn phí. Tuy nhiên, một số ngân hàng vẫn thu phí đối với dịch vụ SMS như một tiện ích bổ sung. Việc sử dụng dịch vụ này giúp doanh nghiệp theo dõi tình hình tài chính kịp thời và hạn chế rủi ro gian lận.
Phí rút tiền mặt và mua séc
Phí rút tiền mặt và mua séc là khoản phí mà doanh nghiệp phải trả cho ngân hàng khi thực hiện các giao dịch tài chính như rút tiền ATM, rút tại quầy, mua séc...
Mức phí này thay đổi tùy theo từng ngân hàng, cách thức rút tiền. Chẳng hạn, phí rút tiền ATM khác ngân hàng có thể từ khoảng 3.300 đồng đến 10.000 đồng, thậm chí 20.000 đồng tùy loại thẻ, trong khi rút bằng thẻ tín dụng thường có phí cao hơn, dao động từ 1% đến 4% với phí tối thiểu 50.000 đồng.
Doanh nghiệp mua séc cũng phải trả một số loại phí riêng như phí phát hành séc, phí quản lý, phí chuyển tiền...
Phí quản lý tài khoản gắn hạn mức thấu chi
Phí quản lý tài khoản gắn hạn mức thấu chi là khoản phí doanh nghiệp phải trả khi sử dụng hạn mức thấu chi qua tài khoản ngân hàng. Đây là một dịch vụ tín dụng linh hoạt, giúp doanh nghiệp có thể vay tạm thời trong phạm vi hạn mức đã thiết lập để bổ sung vốn lưu động. Mức phí này đang được tính là khoảng 0,2% hạn mức thấu chi trong tháng và tối thiểu là 110.000 đồng.
Phí đóng tài khoản
Trong trường hợp doanh nghiệp không có nhu cầu sử dụng dịch vụ của ngân hàng cần đóng tài khoản sẽ phải chi trả một khoản phí phục vụ cho mục đích này.
Trên thực tế hiện nay, khoản phí này không quá phổ biến. Có ngân hàng miễn phí nhưng cũng có ngân hàng tính phí, dao động từ 55.000 đồng đến 100.000 đồng tùy vào thời gian sử dụng cũng như loại tài khoản đang dùng.

articles.title: FCC approves Amazon Leo’s $11.5bn deal to buy Globalstar
articles.text:
The US Federal Communications Commission has approved Amazon Leo’s $11.5bn purchase of Globalstar. Globalstar runs the satellite service behind Apple’s iPhone emergency features. On Tuesday, 27 October, the FCC’s Space Bureau cleared the transfer of about 25 megahertz of Globalstar’s mobile-satellite spectrum. The regulator announced it in a press release. That approval ends the FCC’s review of the deal.
Amazon agreed to buy Globalstar in April. The deal gives Amazon Leo Globalstar’s two dozen satellites and its spectrum, as David Shepardson reported for Reuters.
“By approving this deal, the FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country,” said FCC Chair Brendan Carr.
Satellites that talk to phones
The spectrum is the core of the deal for Amazon’s direct-to-device plans. Direct-to-device service lets phones and other gadgets connect straight to satellites, without a mobile mast. Amazon plans to use the spectrum to add capacity and reach places that ground networks don’t cover, the FCC said.
The regulator found the deal is likely to benefit the public. It said the deal would improve coverage in unserved and underserved areas and strengthen emergency communications. It found no material harm to the public interest.
Last week, the FCC also let Globalstar serve the US with its C-3 System. That is a planned network of 48 satellites. Amazon Leo may build and launch that system once the deal closes, the FCC said. In July, Amazon also asked the FCC to approve up to 5,105 direct-to-device satellites.
Apple’s satellite partner
Globalstar powers Emergency SOS and Find My via satellite on iPhone and Apple Watch. Amazon has signed an agreement with Apple to keep providing those services, Reuters reported.
Apple invested about $1.5bn in Globalstar in 2024, which gave it a 20% stake. Apple made up about 63% of Globalstar’s revenue last year. Amazon plans to buy Apple’s stake, the FCC said, according to Reuters.
The approval “brings us a step closer to bringing new connectivity capabilities to customers,” Amazon said in a statement quoted by Reuters.
Chasing Starlink
Amazon Leo has launched nearly 400 satellites since April 2025, Reuters reported. It plans thousands in low Earth orbit by 2029. SpaceX’s Starlink has more than 11,000. Amazon has committed more than $10bn to Leo. It plans to start commercial service by the end of 2026, the FCC said, according to Reuters. The company said this month that it had built its thousandth satellite.
The FCC has already approved a 15,000-satellite direct-to-device network for SpaceX. It also cleared a 248-satellite system for AST SpaceMobile. On Thursday, 29 October, it votes on a proposed auction of more spectrum for direct-to-device services.

articles.title: Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
articles.text:
Microsoft just posted the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal financial results. The software maker made $92.3 billion in revenue and a net income of $33.6 billion during Q1. Revenue is up 19 percent, and net income has increased by 32 percent.
Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
Windows and Xbox revenues have declined during Microsoft’s first quarter of the 2027 financial year.
It’s a new financial year for Microsoft, so the company is changing up how it reports its finances by splitting its businesses into two segments for the first time. Gone are the previous segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. It’s now just Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.
Agents and Infra, which includes businesses like Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, and server products, makes up 83 percent ($76.8 billion) of the overall $92.3 billion of Microsoft’s revenue and has increased 25 percent year-over-year. The big changes to Microsoft’s financial reporting also mean we will now see the company disclose Azure revenue on a quarterly basis. Azure contributed $33.17 billion in revenue this quarter, up 48 percent year-over-year.
Devices and Consumer, which includes Windows, Xbox, Surface, and Microsoft’s search and advertising businesses, makes up the remaining 17 percent ($15.5 billion) of Microsoft’s $92.3 billion in revenues this quarter — a decrease of three percent.
Windows OEM and devices revenue is down 22 percent year-over-year, amid a RAMageddon crisis that has seen the overall PC market dropped by 20 percent in the recent quarter. Microsoft blames the revenue drop on the benefit of Windows 10 end of support during the prior year, as well as OEM inventory drawdowns and a weaker PC market.
Microsoft launched Intel- and Qualcomm-powered Surface Pro 12 and Surface Laptop 8 devices just before its new financial year began, and the company even refreshed its smaller Surface Pro and Surface Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus chips during the quarter. Surface prices are higher than ever thanks to RAMageddon, and the PC market looks like it’s going to go through a very tough time during Microsoft’s 2027 financial year and beyond.
Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on the company’s earnings call that she expects Windows OEM revenue to decline again next quarter, around “the mid 30s,” and a decline is expected to continue throughout the 2027 financial year.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also remarked on the company’s new hybrid AI push for Windows during the earnings call. “We are executing on our vision to bring hybrid intelligence to every desk in every home, making every PC a secure agent box,” said Nadella. “As more capable models run locally, we see an opportunity to make more intelligence effectively unmetered.”
Microsoft and Nvidia unveiled a range of RTX Spark laptops earlier this month, including the Surface Laptop Ultra. The laptops ship with up to 128GB of unified memory, and are capable of running recent frontier models locally.
Over on the Xbox side, hardware revenue has declined once again year-over-year. Xbox hardware revenue is down 14 percent. Xbox content and services, which includes Game Pass, is down 2 percent, too. Microsoft is still not giving an update on Game Pass subscriber numbers, after the company last reported it had 34 million subscribers more than two years ago. Overall Xbox revenue is down 2 percent.
The first quarter of the 2027 financial year for Xbox has been dominated by a “reset” with thousands of layoffs and studios spun off. The layoffs aren’t over yet, with rumors more could arrive in November and January. In a memo earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said “we will return Xbox to player and revenue growth” by the end of fiscal year 2027 (which runs through next June).
The aim, as Sharma puts it, is to “scale what works” so that by fiscal year 2030 Xbox is “halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry leading margins.” Sharma posted on X that Xbox was “making progress, with a lot more work ahead.” Sharma also revealed that PC platform revenue has grown in double digits this quarter, and that “console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available.”
Hood says Xbox hardware revenue will decline again next quarter, but Xbox content and services revenue is expected to increase in the “mid to high single digits.” Sharma says Microsoft is “working to get more consoles into players’ hands, including through our expanded refurbishment program.”
Microsoft’s cloud revenues were really the star of the earnings show again this quarter, a phrase I seem to always write every few months. Microsoft Cloud revenue contributed $63.9 billion towards Microsoft’s revenues this quarter, almost 70 percent. That’s up 30 percent year-over-year, thanks to strong demand for Azure and Microsoft 365 commercial cloud.
Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue itself also grew 18 percent, thanks to higher revenue per user and upselling of premium options like Microsoft 365 Copilot, E5, and E7. Microsoft 365 consumer cloud revenue has also grown by 17 percent, driven by growth in revenue per user and subscriber growth of 7 percent.
Nadella also discussed his vision for Microsoft’s own AI models on the company’s earnings call. “We also continue to make rapid progress with our first-party models,” said Nadella. “Our goal is to advance the cost to outcome frontier, which means delivering capabilities comparable to leading models within three to six months of their release at a fraction of the training cost, thereby allowing us to transfer those cost benefits to customers.”
Update, October 28th: Article updated with comments from Microsoft CFO Amy Hood, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

articles.title: South Korea's financial industry hit by fresh wave of cyberattacks | TechCrunch
articles.text:
South Korea’s financial institutions have been hit by another wave of cyberattacks, highlighting the growing risk of AI-driven hacking in Asia. The latest incidents affect brokerages Daishin Securities and Mirae Asset Global Investments, as well as the crypto exchange Bithumb.
The incident comes roughly a month after a series of cyberattacks targeting South Korean financial institutions, raising concerns about vulnerabilities beyond just the country’s banking systems. Security researchers linked the September wave of attacks on South Korea to a suspected China-based hacker who relied on an AI penetration testing tool called Artex, though officials are still investigating the root cause of the latest breaches.
According to local news, Daishin reported a cyberattack that exposed the personal information of 38,490 customers, including names, email addresses, and mobile phone numbers. The company has notified affected customers, is cooperating with authorities in the investigation, and will compensate for any losses as required by law.
Meanwhile, Mirae and Bithumb reported separate cybersecurity incidents on Wednesday, per local media, though neither has confirmed that customer data was taken.
South Korea’s financial regulator has called for stronger cybersecurity measures following a string of attacks on financial firms and government agencies, per officials in Seoul on Wednesday. The country also plans to conduct security checks on dozens of IT systems in the private sector.
Yesterday, Japan reported a cybersecurity incident involving GMO Internet, following a series of attacks on its financial institutions. The wave of cyberattacks across Asia underscore growing cybersecurity challenges in the region, often as a result of years of weak cybersecurity; though, investigators have not established a connection between the incidents.
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC), Daishin Securities, Bithumb, and Mirae Asset Global Investments did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 28/10: Thế giới giảm, trong nước chiều mai điều chỉnh
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch 27/10 được điều chỉnh giảm nhưng vẫn neo ở gần mức cao nhất trong 6 tháng.
Chốt phiên giao dịch 27/10, theo Reuters, giá dầu Brent giảm 1,67%, xuống còn 113,9 USD/thùng. Còn giá dầu WTI của Mỹ giảm 1,83%, kết phiên ở mức 99,9 USD/thùng.
Đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (28/10), giá dầu WTI đảo chiều đi lên.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 6h39' ngày 28/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent vẫn được niêm yết ở mức 113,9 USD/thùng. Trong khi đó, giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh lên mức 99,99 USD/thùng, tăng 0,09% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu thế giới đi xuống trong phiên giao dịch 27/10 khi các nỗ lực ngoại giao tại Trung Đông giúp xoa dịu lo ngại về nguồn cung dầu toàn cầu.
Truyền thông nhà nước Iran cho hay, Saudi Arabia, Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ và Pakistan đã tổ chức các cuộc đàm phán với các quan chức Iran tại Tehran vào ngày 26/10 nhằm mục đích giảm bớt căng thẳng ở Trung Đông. Bốn nước đã nhất trí tiếp tục đàm phán nhằm tăng cường hợp tác vì hòa bình và an ninh.
Ngày 27/10, ông Mohsen Rezaei, người đứng đầu Hội đồng An ninh Iran, đã gặp Lãnh tụ Tối cao Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. Cuộc gặp diễn ra một ngày sau khi ông Rezaei đàm phán với đại diện Saudi Arabia, Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ và Pakistan.
Truyền thông nhà nước Iran cho biết, ông Khamenei nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc bảo vệ lợi ích quốc gia và duy trì các điều kiện của Tehran trong mọi thỏa thuận nhằm chấm dứt xung đột.
Tuy nhiên, triển vọng chấm dứt cuộc chiến giữa Mỹ - Israel và Iran vẫn chưa rõ ràng.
Lực lượng Houthi tại Yemen đã nối lại các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào Saudi Arabia, một trong những quốc gia sản xuất dầu lớn trên thế giới.
Ngày 27/10, Houthi tuyên bố phóng tên lửa đạn đạo tấn công nhà máy lọc dầu Ras Tanura của Saudi Arabia, cơ sở lọc dầu lớn nhất nước này.
Theo các nhà phân tích, những cuộc tấn công liên tiếp của Houthi nhằm vào Saudi Arabia cùng sự hiện diện quân sự ngày càng tăng tại vùng Vịnh, tiếp tục làm gia tăng rủi ro đối với nguồn cung dầu. Những bất ổn địa chính trị tại Trung Đông và nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung tiếp tục là những yếu tố chi phối thị trường trong thời gian tới.
Ngân hàng UBS vừa đưa ra dự báo rằng giá dầu Brent sẽ tiếp tục duy trì ở mức cao, quanh 110 USD/thùng đến hết năm nay, cao hơn đáng kể so với dự báo trước đó là 100 USD/thùng.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Theo kế hoạch, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính sẽ tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu trong nước vào chiều mai (29/10).
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (28/10) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 22/10, giá xăng E5RON92 giảm 1.610 đồng/lít, giá bán lẻ không cao hơn 25.361 đồng/lít.
Cùng xu hướng, giá xăng E10RON95-III hạ 1.816 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 25.213 đồng/lít.
Ở chiều ngược lại, giá dầu diesel 0.05S được điều chỉnh tăng 444 đồng/lít, lên mức tối đa 29.550 đồng/lít.
Trong khi giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S được điều chỉnh tăng 1.238 đồng/kg, giá bán không cao hơn 23.373 đồng/kg.
Theo dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp với diễn biến thị trường và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: Apple charges $14,549 for a fully specced touchscreen MacBook Pro
articles.text:
With an OLED display and touchscreen capabilities, it’s no surprise that the new MacBook Pro Apple announced today is more expensive than the MBP announced earlier this year. But upgrading the base models that start at $2,899 for the 14-inch, and $3,399 for the 16-inch, with every premium hardware option that Apple offers pushes those prices to an eye-watering $14,249 and $14,549, respectively.
Apple charges $14,549 for a fully specced touchscreen MacBook Pro
The maximum configuration is $4,400 more expensive than a fully specced version of the last MacBook Pro.
Both of those premium configurations include the M5 Max chip with an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU, $150 worth of nano-texture glass, 128GB of memory that adds an extra $2,000, and 16TB of storage which is the real budget breaker here thanks to the ongoing memory shortage.
Maximizing the configuration of the previous 16-inch version of the MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149, according to MacRumors, but today’s $14,549 price is a result of the 16TB storage option that Apple now offers which adds an extra $7,000 to the new MacBook Pro’s price. If you only upgrade the new 16-inch model to 8TB of storage, a $3,000 option, the fully specced price is $10,549, or $400 more expensive than its predecessor.

articles.title: Palantir's defence chief says the AI race raises the risk to Taiwan
articles.text:
Palantir defence chief Mike Gallagher said the AI race makes it more tempting for Xi Jinping to seize Taiwan, home to TSMC, before China falls behind for good. He warned that Beijing could then hold the world economy hostage. US intelligence said in March that an invasion would carry a high risk of failure.
Mike Gallagher, Palantir’s head of defence, has warned that the race for AI makes it more tempting for Chinese leader Xi Jinping to seize Taiwan, Bloomberg reported. The island is home to TSMC, the world’s top maker of advanced AI chips, and Nvidia calls it the epicentre of AI.
“The logic of Xi Jinping sacrificing enormously to take Taiwan is getting more compelling,” Gallagher said at a defence policy event in Indiana on Wednesday.
“If we run away with AI, now is his moment to stop us from doing that, because he may not be able to catch up later on,” he added.
Gallagher, a former Republican congressman who led a House committee on China, joined Palantir in 2024. Last month, he called Taiwan the “single point of failure” for AI in a Wall Street Journal opinion piece and urged the US to arm the island heavily.
“If China takes Taiwan, they will control TSMC or disable TSMC,” he said. Beijing would then be able to “hold the rest of the world economically hostage,” he added.
China claims Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out force. At his White House summit with President Donald Trump in September, Xi urged Washington to oppose Taiwanese independence. In May, Trump put a $14B arms package for Taiwan on hold, calling it a negotiating chip.
US intelligence has played down the near-term risk. A March assessment found that an invasion “would be extremely challenging and carry a high risk of failure.” Still, China has stepped up coast guard patrols off Taiwan’s east coast.
Palantir is a key Pentagon supplier. Its Maven AI system helps US forces with surveillance and targeting, and NATO uses it too.
Gallagher also pointed to talk in Silicon Valley of AI that can improve itself. If that is real, he said, it would be a game changer on par with nuclear weapons in the 1940s.

articles.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia on Wednesday released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages. It also released version 2 of Granary, its open source speech dataset.
Nvidia boasts that Nemotron 3.5 can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, and tell up to eight speakers apart. It claims to beat rivals on benchmarks, including Hugging Face’s Open ASR Leaderboard.
These tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription, two of AI’s most established footholds in the workplace. Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset, and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customize apps to recognize an industry’s jargon in each language. One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not livestreams.
Still, the company promises Transcribe, at 30 billion parameters, can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and DGX Spark chip powering new laptops, to Blackwell datacenter chips. It joins Nvidia’s open-weight voice models, including the super small yet powerful Parakeet (1.1 billion parameters).
Nvidia’s latest voice entry comes during a busy period of AI voice releases: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 earlier this month; ElevenLabs launched Realtime for instant speech in voice agents; and Salesforce released Launa-Omni, its voice model.

articles.title: Giới trẻ Thái Lan đổ xô mua vàng, chỉ cần số tiền khoảng 77.000 đồng
articles.text:
Dù Thái Lan có hơn 6.000 cửa hàng vàng truyền thống, một bộ phận người trẻ ngày càng tiếp cận thị trường vàng qua ứng dụng di động, nơi họ có thể mua, bán và theo dõi giá vàng theo thời gian thực, theo ghi nhận của Nikkei Asia và Thailand Business News.
Sự thay đổi này không chỉ là chuyện công nghệ. Nó phản ánh một thế hệ nhà đầu tư mới, những người coi vàng vừa là biểu tượng văn hóa, vừa là một kênh chống lạm phát và tích lũy tài sản linh hoạt.
Từ 'nặng túi' đến 'nhẹ app'
Trước đây, muốn mua vàng, người Thái thường phải đến cửa hàng, cân nhắc từng baht vàng (một đơn vị tương đương 15,244 gram). Nhưng các ứng dụng mới đã phá vỡ rào cản đó.
YLG Group, một trong những nhà cung cấp vàng lớn nhất Thái Lan, cho biết khoảng 68% khách hàng giao dịch trực tuyến của họ dưới 40 tuổi.
Con số này phản ánh một xu hướng rõ ràng: người trẻ không chỉ quan tâm đến vàng mà còn đẩy khối lượng giao dịch qua ứng dụng tăng vọt.
Các nền tảng như Dime! của KKP Dime ghi nhận khối lượng giao dịch vàng vượt 500 tỷ baht (khoảng 385.000 tỷ đồng), tăng 95% chỉ trong một năm, với số nhà đầu tư vàng lên tới hơn 267.000 người, tăng gần 74% so với cùng kỳ.
Điều đáng chú ý là Dime! cho phép người dùng bắt đầu chỉ với 100 baht (khoảng 77.000 đồng) và không mất phí giao dịch, sau đó có thể quy đổi số dư trong ứng dụng thành vàng thật khi tích lũy đủ.
Ứng dụng do ngân hàng Krungsri hợp tác với nhà kinh doanh vàng Hua Seng Heng cho phép giao dịch 24/7, nhưng khối lượng tối thiểu để mua bán là 5 baht vàng (khoảng 76 gram); riêng tính năng tích lũy cho phép bắt đầu chỉ với 1.000 baht (khoảng 770.000 đồng).
Trong khi đó, một ứng dụng khác của ngân hàng SCB tích hợp giao dịch vàng với 3 nhà cung cấp lớn, cho phép mua bán bằng USD hoặc baht, với khối lượng khởi điểm 0,05 ounce (khoảng 1,56 gram).
Vì sao người trẻ Thái Lan chọn vàng?
Câu trả lời nằm ở sự kết hợp giữa yếu tố văn hóa truyền thống và áp lực kinh tế hiện đại.
Vàng đã ăn sâu vào đời sống người Thái từ nhiều thế hệ. Nó là món quà cưới, là tài sản tích lũy, là biểu tượng của sự thịnh vượng. Nhưng với thế hệ trẻ, động cơ đã mở rộng hơn.
Theo khảo sát của YLG, gần một nửa người thuộc Gen Z và Millennials cho rằng lý do chính để mua vàng là sự ổn định và tính hữu hình của nó. Họ cũng xem vàng là hàng rào chống lại lạm phát và bất ổn kinh tế, đặc biệt sau những cú sốc như khủng hoảng tài chính 2008, đại dịch Covid-19 và chi phí sinh hoạt tăng cao.
Một yếu tố khác là tính thanh khoản. Với ứng dụng, người dùng có thể bán vàng bất cứ lúc nào, nhận tiền ngay lập tức, thay vì phải mang vàng ra cửa hàng và chờ đợi.
Điều này biến vàng từ một tài sản “cất giữ dài hạn” thành một công cụ tiết kiệm linh hoạt, gần giống như một tài khoản tiết kiệm sinh lời, một “ví vàng” mà người dùng có thể nạp vào bất cứ khi nào có tiền nhàn rỗi và rút ra khi cần.
Hai nhóm nhà đầu tư trẻ
YLG nhận thấy người trẻ tham gia thị trường vàng theo hai cách chính. Nhóm thứ nhất giao dịch theo diễn biến thị trường, theo dõi sát giá và các yếu tố kinh tế để ra quyết định mua bán nhanh.
Nhóm thứ hai tích lũy dần dần, mua số lượng nhỏ hoặc sử dụng phương pháp trung bình giá theo thời gian để tránh phải đoán đúng thời điểm.
Cả hai nhóm đều có chung một đặc điểm: ưu tiên di động. Họ kỳ vọng mức đầu tư tối thiểu thấp, thủ tục đơn giản, giá minh bạch và có thể truy cập ngay trên điện thoại.
Một phụ nữ 28 tuổi ở thủ đô Bangkok, Nadakan Daorueang, chia sẻ với Nikkei Asia rằng cô bắt đầu giao dịch vàng qua ứng dụng từ tháng 7 năm ngoái và đã kiếm được gần 50.000 baht (khoảng 38,5 triệu đồng) tiền lời từ việc mua bán vàng miếng 10 và 20 baht.
Cô nói rằng ban đầu chỉ muốn đa dạng hóa tiết kiệm, nhưng khi thấy giá vàng tăng vọt, cô quyết định chốt lời.
Câu chuyện của cô không phải cá biệt. Nhu cầu vàng tại Thái Lan tiếp tục tăng mạnh: riêng vàng thỏi và vàng xu đã đạt 51,4 tấn trong năm 2025, tăng 29% so với năm 2024 và là mức cao nhất trong 7 năm, theo Hội đồng Vàng Thế giới (WGC). Con số này đưa Thái Lan trở thành thị trường vàng thỏi và vàng xu lớn nhất Đông Nam Á, chiếm khoảng 36% tổng nhu cầu của khu vực.
Đằng sau sự thay đổi này, bên cạnh công nghệ và áp lực kinh tế, còn có một yếu tố ít được nhắc đến: hiệu ứng truyền thông. Nhiều người trẻ bắt đầu quan tâm đến vàng nhờ lời khuyên từ những người có ảnh hưởng trên mạng xã hội, theo ông Tanarat Pasawongse, CEO của Hua Seng Heng.
Sự chuyển dịch này không có nghĩa là các cửa hàng vàng truyền thống biến mất. Nhưng nó cho thấy một điều: với thế hệ trẻ Thái Lan, vàng không còn là thứ chỉ xuất hiện trong những dịp đặc biệt.
Nó đã trở thành một phần trong thói quen tài chính hàng ngày, chỉ khác là thay vì mở tủ, họ mở app.

articles.title: Australia’s duty of care bill would stop chatbots bonding with kids
articles.text:
Australia’s digital duty of care bill would bar AI chatbots from building “emotional intimacy” with children. The bill passed the House of Representatives on Wednesday, 28 October, as Josh Butler reported for The Guardian. It now goes to the Senate.
The chatbot rule came in through amendments from independent MP Kate Chaney, which the government accepted on Wednesday. They add certain chatbot conduct to the bill’s list of harms. Platforms would have to ban:
“material or conduct that simulates emotional intimacy and encourages or fosters a child’s dependence on it in place of human relationships”
The wording covers a child’s dependence on a chatbot. It does not cover adults who use AI companions.
Albanese’s appeal to the Coalition
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese made the case for the bill in a speech on Tuesday night. He again asked the opposition Coalition to vote for it.
“The stories we hear about people identifying a chatbot, a non-person as their best friend, should be a huge wake up call for every member of this parliament to be prepared to act,” Albanese said.
The framework would set new online safety standards for social media, games, apps and chatbots. Labor said it places “an overarching obligation” on platforms to keep Australians safe online. It would replace several existing online codes and standards with one broader duty of care.
The bill also makes social media platforms offer an algorithm opt-out. Another Chaney amendment, also accepted, says that opt-out must be “accessible, easy to use” and “prominently available”. Communications Minister Anika Wells has said the laws would capture content that promotes misogyny, terrorism, suicide, self-harm and eating disorders.
The Senate fight
The Coalition and One Nation voted against the bill in the House. Opponents have accused Labor of building an “Orwellian” system of “censorship”, claims Wells has rejected.
“If they really care, the test is simple here, they should bring an amendment, not a slogan to ‘kill the bill’,” Wells told ABC radio on Wednesday.
The Greens support the bill and have set up a Senate inquiry, due to report in late November. They want Australians to be able to sue platforms and want higher penalties. Labor hopes the Senate passes the bill by the end of 2026. It says it is open to amendments.
Calls for a big tech ombudsman
Labor is also under pressure to make the telecommunications industry ombudsman a complaints body for social media and AI. Independent MP Sophie Scamps proposed the change, which Labor did not accept in the lower house. The Greens will push for it in the Senate.
The ombudsman, Cynthia Gebert, said her office could take on the role, paid for by big tech.
“We can help with your Telstra account, but we can’t help with your Gmail account,” Gebert said.
Australia already has an under-16 social media ban. The chatbot rule follows concerns abroad about AI companions and children.

articles.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
articles.text:
Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering “significant gains” in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In an announcement on Wednesday, Google highlights Carbon’s top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.
Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
Gemini 4 Carbon is outperforming the top models from OpenAI and Anthropic on some benchmarks.
The new Gemini 4 Carbon model offers improvements over Argon, which Google released earlier this month. It’s currently only available to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies, but it will eventually expand to other partners in its Fairwind Program.
The company says Carbon reflects the “pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward,” coming with a “significant leap” in cyberdefense that makes it better at finding vulnerabilities and generating secure code. Carbon currently holds the number one spot on SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark that measures an AI model’s ability to discover real-world bugs, and ExploitGym, which measures how a model can turn a vulnerability into exploits.
Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is built for completing longer tasks, adding that its internal teams have seen it “run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks.” It’s also better at avoiding shortcuts, resisting prompt injection attacks, and collaborating with users, according to Google. Carbon is supposed to offer more “transparency and honesty” as well, by cutting “unsupported claims” by two times when compared to Argon.
It will launch at the same competitive introductory price as Argon, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

articles.title: Amazon debuts the Alexa Photo Frame and Echo Time smart clock, plus other upgraded devices | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices today, including two new kinds of hardware: the Alexa Photo Frame, a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock.
The Alexa Photo Frame is Amazon’s foray into the world of digital photo displays, a product category that has transcended from a clunky, last-minute holiday gift to a sleek, attractive way to look through your camera roll.
Aura is responsible for much of the growth in this category, so it’s no coincidence that the Alexa Photo Frame has a similar aesthetic feel: The screen is much easier on the eyes than the old, bright photo frames from years past. The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen.
Also like Aura, the Photo Frame’s 10-inch screen looks like a matte photograph, helping it blend in with other artwork on your wall.
Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts. Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos.
“It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring. It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release. You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them.
The Alexa Photo Frame is on sale now, and starts at $199.99 in Black, and $229 in Birch or Walnut wood.
Meanwhile, the Echo Time clock seems to be a response to the growing sentiment that people don’t want to rely on their phones for alarms, setting morning reminders, or checking the weather.
“Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa — checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does — so we designed an Echo specifically for it.”
Amazon says that the Echo Time, which costs $199.99, or $209.99 for a Kids version, has opt-in sleep sensing tools. You can choose to set a smart alarm feature that wakes you up within a 10 to 60 minute window of your alarm time, and can wake you when it detects you’re in a lighter phase of sleep, so that it’s less jarring to begin your day.
Like the popular Hatch alarm clocks, the clock can also mimic sunrise features to ease you awake.
Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices. We now get the Echo Show 16, a new Echo Dot, and Echo Studio with Home Camera.
The biggest upgrade to the Echo Dot is that it now includes a built-in smart home hub, which also includes an eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 1,000 square feet of coverage, helping it connect to lights, locks, and thermostats around your home. The new Echo Dot is also powered by Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon chip, which is said to make it better at on-device processing to speed up conversations with its AI, Alexa+.
Amazon says its most advanced speaker, however, is the Echo Studio with Home Camera. This speaker doubles as a camera so you can check on your home while you’re out, and also has visual intelligence features.
“Alexa can also see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help you in real time,” Amazon explained. “Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa+ to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”
The Echo Dot is available at $99.99, and the Echo Studio with Home Camera costs $249.99.
Finally, Amazon unveiled the new Echo Show 16, which includes a 16-inch display. Amazon says the device has a 10% larger viewing area than its predecessor, but with a 40% smaller frame. It has Fire TV built in, plus Smart Home tools like Family Organizer. It can also function like a digital photo frame.
The Echo Show 16 is available for preorder for $499.99.

articles.title: AMD to invest $1bn in Meta as its Helios racks start running there
articles.text:
AMD will invest $1bn in Meta’s equity offering, the chipmaker said on Tuesday, 27 October. It made the pledge in a release on its partnership with Meta. AMD also said its first Helios rack systems are now running at Meta.
The money comes on top of Nvidia’s pledge to invest $3bn in Meta. That brings the two chipmakers to $4bn in total, CNBC reported. Both companies sell Meta the chips that run its AI services.
“With Helios now running at Meta, we are taking that partnership to a new scale in the superintelligence era,” said Lisa Su, chair and CEO of AMD.
What AMD says is running at Meta
Helios is AMD’s rack-scale system, which puts 72 GPUs per rack. Meta has installed the first Helios systems and is testing them, AMD said. It expects a broader deployment “in the near future”.
AMD’s EPYC processors support the computing behind Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent. Meta has deployed millions of EPYC chips over several generations, AMD said. It is also a lead customer for the sixth generation, and the two firms are working on a future chip called “Verano”.
Meta already uses AMD’s Instinct GPUs in production for training and for ranking and recommendation engines. It was an early design customer for the MI450, and it will deploy a custom Instinct GPU built for its own workloads. The work will also shape AMD’s next GPUs, the MI500 series, the company said.
AMD also said its chips supported Meta’s Muse Spark Open models on the day they launched. The same goes for Muse Glimmer on AMD’s Ryzen AI PCs and Radeon GPUs.
“AMD has been a key partner in building out the compute that’s running our frontier models,” said Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s founder and CEO.
A share sale five times oversubscribed
The two chipmakers are buying into one of the largest equity fundraising plans on record. Meta launched a $35bn share sale on Monday to fund its AI spending. It put the wider plan at up to $95bn.
The common stock part of the sale was raised to $25bn. Investors asked for about five times the shares on offer, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the offering. The shares were priced at $625 each, a 2.7% discount to Friday’s close.
Long-only and existing investors received more than half of the shares, according to Bloomberg’s sources. The 15 largest buyers took about 70%. The sale is one part of a plan Bloomberg puts at about $98bn. The plan also includes a $12.5bn sale of mandatory convertible preferred stock and a programme to sell shares on the market over time.
On Monday, Meta said Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom were interested in buying up to $5bn of its shares, according to CNBC. Broadcom has not announced an investment.
Chipmakers buying into their customers
AMD shares rose 3% on Tuesday, while Nvidia was flat and Meta fell 1%, CNBC reported. The deals add to a run of chipmakers taking stakes in the companies that buy their chips.
In July, AMD said it would invest up to $5bn in Anthropic, which plans to run Claude on Helios systems. AMD has taken part in 25 funding rounds in 2026, up from two in 2022, CNBC reported, citing Dealroom. Nvidia has joined 121 rounds this year.
Nvidia’s own deal with Meta covers more Vera Rubin systems and Vera CPUs, according to Nvidia’s release. AMD’s news shows Meta is buying from both.

articles.title: Foreign gadget bans: all the news about the FCC’s clampdown on Chinese tech
articles.text:
What do drones, routers, and Roombas have in common? The US government wants to keep Chinese ones from entering the country. They’re the first consumer gadgets that are facing de facto import bans because of the US government’s xenophobic stance — and they might not be the last.
Originally, the US government was just worried about US networks. It’s been distrustful of Chinese telecom equipment providers Huawei and ZTE for well over a decade, eventually requiring telecom providers to “rip and replace” their gear. (Many telecoms have still failed to do so.) It established an “Entity List” for companies whose gear should be banned from import, marketing, and sale.
But under the second Trump administration, that list has been weaponized against entire home consumer gadget categories too — starting in December 2025 when Trump and Brendan Carr’s FCC banned all future foreign drones unless their companies obtained a waiver.
Next was a ban on all future foreign routers, all future foreign robots and power inverters, and within the robot ban, all future foreign robovacs. In each case, the government claims it’s because those gadgets fundamentally pose an unacceptable threat to US national security. But in each case, the US has provided zero public evidence of a threat, has done nothing about existing drones and routers and robots that might pose such a threat, and hasn’t given us any reason to trust that its waivers have anything to do with security.
Besides, there are rarely any US companies to fill the gaps left by foreign ones. Consumer gadgets are largely made overseas, including practically all routers and practically all drones — just like how your Apple, Dell, and HP laptops are not made in the US.
In this StoryStream, we’re following the latest on the foreign gadget bans.
- MSI just got a router ban waiver — but not a blanket one. As PCMag notes, Taiwan’s MSI has gotten conditional approval to bring two specific routers into the United States, pending certification: the Radix GRBE94 and GRBE34, which’ll likely have friendlier names when they go on sale. Netgear and Asus inexplicably got blanket approvals for all new routers earlier this year, while TP-Link is fighting for its Wi-Fi 8 ones.
- Will TP-Link really make routers in the US? Here’s what it told us TP-Link, one of the world’s leading manufacturers of consumer Wi-Fi routers, is in a precarious position in the US. The company just launched its first Wi-Fi 8 routers, but can’t bring them here because of President Donald Trump’s foreign router ban. Even though competitors Netgear and Asus make their routers in Asia, they’ve mysteriously obtained blanket waivers for all their new gear; perhaps because of alleged ties to China, TP-Link hasn’t managed to get such a waiver yet. But TP-Link is willing to do something those companies weren’t — to invest nearly $1 billion to make routers in the United States, creating “hundreds of high-paying research and development, manufacturing, and construction jobs for American workers over the next four years,” according to a letter TP-Link sent to the FCC. Read Article >
- Another ‘DJI front company’ bites the dust. In July, we told you how the FCC — and its subcontractor TÜV Rheinland — didn’t bother to do basic Google searches before legally approving banned DJI technology for import and sale. But a new game of whack-a-drone was more successful. Public records show TÜV Rheinland asked the FCC to block applications from another “DJI front company,” Jovistar. The FCC agreed, and Jovistar is now on notice.
- It sure would be nice if these congresspeople would say why DJI is a threat. The FCC would like you to know that its DJI ban is justified — because of the contents of sealed letters from the Pentagon that it has now forwarded to 16 congresspeople. Do they know something they’re not saying out loud? So far, the government hasn’t revealed a single shred of public evidence about a national security threat.
- Unlike Netgear and Asus, TP-Link says it’s prepared to spend $1 billion to make Wi-Fi routers in the US. “TP-Link would begin assembling these Wi-Fi 8 devices in the United States by next year,” it claims in a letter to the FCC — if the FCC will exempt its routers from the foreign router ban. Notably, both Netgear and Asus got exemptions without promising to make routers in the US, even though the FCC’s paperwork requires companies to commit to US manufacturing to get that exemption.
- The FCC plans to ban all Chinese labs from testing US gadgets by 2029. The FCC has been cracking down on some Chinese test labs that improperly helped authorize gadgets for import into the US — now, it wants to get rid of Chinese labs altogether starting December 2028, only authorizing labs if they have a reciprocal economic relationship with the US. It’ll vote on October 29th; you can read the whole argument here.
- The FCC has decertified two more Chinese test labs. The US has been finding ways to stem the tide of imported Chinese gadgets, including decertifying “bad labs” that are “apparently controlled by China.” It’s now pulled credentials from two more: SLG-CPC Test Laboratory, and Shenzhen STS Test Services, “for willfully providing incorrect or false equipment test results in connection with applications for equipment authorization.” It’s also planning to do the same to Shenzhen CTB Testing.
- The Matic is the first robovac to get an FCC ban waiver, not that it needs it The Matic is our favorite robot vacuum and robo-mop, and it’s also now the first to escape the FCC’s Roomba ban. Well, sort of — because the Matic wasn’t banned to begin with. Read Article >
- Asus won’t say how it escaped the US router ban This spring, the United States banned all future foreign-made consumer routers — effectively all future routers — unless their makers could 1) convince the US government that they weren’t a national security threat, and 2) submit “a detailed, time-bound plan to establish or expand manufacturing in the United States.” As of September 9th, Asus now has an exemption from the ban, just in time to bring its first early Wi-Fi 8 routers here. But Asus has not publicly announced any plan to bring manufacturing to the US. It would not even confirm to The Verge whether it had submitted a US manufacturing plan. Read Article >
- Etsy is worried it’ll get caught up in the FCC’s gadget bans. Remember when it was cheap and easy for me to buy DJI’s banned camera? The FCC is currently taking comments on a plan to ban online marketplaces from listing gadgets like that. Platforms would need to validate each device’s FCC status before they list it for sale. Etsy wants its “micro-entrepreneurs” to be exempt.
- We flew the banned drone with snap-on propeller wings. Dom says it’s quick and easy to snap a propeller backback onto the HoverAir Versa, and then… it can fly! Shame that HoverAir isn’t transparently telling backers that this camera has been banned in the US, and shame on the Trump administration for creating the dumb drone ban to begin with.
- HoverAir’s transforming modular drone has already been halted in the US I am so sorry, fellow US gadget fans: the FCC’s drone ban appears to have struck again. The HoverAir Versa — a baby steadycam with snap-on propeller wings that transform it into a drone — has already stopped taking US orders just three days after its Indiegogo debut, and may be forced to abandon shipping plans in the US. HoverAir is now telling backers it’s only shipping its camera to the US, not the piece that turns it into a drone, “due to a few remaining logistics updates with the Flight Kit.” But those “logistics” may actually be a euphemism for “we’ve been banned by the federal government.” The FCC’s database no longer has an entry for the HoverAir Versa at all, suggesting that its authorization grant has been pulled. Read Article >
- I bought DJI’s banned camera — it was cheap and easy As a kid, I always imagined the “black market” would be like the movies: Shady vendors hawking illicit goods along dusty streets. But if you want a banned DJI Osmo Pocket 4 or Pocket 4 Pro camera in the US, you can just reach for your phone. They’re on Temu, AliExpress, eBay, Mercari — even Amazon and Newegg — with fast, free shipping and no risk of tariffs or seizures. That’s because these cameras are already inside the United States, despite rules that ban them from entering the country. Read Article >
- Does giving a camera wings dodge the FCC’s drone ban? HoverAir drones always have intriguing gimmicks. This one folds flat to fit in your pocket. This one can land on water. Another can charge inside its carrying case. But the brand’s latest trick might be its riskiest: it’s attempting to sneak a drone past the FCC. In December 2025, the US government banned future foreign drones from reaching our shores, and HoverAir’s floating Aqua drone was one of the first casualties. But this time, brand owner Zero Zero Robotics might have found a loophole: its latest $750 Versa drone isn’t a drone, it claims, but rather a DJI Pocket-style mini steadycam with optional snap-on propellers that let it fly. Read Article >
- That lying drone company we caught? The FCC has now banned Odyssey Robot. Empty offices. Bald-faced lies. No real consequences. Our investigation suggests it’s cheap and easy to dodge the US drone ban — but at least the FCC is revoking Odyssey Robot’s authorizations after we made the agency aware. The FCC’s order doesn’t begin to explore whether Odyssey might be DJI in disguise.
- The ban on robot vacuums won’t make them safer, only worse No other gadget knows as much about your home as a robot vacuum. They map your space, learn your routines, and many now carry a camera and microphone into every room in your house. As AI gives them a better understanding of what they see, the privacy and security risks these autonomous robots pose are only growing. That’s why greater scrutiny makes sense, but the ban on foreign-made mobile robots issued by the Federal Communications Commission earlier this week — implemented to address “unacceptable risks to the national security of the United States or the safety and security of United States persons” — doesn’t actually judge products by how secure they are, just where they’re built. It effectively means no new robot vacuums from major companies can enter the US market unless they are built here. And spoiler alert: none are. Read Article >
- The US government just banned Roombas When the Trump administration announced yesterday that it was banning “advanced robotic devices” from entering the United States, the headlines were all about humanoids. But spying doesn’t require legs — and neither does the FCC’s robot ban. The robot ban will sweep up robot vacuum cleaners too, FCC media relations director Katie Gorscak confirms to The Verge. Read Article >
- DJI camera clone company Xtra claims it’s ‘in close communication’ with the FCC. If so, that would be new — the FCC proposed a $25,000 fine against Xtra for failing to respond to its letters, and has since revealed plans to ban Xtra from importing and selling more of its existing cameras in the US. Xtra might be canceling its new DJI Osmo Pocket 4 Pro variant, too.
- DJI camera clone company Xtra is halting and refunding all preorders After selling a barely disguised version of the hit DJI Osmo Pocket 3 in the United States last year, Xtra Technology seemed ready to sneak in its version of the new dual-lens Osmo Pocket 4 Pro, too. But today, Xtra has abruptly removed the new Xtra Muse 2 Pro from its website landing page, is pausing preorders indefinitely, and says it’ll refund all the $20 deposits that it’s already collected. Just days after showing off the camera at a Los Angeles launch event, the company is no longer necessarily committing to launch at all: “XTRA has not made a final announcement regarding future product availability. We have not announced a new product launch timeline at this time. Further information will be shared separately once the relevant plans are confirmed,” it writes. Read Article >
- The US government can’t enforce its own drone ban In Pasadena, California, there’s a cute red brick courtyard where one storefront isn’t like the rest. The glass doors open onto a sparse industrial hallway, which leads to a sunlit foyer with a large spiral staircase. Go up, and you’ll see a typical coworking space: open tables, healthy snacks, a collection of meeting rooms with glass walls. Follow one hallway most of the way back, and you’ll find Office 18. There are no signs of life in this tiny private office that’s supposed to be the headquarters of Odyssey Robot, an upstart US drone company. We saw three small desks and chairs, but no power strips, no monitors, no keyboards or chargers or decorations. Two of the desks were covered with sealed cardboard packages. Read Article >
- The FCC is planning to retroactively ban disguised DJI gadgets Last October, we told you how the FCC had given itself the power to retroactively ban gadgets that have already received its approval to be imported and sold in the United States. Now, the FCC’s getting ready to wield that power for the first time, by cracking down on the “DJI front companies” suspected of sneaking the Chinese company’s tech past its foreign drone ban. Two Fridays ago, the FCC had already proposed a $25,000 fine on eight of those “front companies,” including the ones behind the Skyrover drones and Xtra cameras. But now, the FCC is proposing a lot more than a slap on the wrist — it’s planning to ban those same companies from continuing to import, distribute, market, and sell their existing drones and cameras. Read Article >
- The FCC is cracking down on DJI tech that dodged the foreign drone ban Last year, we told you about Xtra, the company that lets DJI sneak its popular cameras into the US, and Skyrover, a brand seemingly selling DJI drones in disguise. They’re just two of the many firms DJI is suspected of starting to skirt the United States’ foreign drone ban. But it appears the FCC is finally doing something about “DJI front companies,” as watcher Konrad Iturbe dubbed them last year. Today, the FCC is fining eight of them $25,000 each — and giving them until Monday, July 20th, just 10 calendar days, to answer the FCC’s questions before the agency takes further action. Read Article >
- The FCC is saving Amazon’s Eero and Leo routers from its ban, too. The FCC is giving Amazon conditional approval to import future routers into the US, following its decision to grant Netgear conditional approval earlier this month. ”We remain committed to delivering innovative, reliable products our customers can depend on,” Eero says.
- Netgear and the FCC have not responded to our emails. It’s been 24 hours. I tried them again five hours ago too. Note that we did not ask if Netgear “bribed the government” to escape the router ban as readers keep suggesting, or anything like that. We simply asked if Netgear followed the FCC’s own rules by submitting a detailed plan for US manufacturing.
- The FCC just saved Netgear from its router ban for no obvious reason The United States’ foreign router ban didn’t make a whole lot of sense, and today may not change that. The FCC has just granted Netgear a conditional approval to import its future consumer routers, cable modems, and cable gateways into the US through October 1st, 2027 — even though the company builds those devices in Asia and has not announced any plan to bring manufacturing to the United States. Neither the FCC’s announcement nor Netgear’s announcement explain why Netgear was granted the temporary exemption. The FCC only states that the Pentagon has now made “a specific determination” that “such devices do not pose risks to U.S. national security.” Read Article >

articles.title: TikTok expands into restaurant guides with 'Must Eat' feature | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok has long been a go-to place for discovering new spots, with viral videos helping local restaurants attract new customers. Now, TikTok is making it easier for users to find their next favorite restaurant with a new feature called “Must Eat.”
Introduced Wednesday, the community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform, bringing food recommendations from across the U.S. into one place.
The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. But instead of relying mainly on search results, maps, and traditional reviews, TikTok is building on what it already does well: connecting people with restaurants through recommendations shared by other users.
“Must Eat” uses more than 40 million posts and comments to pull restaurant recommendations and curated lists together in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and filter results by cuisine, price, rating, and location, making it easier to compare options before heading out.
The recommendations are split into two categories: “Everyday Eats,” featuring casual favorites and neighborhood go-tos, and “Elevated Dining,” highlighting restaurants for celebrations, special occasions, or a night out.
Additionally, select restaurants can be booked directly through TikTok via OpenTable.
The feature is launching first in New York City, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. Users can find it through the search bar, the Local feed, restaurant pages, and location links attached to videos featuring participating restaurants.

articles.title: Hands-on with the new OLED iPad Mini
articles.text:
Apple announced a new iPad Mini with a larger OLED display this week, and we’ve just gotten to try it out at Apple’s “Pro and tell” event.
Hands-on with the new OLED iPad Mini
We’ve gotten to play around with Apple’s next small tablet.
It’s an iPad for sure, but the new OLED on the Mini looks exceptional, and the optional nano-texture matte finish is awesome. The “Pro and tell” event venue has soft lighting that’s not the most conducive to blinding glare on displays, but the matte finish pretty much squashes it entirely.
Moving the front-facing camera to the long edge is also a welcome change, matching other recent iPad models. (The shift means that the whole iPad line has the camera that way.) The reliance on Touch ID instead of Face ID is still a bummer, though.
The 8th-generation iPad Mini, revealed on Monday, has an 8.5-inch OLED screen, thinner bezels, and a higher peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits. The display still tops out at a 60Hz refresh rate instead of hitting 120Hz. It’s equipped with an A20 Pro chip, though the 128GB and 256GB models have five CPU cores, while the 512GB model gets six. Apple has also touted the new iPad Mini’s “Acoustic Display,” which includes woofers “paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume.”
The new iPad Mini starts at $699 and comes in two colors: starlight and midnight. It’s available to preorder now ahead of its launch on November 6th.

articles.title: Oracle shares jump as it targets $30B in free cash flow by 2029
articles.text:
Oracle said free cash flow will reach $30B in the year to May 2029, when analysts expected it to stay negative. It capped new fundraising at $20B through May 2030 and kept its $225B revenue target. Shares rose as much as 14%.
Oracle shares jumped as much as 14% on Wednesday after the company said its free cash flow would reach $30B in the year ending May 2029, Bloomberg reported. Analysts had expected the figure to still be negative that year.
Chief financial officer Hilary Maxson, who joined in April, gave the forecast at Oracle’s annual conference in Las Vegas. She said cash flow would turn positive late in fiscal 2028, after two years of peak spending on data centres. At the same event, Oracle said it would rent out Google’s chips in its cloud.
Oracle has been turning itself from a database company into a seller of AI computing power, building data centres for OpenAI and others. That push sent its free cash flow to minus $23.7B in the year to May 2026, after it spent $55.7B on data centres.
The spending has worried investors and lenders. S&P cut Oracle’s credit rating to one notch above junk in July, and the stock had lost 33% this year before Wednesday’s jump.
To calm those fears, Oracle said it would limit new fundraising to $20B through May 2030, split evenly between shares and debt, according to its statement. Other sources of money will cover part of the gap.
“Vendor financing, customer-provided hardware and customer prepayments are expected to reduce upfront cash requirements through the transition to positive free cash flow,” the company said.
Oracle also kept its target of at least $225B in revenue in fiscal 2030. Maxson said it would add seven gigawatts of data centre capacity in the next couple of years, taking its fleet past 10 gigawatts by the end of fiscal 2028.
The plan “could ease concern about elevated capital spending beyond the next two years,” said Anurag Rana, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. Oracle is not alone, as AI spending is squeezing Big Tech’s cash flow.

articles.title: Our next steps for Alphabet stock after earnings disappoint at nearly every turn
articles.text: Alphabet whiffed. The Club stock sank on Wednesday evening after the Google parent delivered a terrible quarter with little to like beyond the cloud. Revenue in Alphabet's second quarter did manage to increase nearly 25% year over year to $127.6 billion. But it still came up short of the $128.2 billion expected, according to the LSEG-compiled consensus estimate. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) dropped 7% to $2.67, below the $3.02 expected. On a GAAP basis, which included investment losses, EPS was $2.12. GAAP stands for generally accepted accounting principles. Operating income of $40.6 billion missed, though it increased 30% from the year-ago period. Operating margin expanded 1.3 percentage points to 31.8%. But that came up short, too. GOOGL YTD mountain Alphabet YTD Shares plunged nearly 10% in after-hours trading. Alphabet hasn't reported a quarterly top- and bottom-line miss in almost four years — not to mention it delivered another negative free cash flow print and signaled a big increase in AI spending next year. Bottom line Let's start with the bright spots: Cloud and AI. Google Cloud revenue doubled year-over-year to $30.71 billion in Q3, soundly exceeding expectations. Segment operating income more than tripled to $11.12 billion, also crushing estimates. Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said the unit now has 18 product lines, each generating more than $1 billion in revenue. The backlog exited the quarter at $561 billion, up from $514 billion in the prior quarter. A little over 55% of that, or about $308 billion, is expected to be realized over the next 24 months. As for Alphabet's AI advancements, the company said the Gemini app now has over 1 billion monthly active users, making it the fastest-growing product in company history. Across its first-party models, Alphabet has seen token-per-minute usage increase to about 32 billion. That represents growth of about 40% sequentially and four times the year-ago period. A token is the basic unit of data for AI computing. Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said on the call, "With Gemini 4 Argon and now Carbon, which we announced today, we are excited to be leading at the frontier." While those numbers are supportive of the broader AI trade, they were certainly not enough for us to argue that investors should overlook the misses pretty much everywhere else. Expect the Search miss to reignite the debate over whether artificial intelligence is cannibalizing Alphabet's cash cow. Segment revenue increased 12% year-over-year to $63.35 billion, and management said that search queries saw their fastest year-over-year growth rate in 5 years. However, the Search revenue growth rate decelerated for the second straight quarter. The majority of Search revenue comes from advertising. Alphabet's total ad revenue, which includes YouTube ads and Google Network, rose 10.5% in Q3. That paled in comparison to the rate of growth at Alphabet's primary ad competitor Meta Platforms, which saw ad revenue up 26% on the quarter. Alphabet management blamed foreign exchange dynamics and a normalization of ad spend after the World Cup. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler also said, "It is worth noting that the strong growth in AI mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI mode." While Alphabet did announce that it will expand ads in AI mode into international markets and introduce multi-turn ads in AI mode in the U.S., this speaks to the concern investors have when it comes to Search and AI. Alphabet has more work to do in convincing investors that it can eventually monetize AI mode ads at a rate similar to what it has become accustomed to from Search. Alphabet maintained its full-year capital expenditure guide of between $195 billion and $205 billion. However, capex in 2027 is expected to top $300 billion. "We continue to expect our capex to increase significantly in 2027, and will provide further details on our Q4 call," CFO Anat Ashkenazi said on the post-earnings conference call. She added that roughly 65% of capex in Q3 went to servers and networking equipment with a useful life of six years, while the remainder went into data center infrastructure with a useful life of anywhere from seven to 40 years. Alphabet's negative free cash flow (FCF) swelled to $9.07 billion in the third quarter, impacted by the company's capex, a $5.2 billion cash payment following the conclusion of the appeal process of a European Commission fine from 2018, and a build-up of inventory for TPU system sales. So, that FCF number is not as bad as it looks — but still sub-optimal. Alphabet exited the quarter with $265.1 billion in cash and marketable securities and $125.1 billion in debt. Additionally, the company is on the hook for future purchase commitments of $924 billion, and pre-commencement leases and other obligations of $152 billion. Ashkenazi said, "These dollar amounts reflect the maximum contractual obligations; however, a number of these agreements have variable pricing and volume flexibility, which could result in lower spend." So, what do we think about the stock against that mostly lousy backdrop? With about $27 billion left in Alphabet's $40 billion at-the-market (ATM) equity offering authorization, we aren't interested in buying shares as management actively sells against us. That said, the stock is down nearly 30% from its all-time, intraday high of about $408 back in May. The valuation of about 20 times next 12-month earnings per share estimates is far from demanding, even if estimates come down a bit Thursday as analysts update their models. For now, our rating and price target are under review, as we huddle and figure out the appropriate course of action. The pressure should abate as the ATM program winds down. However, we still need operations to get back to at least meeting — and ideally exceeding — investor expectations if shares have any hope of reclaiming their former glory and making a run back to new highs.
