articles.title: FedEx's soft holiday-quarter outlook doesn't change our view on the stock
articles.text: FedEx on Wednesday night demonstrated that its transformation under CEO Raj Subramaniam is making progress, even amid higher fuel prices and a tight labor market for truck drivers. The company is controlling what it can control to become more profitable and stronger, enabling us to stay patient while all the moving pieces get sorted out. Revenue in the July-to-September quarter rose 12% year over year to $22.86 billion, beating the LSEG consensus of $22.42 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) increased 28% from a year earlier to $3.74, topping analyst expectations of $3.36, according to LSEG data. Adjusted operating margin came in at 5.24%, essentially in line with the 5.21% consensus. It represents modest year-over-year expansion. Shares fell more than 2% in extended trading to roughly $297 apiece. Combined with a 0.8% drop in Wednesday's regular session, the stock is set to give back almost all of the gains registered in the first two trading days of the week. Most of that advance came Tuesday, when shares rallied 2% in sympathy with parcel-delivery rival UPS after Big Brown reported better-than-expected results. As of Wednesday's close, FedEx is up 31% year to date, though it's down about 10% from its all-time closing high of $339.35 on Aug. 13. FDX YTD mountain FedEx's year-to-date stock performance. Bottom line Why aren't investors as enthusiastic about FedEx on Wednesday night as they were about UPS a day earlier? The simple answer is that the headline revenue and profit beats don't tell the whole story, though we're certainly glad both boxes were checked in the company's first official earnings report without its freight division, which was spun off in June as FedEx Freight . This also marks FedEx's first earnings report since adopting a December-ended fiscal year (previously May), adding another variable to interpreting the numbers. The sellers may be disappointed by FedEx's profit guidance for the October-to-December quarter, which is the peak season for these delivery giants. At the midpoint of its outlook for the final three months of the year, FedEx expects to earn $6.33 a share. That is below the FactSet consensus of $6.58. And while the company expects adjusted operating income to be up year over year, executives highlighted a few "transitory headwinds" that will weigh on results in the December quarter. Chief among them is higher rates for third-party transportation — dubbed "purchased transportation" — as the labor market for linehaul truck drivers has tightened. By geography, FedEx expects the international segment to see operating margin expansion in the holiday quarter, while the domestic business will see margins "down moderately" due to those higher purchased transportation costs and higher fuel expenses. Fuel surcharges help FedEx protect its bottom-line profits, but they also boost top-line revenue and squeeze margins (a dynamic we explained in June). A big part of our reason for owning the streamlined, freight-free FedEx is that Subramaniam is making the company more efficient and profitable. So why are we willing to look through the light EPS guide and these domestic margin pressures? For starters, Subramaniam has a track record of being conservative with guidance, so he deserves the benefit of the doubt again. As for the margins, executives said on multiple occasions that they expect the domestic operating margin to expand annually in 2027. Interim CFO Claude Russ said the company has both "operational and commercial levers" to pull next year to overcome some of these cost headwinds and ensure margin expansion. We also like that the company continues to make its delivery network more efficient through consolidation, part of what it calls its Network 2.0 plan. Subramaniam said Wednesday that nearly 65% of eligible parcel volume is flowing through about 630 Network 2.0-optimized stations. That's up from 45% and nearly 490 optimized stations at the end of June. Subramaniam said the company will tackle the large Los Angeles market, along with Charlotte and Oklahoma City, after the peak season concludes. "One hundred percent, we're convinced that we're going to improve our domestic margins in 2027 and beyond," Subramaniam said. Another sign that FedEx is controlling what it can: revenue in the September quarter grew across its key business-to-business verticals, including the data center buildout, and premium business-to-consumer parcels. And ground economy volume was down 4%, which COO Brie Carere noted was "intentional as we really lean into premium." This is part of FedEx's decision to move away from delivering low-margin packages to your doorstep for customers such as Amazon — something we fully support because it will enhance profitability over the long run. (For its part, UPS has embraced a similar strategy.) Finally, FedEx repurchased $2 billion of stock in the June-to-September period, a sizable step up from the guidance management provided in June. At the time, interim finance chief Russ said FedEx expected to repurchase about $1 billion through the remainder of calendar 2026. With the way the stock slumped from mid-June into late July — and then again from late August through September — we support the increased buyback activity. It's a positive sign of confidence that the management team believed the market wasn't fully valuing the shares. FedEx has $4.3 billion in buyback dry powder remaining. Something to watch with capital allocation is how FedEx monetizes its retained 19.9% stake in FedEx Freight . This came up on the earnings call, though nothing concrete was offered other than that it provides the company "meaningful optionality." Add it all up, and our reasons for starting a position in FedEx back in May remain intact. Though there are some challenges in the operating backdrop at the moment, we're confident in Subramaniam and team's ability to navigate through them. We're reiterating our buy-equivalent 1 rating and price target of $380. articles.title: Samsung Electronics third-quarter profit in line with estimates amid rising demand for AI memory chips
articles.text:
South Korean tech giant Samsung Electronics on Thursday reported third-quarter operating profit that is broadly in line with analysts' expectations, as demand for advanced memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications continued to grow.
Here are Samsung's third-quarter results compared with LSEG SmartEstimates, which are weighted toward forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate:
- Revenue: 195.25 trillion won vs. 195.79 trillion won expected
- Operating profit: 107.44 trillion won vs. 107.66 trillion won expected
Samsung's revenue rose 126.88% year-on-year and 13.85% from the previous quarter, while operating profit rose 783.11% from a year earlier.
During the third quarter, Samsung Electronics and five of its affiliates announced a combined $1 billion investment in KKR-backed Helix Digital Infrastructure. Samsung Electronics will invest $500 million, with the remaining amount coming from its affiliates.
Samsung has also announced a partnership with French AI startup Mistral AI to use AI technologies in its semiconductor operations, including chip design and manufacturing. The company also led Mistral's Series D funding round.

articles.title: Microsoft’s strong quarter backs up its stock rebound. Here's our new price target
articles.text: Shares of Microsoft edged higher Wednesday evening after the tech giant reported better-than-expected results across all key metrics and signaled that growth in its all-important Azure cloud computing business continues to accelerate. Revenue in the three months ended in September rose about 19% year over year to $92.28 billion, beating the LSEG consensus estimate of $90.69 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) totaled $4.92, up 32% from a year earlier, beating the $4.73 consensus, according to LSEG. Azure cloud revenue grew 48% year over year on a reported and constant-currency basis, beating FactSet consensus estimates of about 44% and 45%, respectively. MSFT 1Y mountain Microsoft 1-year stock performance Bottom line Earlier this year, Microsoft shares were down about 25%, trading in the mid-$300s on concerns that it had fallen behind in the AI race, that its seat-based subscription model was vulnerable to disruption, and that the company lacked innovation in its AI tools. But that all changed in July: Azure revenue growth accelerated; momentum in Copilot paid seats grew; and, perhaps most importantly, the company separated itself from the other major hyperscalers by spending within its means and not burning through all its cash flow to support its AI efforts. The stock gained roughly 51% from its summer low in late June through Wednesday's close. That rebound is likely to continue after another clean earnings report. Microsoft shares are up another 3% in after-hours trading, putting the stock in record-high territory. We'll see how it trades Thursday in what may be a tough day for tech following misses from Alphabet, ServiceNow , and Fortinet , but any dip will have nothing to do with its excellent quarter. To start, Azure revenue growth accelerated to 48% year over year, exceeding analyst expectations and management's guidance of about 45%. More precisely, Azure revenue totaled $33.17 billion in the quarter, up from $22.38 billion last year. Microsoft's disclosure of quarterly Azure cloud revenue is new, following changes to its reporting structure announced in September. Why we own it Microsoft is a core backbone of global productivity thanks to its Office 365 suite and hybrid cloud platform Azure. The company is also proving itself to be a key provider of AI tools, in part due to its large investment in OpenAI, the startup behind ChatGPT. We also like what it's doing in the video gaming industry as it looks to grow recurring revenue streams. Competitors : Amazon , Alphabet and Salesforce Weight in portfolio : 2.9% Most recent buy : Aug. 5, 2024 Initiated : Dec. 4, 2017 Past Microsoft quarters were held back by capacity constraints, leaving Azure revenue on the table. Similarly, Azure revenues were limited by the company allocating capacity to other opportunities, such as Copilot and internal R & D. But there has been a major emphasis on bringing capacity online faster to meet accelerating demand. Microsoft added 24 new data centers across five continents in the quarter. Notably, Azure revenue exceeded expectations despite Microsoft experiencing third-party capacity delays. These third-party delays are something we must monitor in the weeks and months ahead, as they could lead to more push-outs in AI spending. Still, Microsoft generated more revenue than expected due to gains in GPU efficiency, which allowed it to allocate additional capacity to customers while increasing revenue per token. This is a particularly notable development because it suggests each dollar of capital spending can support greater revenue generation and potentially higher returns on investment. We've been skeptics on Copilot, but it's clear this AI tool is gaining traction in the enterprise. Microsoft calls Copilot "the new OS [operating system] for work." On the earnings call, CEO Satya Nadella said that Copilot's daily users increased by 50% year over year, while user satisfaction improved by nearly 20% quarter over quarter to an all-time high. We didn't hear anything new regarding paid seats, but the company sounded upbeat about its adoption. Finally, we appreciate Microsoft's unwillingness to wreck its balance sheet and burn through all its cash flow. Capital expenditures (including finance leases) were $45.2 billion, up modestly from $41 billion in the prior quarter and $34.9 billion in the prior year. But Microsoft's spending was much lower than the $51 billion analysts had forecasted and the $50 billion projected by management. Although some of the differences between actual spending and management's guidance were due to those delays in third-party capacity deliveries — meaning some of that spending will be pushed into future quarters — free cash flow remains firmly in positive territory. This financial discipline allows the company to continue investing aggressively in AI while also returning capital to shareholders, including $2.9 billion in share repurchases during the quarter. That amount may seem trivial, but it's noteworthy in a year when Alphabet and Meta issued equity to fund their AI investments, diluting existing shareholders. Microsoft's positive free cash flow suggests the business doesn't have any immediate cash needs. However, CFO Amy Hood acknowledged that the company "will access additional sources of funding when we believe it is attractive to do so." We do not want Microsoft to follow Meta and Alphabet's lead with equity offerings, so this is something to be mindful of in the future. Looking ahead, the company's revenue outlook for the current quarter was slightly better than expected, driven by continued upside in Azure despite third-party capacity constraints. Azure revenue is expected to grow about 49%-50% in constant currency, above analyst forecasts of about 46% growth, according to FactSet. It all adds up to a great quarter, solid guidance, and continued financial discipline that could make this stock one of the more attractive hyperscalers in the market. We are increasing our price target to $580 from $550 and maintaining our 2 rating. Guidance Microsoft's quarterly outlook offered slight upside. The company guided revenue from its Agents and Infra segment to $80.1 billion to $80.7 billion, which is above the FactSet consensus of $79.6 billion. In Devices and Consumer, revenue is expected to be $15.9 billion to $16.4 billion, which is roughly in line with the consensus estimate of $16.29 billion, according to FactSet. This means Microsoft forecasts total company revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion, above the Street's $95.6 billion. In terms of capex, Microsoft plans to spend over $50 billion in the second quarter and $170 billion over the calendar year. The full-year figure is slightly lower than the $175 billion previously expected, with the difference attributable to capacity delays at third parties — something to keep an eye on for the semiconductor and power infrastructure food chain. articles.title: What investors need to know about Alphabet's stock-busting earnings report
articles.text: Wall Street is seeing a major potential shift in Google's core advertising business as artificial intelligence replaces traditional internet searching and the long-established ways in which it is monetized. Shares of Alphabet , Google's parent company, tanked after Wednesday's third-quarter earnings report, falling close to 10% in after-hours trading. Revenues for its services division, which is mostly from ads, came in at $96.3 billion for the quarter, more than $2 billion shy of analysts' expectations at $98.5 billion, as cited by the Wall Street Journal . GOOGL 5D mountain Alphabet 5 day The Street thinks investors need to be more cautious with Google now that a key revenue driver for the business is being called into question. "Given the abrupt deceleration in digital advertising revenue, investors should be more cautious as that trend may continue going forward," Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, told CNBC. "The burden of proof is now on Google that they are not in a permanent decline due to the shift [toward] people using AI chat instead of search." Analysts are questioning whether the advertising revenues miss could be the start of a larger trend in behavioral changes among internet users. "The world of search is shifting because of the fact that so many people are now doing the kinds of things they would traditionally do through Google, through the chatbots," Bob O'Donnell, founder of TECHnalysis Research, said. "Clearly, I think we're starting to see changes in habits, and so they will take time to really [have an] impact. But when they start to change, that theoretically is going to be a big deal." On Wednesday evening's earnings call, analysts wanted to know how ads were going to figure into AI queries versus traditional internet searches in the future. "[There was] obviously some deceleration in search growth," Doug Anmuth, head of internet equity research at JPMorgan, said. "Can you just help us understand the disconnect there? Is it simply that you haven't been showing as many ads basically in AI overviews in AI mode and that's now becoming a bigger percentage of the overall queries?" Google executives on the call acknowledged the dip and said they were running experiments to improve results. "The strong growth in AI mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we are seeing in AI mode," Philipp Schindler, Google's chief business officer, said. "To be clear, we feel very good about our trajectory here. Our ad experiments have shown promising results, and we're now scaling ads within … AI mode to more users and more queries."

articles.title: Inside India newsletter: New Delhi approves $22 billion in military spending amid China border tensions
articles.text:
Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.
Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.
India, the world's fifth-largest military spender, shares a contentious relationship with two of its nuclear-armed neighbors — China and Pakistan. Last year, New Delhi carried out military strikes against alleged terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan, and last week an Indian official confirmed some border clashes with China.
As tensions at its borders simmer, India this week announced plans to spend billions of dollars on procuring modern warfare equipment. From whom will it get the goods?
Any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team.
The big story
The world's second-largest arms importer, India, is pouring billions of dollars into modernizing its military as it seeks to counter the technological advancements of neighboring China, with whom it shares an uneasy peace.
Last week, an Indian military official said that confrontations with Chinese soldiers were ongoing across several locations along the country's north-eastern border.
Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor, the director general of a division of India's central armed forces, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, also called China the "biggest adversary" and urged for modernization of defense equipment. "It will be difficult to compete with China using traditional methods," Kapoor said.
Following Kapoor's comments, India approved spending 2.12 trillion rupees ($22 billion) to modernize its defense equipment on Monday. The country plans to spend on long-range kamikaze drones, surveillance and strike systems, counter-drone technologies, short-range air defense, artillery, helicopters and naval platforms.
Experts told CNBC that New Delhi increasingly views Beijing as a threat, especially given the Sino-Pakistan military ties, and the latest purchases were aimed at bridging the technological gap with China.
A spokesperson for India's foreign ministry said on Friday that "the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns." Beijing responded, saying it "strictly abides by the relevant agreements and common understandings reached between the two countries."
India's military policies are largely driven by its long-standing conflict with Pakistan, and an "increasing perception of China as a threat," Pieter Wezeman, senior researcher at the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, told CNBC.
According to a SIPRI report earlier this year, 61% of Chinese arms exports were supplied to Pakistan between 2021 and 2025.
India's latest weapons purchases will involve importing components and technology from South Korea for the artillery, engines and avionics from France for the helicopters, and drones from the U.S. and Israel, Wezeman said.
Collaboration with Russia and Japan could also be on the cards, given India's need for a technological upgrade.
Foreign partnerships
Since April, India has greenlighted military spending totaling 3.7 trillion rupees, which is more than 50% of the 6.73 trillion rupee worth of approvals — a 10-year high — in the financial year ended March 2026, Citi said in a report on Tuesday.
While New Delhi has said it plans to procure 82% of the defense equipment from local industries, foreign companies are likely to play a key role in providing technology crucial for military modernization.
Foreign partnerships remain important for technologies that India does not yet produce independently, Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo, told CNBC. India relies on imported technologies for specialized components such as aircraft engines, propulsion systems, sensors and electronic subsystems, he explained.
"American, Israeli, and Russian defense manufacturers are likely to find substantial opportunities in India's expanding defense market," through joint ventures, co-production and technology partnerships with Indian companies, Chaturvedi said.
India was the world's second-largest importer of major arms in 2021–25 with an 8.2% share of total global imports, even as its reliance on overseas suppliers dropped by 4% during the same time due to growing local design and production abilities, according to SIPRI.
New Delhi is also the world's fifth-largest military spender, with $92 billion, but this is less than 30% of Chinese military expenditure and around a 10th of America's, Wezeman of SIPRI pointed out.
India faces some practical challenges in matching China's scale of military modernization, but the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have shown that mass-produced systems like drones can address asymmetry, Collin Koh Swee Lean, a senior fellow at Singapore's Nanyang Technological University, said.
Need to know

Major Indian online investment platforms are unlocking access to U.S. stocks for millions of retail investors eager to diversify into global assets as the country's markets continue to underperform.
Meta- and Google-backed Jio Platforms' shares soar over 21% on trading debut after record IPO
Jio Platforms' shares rose 21.4% on their trading debut Wednesday after a record initial public offering that was lapped up by retail as well as institutional investors.

articles.title: As Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning business
articles.text:
Waymo is dominant in the U.S. and expanding overseas, but it remains immaterial in terms of revenue to parent Alphabet, which is pouring cash into its growth.
In Alphabet's third-quarter earnings report on Wednesday, the company said its Other Bets segment, which includes Waymo, generated $372 million in revenue, up 8% from a year earlier, and accounting for just 0.3% of total sales.
That revenue comes at a steep price. Operating loss in the Other Bets segment widened to $2.05 billion during the quarter from $1.43 billion a year ago. The unit also houses drug design research business Isomorphic, which is using Google's Gemini 4 Argon AI models.
CEO Sundar Pichai touted Waymo's expansion toward the end of his introductory remarks on the earnings call. The company has a commanding lead in the U.S. robotaxi market, where it faces emerging competition from Amazon's Zoox and Tesla. Waymo said in August that it plans to roll out robotaxi rides in Germany in 2027, marking its third international market and first in the EU.
"Waymo now operates in 15 major U.S. cities and just recently opened up service to the public in San Antonio, San Diego and Tampa with planned expansions into Canada, Germany, Singapore and Spain," Pichai said on the call.
Waymo's steepest competition on the global stage comes from Baidu's Apollo Go, which is based in China.
For years, Alphabet was able to operate Waymo as a side project while its core online ads business racked up tens of billions of dollars in annual profit and threw off mounds of cash. But with the company now investing heavily in artificial intelligence, free cash flow has turned negative and Wall Street has shown signs of concern.
Alphabet reported an earnings and revenue miss on Wednesday, sending the stock down almost 10% in extended trading. The company maintained its full-year capital expenditures forecast at between $195 billion and $205 billion, largely for AI infrastructure, and reported negative free cash flow of over $9 billion for the quarter.
Earlier this month, Waymo announced that it had closed a $5 billion term loan, its first debt financing. In February, the robotaxi business announced that it had raised $16 billion at a $126 billion valuation in a funding round led by Alphabet that included support from Andreessen Horowitz, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins and others.
Last week Waymo started offering driverless rides to and from the Las Vegas airport, after previously announcing airport service in five other cities, including San Francisco and Phoenix.
"Waymo is on a great trajectory," Pichai said on Wednesday. "We have now driven more than 300 million fully autonomous miles."
Tesla says on its website that driverless vehicles in its Robotaxi network have completed about 3.8 million miles "unsupervised," or without a human driver at the wheel. CEO Elon Musk said on the company's earnings call last week that the Robotaxi business should become a "meaningful" revenue contributor by the second half of 2027.

articles.title: One passport isn’t enough for some wealthy Chinese. Here’s where they’re looking next
articles.text:
For some wealthy Chinese, securing a foreign passport is becoming the ultimate trade-off: giving up their Chinese citizenship.
Wealth advisors say a growing number of affluent Chinese are considering renouncing their nationality as Beijing intensifies scrutiny of offshore wealth, with concerns over taxes, geopolitical uncertainty and greater international mobility driving their interest in alternative passports.
China does not recognize dual nationality, meaning Chinese nationals seeking to acquire foreign citizenship must renounce their passports.
"We have had some clients who are willing to give up their Chinese citizenship to hold multiple passports," said Armand Arton, CEO of immigration migration consultancy Arton Capital, who added that the choice of passports depends on their lifestyle and business needs.
Meanwhile, Ryan Lin, director at Singapore-based legal firm Bayfront Law, said he has seen an increase in wealthy Chinese considering renouncing their nationality since July.
That month, Beijing introduced new measures targeting offshore trusts, with certain incomes and transactions potentially subject to a 20% tax. The changes have prompted some families to reassess how they hold and transfer assets overseas.
Previously, clients would discuss the possibility of giving up their citizenship. Now, more are expressing concrete intentions to do so, Lin told CNBC.
Manish Tibrewal, co-founder of multi-family office Farro Capital, also reported growing interest in foreign passports.
The wealth advisory firm is helping some Chinese families pursue Caribbean citizenship alongside Singapore permanent residency, with the longer-term possibility of obtaining Singapore citizenship, subject to government approval.
Tibrewal said the number of Chinese families actively exploring alternative citizenship options since July far exceeds those who have completed the process last year.
Inquiries from Chinese clients have risen 33% since July, investment migration firm Savory & Partners said, while Global Citizen Solutions reported an increase of nearly 40% compared with the same period last year.
Both firms specialize in investment migration, which helps wealthy individuals obtain foreign residency or citizenship, often through qualifying investments in their destination countries.
Renouncing Chinese citizenship does not automatically erase existing tax liabilities though.
Individuals could remain liable for taxes on historical gains, depending on how their wealth was structured, even after giving up their nationality, but a genuine change in citizenship and residency could affect future obligations, experts said.
For many wealthy Chinese, relinquishing their nationality remains a significant sacrifice, particularly for those whose businesses and fortunes are tied to the mainland.
Lin said those most willing to take that step generally have few remaining business links to China, with much of their wealth and operations already based offshore.
So where are they looking to move?
Caribbean: quicker route to citizenship
For wealthy Chinese seeking an alternative passport rather than merely overseas residency, the Caribbean has emerged as a popular choice.
Countries such as Antigua and Barbuda offer citizenship-by-investment programs that allow eligible applicants to obtain nationality through qualifying investments or contributions.
Tibrewal said Caribbean citizenship can potentially be secured within six months, making it considerably faster than pathways in Europe or the United States, where residency requirements often precede naturalization.
Arton said the appeal is less about permanently relocating and more about greater flexibility to travel and establish an international base.
Global Citizen Solutions said the Caribbean recorded the strongest growth in Chinese inquiries among the destinations it tracked this year.
Europe: Portugal, Italy and Hungary
European countries are also attracting interest, although many offer residency pathways rather than immediate citizenship.
"For Chinese HNWIs who are not willing to give up their citizenship, a portfolio of residencies or long-term visas is a more appealing option," Arton said.
Portugal remains popular through its golden visa program, which offers residency through qualifying investments and a potential longer-term route to citizenship.
Arton also added that Italy is attracting wealthy families through its favorable tax arrangements for qualifying new residents, international schools and financial services infrastructure.
Hungary is another emerging destination, offering long-term residency through qualifying investments starting at 250,000 euros ($290,000).
“Hungary is the one that surprises people,” according to Global Citizen Solutions. “As the larger European golden visa routes have closed or become more expensive, Hungary offers residency in the Schengen area through a regulated fund investment.”
Singapore: established Asian hub
Singapore remains attractive to wealthy Chinese because of its political stability, established wealth management industry, international schools and proximity to mainland China.
Some families are pursuing Singapore permanent residency as part of longer-term citizenship plans, although naturalization is neither automatic nor guaranteed.
Tibrewal said his firm was assisting some clients with plans involving Caribbean citizenship and Singapore residency, with Singapore citizenship a possible longer-term objective.
Australia, Malaysia and other emerging destinations
Australia is another popular option, particularly for families prioritizing education and quality of life.
Malaysia is also gaining attention, especially Kuala Lumpur and Penang, where lower living costs, Chinese-speaking communities and international schools appeal to families, said the migration consultancies.
"We also see interest beyond the obvious hubs in Asia, including Penang and Thailand's long-term resident visa, from families who value lifestyle and lower costs," said Global Citizen Solutions.
Meanwhile, Argentina and parts of Eastern Europe are emerging as alternative destinations for those seeking to diversify their international residency options.
Arton Capital identified Argentina as a market worth watching, while Savory & Partners highlighted growing interest in Serbia, North Macedonia and Bulgaria.
Advisors caution that interest in overseas citizenship does not necessarily translate into completed renunciations or physical relocations.
"It's important to recognize that exploring overseas residency, building a passport portfolio, and relocating an entire family are very different decisions," Arton said.

articles.title: Jim Cramer sees major implications from SK Hynix's home-run quarter
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Wednesday that SK Hynix's blockbuster earnings proved artificial intelligence stocks can still rally in a market that has grown increasingly skeptical of the massive data center build-out.
The South Korean memory giant's New York-listed shares surged more than 13% after it delivered better-than-expected results and an upbeat outlook. The report lifted other chipmakers, with Micron jumping almost 6%, Arm advancing 4% and AMD rising 3%. The rally stood out at a time when even strong earnings haven't been enough to lift some AI-related stocks, as investors question whether the enormous spending on data centers will pay off.
"SK Hynix put on a clinic last night about how you can get your stock to move higher," the "Mad Money" host said.
Cramer identified several factors that helped SK Hynix overcome Wall Street's skepticism, starting with its low valuation. The company trades at just four times 2027 earnings, reflecting doubts about whether the memory boom can last. That left room for the stock to rally if results exceeded expectations.
And SK Hynix delivered. Revenue topped estimates by roughly 6%, with gross margins of 85.7%. The company also projected shipment growth in the mid-20% range this quarter, up from 10% in the third quarter.
"Accelerating growth is like catnip to growth investors – it lets their imagination run wild about how good things could get," Cramer said.
Perhaps most importantly, SK Hynix indicated that its production was effectively sold out through 2029, supported by long-term customer agreements. Cramer said the outlook demonstrated just how strong demand remains for memory chips used in AI data centers.
He highlighted the company's plans to invest heavily in additional manufacturing equipment. Historically, expanding production has raised fears of oversupply and falling memory prices. "This time, demand is so strong that Hynix knows that more supply won't sate the market," Cramer said. "That shows a level of confidence that is extraordinary."
The company also outlined substantial shareholder returns through dividends and stock buybacks, giving investors another reason to be optimistic.
For Cramer, the combination of a low valuation, strong earnings, accelerating growth, sustained demand and shareholder returns offered a blueprint for how AI-related companies can win over investors in a challenging market.
"If you get through that gauntlet, then this market says you have a winner," he said.
Cramer said the results also bode well for Micron, which is a holding in Cramer's Charitable Trust, the portfolio run by CNBC's Investing Club. He noted that Micron trades at a low multiple and has similar long-term customer agreements. There's also potential, he said, for the chipmaker to deploy its growing cash pile toward a significant buyback when CHIPS Act funding restrictions ease on Dec. 9.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says these tech giants can weather market turbulence
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Wednesday that a handful of technology giants have become so powerful that their influence extends far beyond their stock prices.
The "Mad Money" host likened them to "nation states," pointing to their dominant competitive positions, ability to generate substantial profits and willingness to aggressively invest in emerging technologies. Cramer identified Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI as companies fitting that description.
"Their heft is so extraordinary that 'Mad Money' cannot go without covering them," he said.
Cramer's Charitable Trust, the portfolio run by CNBC's Investing Club, owns shares of Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft and Nvidia.
Still, even these giants aren't immune to broader market forces. Cramer compared them to aircraft carriers — better equipped to withstand turbulent conditions than smaller vessels, but still vulnerable to powerful economic currents.
Those pressures were evident Wednesday as oil prices climbed with renewed concerns about the conflict with Iran, while Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh warned that inflation remained elevated, leaving the possibility of further rate hikes on the table.
"I listened and I didn't hear anything that could derail the biggest companies," Cramer said.
Microsoft's latest earnings offered a case in point. Shares climbed 4% in extended trading after the software giant topped earnings and revenue expectations. Revenue rose 19%, while its Azure cloud business grew 48%, accelerating from 42% in the prior quarter and exceeding expectations. Microsoft also demonstrated spending discipline, with capital expenditures and finance leases of $45.2 billion coming in below Wall Street's forecasts despite continued investment in AI infrastructure.
"This was the winner from tonight's two big Magnificent 7 reports," he said, while cautioning that Microsoft's conference call and guidance could still change investors' assessment.
Alphabet's results, meanwhile, demonstrated that even dominant technology companies face risks. Shares slumped 7% after the Google parent missed earnings and revenue expectations. Although revenue grew nearly 25% and Google Cloud sales more than doubled, its core Search business fell short of estimates, raising fresh concerns about AI's impact on Google's advertising business. Free cash flow was also negative $9.1 billion.
"Tonight, we saw why you ignore these stocks at your own peril," he concluded. "We saw nothing that shocked us. Nothing that enraged us. Alphabet's going to catch a downgrade or two, search could really be hurting. But Microsoft? It's justifying its monster move off the bottom back at the end of June earlier this year."

articles.title: Weil, Gotshal & Manges, longtime Wall Street law firm, plans wind down
articles.text:
A management committee of Weil, Gotshal & Manges, the long-time Wall Street law firm, has recommended that its partners wind down operations, the firm said Wednesday.
The recommendation came after an exodus of partners and the reported end, days ago, of talks with Willkie Farr & Gallagher about a potential merger.
Weil, which has about 1,200 lawyers, in 2025 reportedly had more than $2 billion in revenue across multi-national operations.
"For more than 90 years, Weil, Gotshal & Manges has had the privilege of advising clients on some of their most consequential matters," the firm said in a statement to CNBC.
"Following a careful review of strategic alternatives, the Firm's Management Committee has recommended to the partnership that the Firm pursue an orderly wind-down," the firm said. "The partners are expected to vote in the coming days."
Weil said that during the wind-down process in coming months, the "firm will continue serving clients with the dedication and excellence that have defined it since its founding and will remain committed to supporting its colleagues."
Over the years, Weil had been involved in major bankruptcy filings, including for Lehman Brothers, General Motors and Enron.

articles.title: Hands-on with Apple's first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optional
articles.text:
Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop models on Wednesday at an event in Los Angeles.
These new MacBooks, called MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display, are still Apple MacBooks. They run MacOS, not iPadOS or iOS, the iPhone's operating system.
Here's the good news for anyone who is worried about the new user interface: You don't have to use it. Touch is entirely optional.
CNBC briefly tested both the 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBooks at the event.
Users can still primarily or entirely use the device's trackpad and keyboard, and there are few visual updates. MacOS still looks largely the same as it used to.
There have been a few user interface updates. For example, the red button on the top left of a window expands when you touch it to make it easier to click. Apple says that third-party developers like Microsoft and Adobe can and will update their apps to expand buttons and other touch targets to be larger. I think that touch will be particularly useful to scroll through websites or documents while lying down.
But even software that hasn't been explicitly updated for the new computer will support touch. Apple says that behind the scenes, its software converts every touch tap into a traditional click. So any button that can be clicked can also be touched.
Using the laptop with your finger feels good, but it won't change the way most people use their laptops. It could be useful for iPhone app developers, who can now test the way their apps work on their Mac. An accessibility feature allows users to pinch to zoom on any part of the user interface.
Apple said on Wednesday that it had used an oleophobic coating on its screens to resist fingerprints. It appears to work. I didn't notice marks on the screen when I used the touch features.
Apple is also, in addition to the touch feature, marketing these laptops as having a superior display, thanks to its new tandem OLED technology that offers deeper blacks and higher contrast.
While photos and other art looked great on the screen, it's not a night-and-day difference from past Apple laptops. A lot of the improvements are aimed at creators who need accurate colors for photo and video editing.
Instead of the notch at the top of previous MacBooks, where Apple hides its cameras, the new MacBooks have a hole-punch cutout in the display, like recent iPhones. Apple's Dynamic Island feature — new to the MacBook — expands to show live activities and Siri.
Apple made a big deal about the laptop's new hinge, which is meant to keep the screen from shaking when you touch it. For example, if you tap the screen on a video call, your camera won't shake as much. But the hinge feels largely the same as Apple's previous MacBook Pros.
There is one new feature that is immediately noticeable and tells people you bought the latest, greatest, and most expensive Apple laptop. (The smaller 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and the bigger one costs at least $3,399.) The Apple logo on the lid now lights up when the computer is on. It's the first Apple laptop that supports it since the 2017 MacBook Air.
The light-up logo drew a cheer from analysts and influencers in attendance when it was announced on Wednesday.

articles.title: Nasdaq-100 futures dip as Alphabet shares sell off after earnings report: Live updates
articles.text:
U.S. equity futures dipped late Wednesday as investors digest the latest round of hyperscaler earnings.
Nasdaq-100 futures lost 1.2%. S&P 500 futures declined 0.5%.
In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 added over 0.58% while the Topix was flat. The Kospi rose 0.11% at open, while the small-cap Kosdaq fell 0.97%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.51% higher.
In after-hours trading, Microsoft advanced 3% after growth in the software giant's Azure cloud infrastructure business helped it post beats on the top and bottom lines in the fiscal first quarter, per LSEG.
That contrasts sharply with Alphabet's 9% slide after adjusted earnings per share and revenue missed expectations in the third quarter, and the company posted negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion. The company kept its full-year capital expenditures forecast at $195 billion to $205 billion.
The results come at a time when the artificial intelligence trade is in focus. AI stocks, such as the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM), have been through a rough patch for most of October, only to perk up in recent days.
Chips helped lift the broader market to a winning regular session on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 rising for a third straight day as Micron Technology jumped almost 6% and Broadcom added more than 2%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite also eked out a gain, advancing 0.3%.
Earlier Wednesday, the Federal Reserve decided to hold steady on rates, leaving the central bank's benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75% and 4%. The decision to hold was widely expected as the Federal Open Market Committee issued a quarter-percentage-point hike in September.
This time, central bank policymakers pointed out that inflation "remains elevated," but also said that it was awaiting the "accumulation of more information" before it takes further steps.
The Fed's decision "can be interpreted as mildly dovish at the margin, but we think it is better viewed as an expression of patience rather than a shift away from a tightening bias," said Daniel Siluk, head of global short duration and liquidity at Janus Henderson Investors. "The door remains open to further tightening, but the Committee appears willing to wait for incoming data to validate the need for additional action."
Traders will get further insight into the economy on Thursday, when the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index report for September comes out. The PCE is a preferred inflation gauge for the Federal Reserve. The first reading of third-quarter GDP and weekly jobless claims are also due.
On the earnings front, all eyes will be on quarterly reports from Caterpillar and Eli Lilly in the morning, followed by Amazon and Intel after the market close.

articles.title: Wall Street looks past Fed pause to tech earnings and AI rebound
articles.text: So much for Fed fireworks. It's time to get back to business. Markets shrugged at the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady on Wednesday. More significant than the Fed's decision or Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference were tech earnings from Microsoft and Alphabet , and a more muted capex outlook from Oracle — the latter a positive catalyst for the stock and the AI trade more broadly. The fact that stocks barely reacted to the Fed could be viewed as a positive. The Fed's decision was widely telegraphed. And Warsh reiterated that he doesn't believe in forward guidance, "absent a crisis." He held true to form in his press conference, which explains why volatility didn't spike as he spoke. The market now shifts back to fundamentals — namely third quarter earnings — along with the outlook for the AI trade. On those fronts, investors may be getting more comfortable after a bout of volatility triggered by a sharp increase in spreads on neocloud debt. "When you have 36% of the S & P 500 reporting in a single week, 44% of the market cap of the S & P 500 reporting in one week, you tend to have most of everything else take a back seat," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. "The market is focusing on earnings, and thus far the scorecard looks very good," Hogan said. Tech stocks are rebounding with neoclouds in particular surging more than 16% this week, as shown through the Roundhill Neocloud ETF . Semiconductors are also higher with the iShares Semiconductor ETF climbing more than 7% this week. That revival comes after South Korea memory giant SK Hynix posted record quarterly profit overnight, and after Anthropic filed its S-1 registration statement on Monday to go public. Investors are in the middle of the busiest week of earnings, with 163 S & P 500 companies set to report results. Results from Alphabet and Microsoft were mixed with investors reacting favorably to Microsoft while Alphabet slid after-hours on prospects for higher capex in 2027 . Amazon.com is the next big one, posting earnings Thursday. Companies are beating forecasts at a decent rate, albeit with a slowdown. The S & P 500 is on track to post a fourth straight quarter of above-25% earnings growth, but revenues are coming in only 1.7% ahead of consensus forecasts, down from an average 3.8% beat in the second quarter, according to economist and strategist Ed Yardeni. Earnings have topped estimates by 6.5%, down from more than 8% in the first and second quarters, which both "excluded mark-to-market gains and a tax reversal," he notes. One positive is that margins are improving, both in tech and beyond. As of October 23, the S & P 500's forward profit margin forecast was at a record high 16.8%, up 1.4 percentage points year-to-date, Yardeni pointed out in a note. It's not just a Magnificent 7 story. The forward profit margin for the S & P 493 collectively is up "an impressive" 2.6 percentage points to 14.6% this year, he added. To be sure, a backdrop of higher yields and higher oil could remain a hindrance for the market. And the path for interest rates remain higher, with fed funds futures continuing to price in a quarter-point hike at the conclusion of the Dec. 9 Fed meeting, putting it in the range of 4.00% to 4.25%. The war with Iran remains an overhang. Renewed hostilities, potentially after the midterms, could send oil prices soaring again and derail a market rally. The political outcome also matters. A Democrat sweep of the House and Senate would have more market implications than a split Congress with Republicans retaining control of the Senate. While AI stocks have rebounded a bit, some investors remain cautious, arguing for diversification from the tech-heavy S & P 500. That strategy has paid off this year with Invesco S & P 500 equal weight ETF up more than 13%. Jeffrey Gundlach, CEO-CIO of DoubleLine Capital, told CNBC on Wednesday that he favors a 30% allocation to equities with a focus on the equal-weight S & P 500. "I don't like the cap-weighted S & P," he said. "I don't want all this exposure to the epicenter of the blast radius of the AI problems or developing problems." Some strategists remain bullish on equities broadly, and see more value in fixed income as yields remain elevated. "While more Fed hikes remain in store in the coming months, we think the current backdrop remains favorable," said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, global head of equities at UBS Chief Investment Office in a note ahead of the Fed meeting. "We do not believe a measured tightening cycle will derail the US economy, and investors should maintain diversified equity exposure and use the rise in yields to add selectively to quality bonds," Hoffmann-Burchardi added.

articles.title: Anthropic’s public benefit structure creates unusual risks for IPO investors
articles.text:
Anthropic's structure as a public benefit corporation (PBC) raises critical questions for investors ahead of the AI lab's blockbuster IPO.
Anthropic aims to go public at a valuation of $1.5 trillion or more, making it the first major frontier lab to test public markets' appetite for AI – at a potentially rich valuation. The PBC wrapper adds another wrinkle, requiring Anthropic to balance a mandate for public benefit with standard fiduciary responsibilities as a publicly traded corporation.
Anthropic's goal, according to its S-1 filing, is "to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity."
Other companies operate as PBCs or under similar structures. Warby Parker is a PBC. Privately held Patagonia is registered as similar Benefit Corp. in California. When Google went public in 2004, its informal motto was "don't be evil," which it included in its IPO prospectus and corporate code of conduct, though Google is not a PBC.
Anthropic has long pitched itself as the responsible AI firm and has taken measures to police its own conduct. In 2023, Anthropic set up a "long-term benefit trust" to oversee its business practices. The company also established a "public benefit fund" with about 847 million shares of Class N stock, or roughly 5% of its fully diluted shares as of June 30.
Seven co-founders, including Dario Amodei, have special voting power through a single Class F share equal to 50.1% of total voting power over matters brought to a shareholder vote. Anthropic said in its filing that it believes those seven are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission."
Anthropic gave itself a long leash to act as it sees fit. Operating as a PBC "gives our board of directors the necessary latitude to balance the pecuniary interests of our stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and the specific public benefit purpose that we promote," the company said in its S-1.
'Good luck'
Legal experts say that Anthropic's PBC structure could create tension in how it operates.
"The obligation of directors is to balance achievement of [public] purpose with achievement of profit, and if you ask me what that means – 'to balance' – I would say, 'Good luck,'" said Lawrence Hamermesh, a Delaware corporate law attorney with decades of experience in PBC law.
PBC law is ambiguous on a key word, "balance," he adds, pointing out that there's no fundamental criterion to distinguish when one interest takes precedence over the other.
"It's hard enough in the ordinary case to win a damages claim against directors for having screwed up and having cost the company some money," he said. "It's doubly hard to do so in a public benefit corporation where you also have this defense that, 'Hey, I was doing it to promote our stated public benefit.'"
How Anthropic handles AI safety is a key risk. Anthropic has been at the forefront in sounding alarms about rapidly advancing AI, outlining legions of risks in its S-1. The company has restricted access to some models it deems too dangerous to be released widely in public. That practice could continue, even if it comes at a cost to revenue and profit growth.
Anthropic will also have to balance its PBC mandates with shareholder interests as it continues to raise capital. The company has multiple share classes with varying degrees of control, shareholder, and voting rights. Investors typically charge more for capital in situations that dilute their control from one-share/one vote, points out John Coates, professor of law and economics at Harvard Law School.
"If the company needs to continue to raise capital over the foreseeable future, as seems to be true of Anthropic, the company will know they need to pay attention to investors' interests for much of that future," he said in an email to CNBC. The PBC structure "adds another dimension of uncertainty about how this investment may play out."
Wall Street's take
Analysts say investors shouldn't gloss over the PBC structure.
"It's interesting to read it right up front in an S-1," Gil Luria, head of technology research at DA Davidson, said. "There's a quote about [how the] goal is for the stock not to trade at higher than the value of the company. Then they talk about things that they do that are not profit-maximizing, like promising never to have ads in Claude … So they led with this, and it's important."
Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney said in a Monday note that Anthropic's PBC status will also limit shareholders' power over the operations of the company.
"Governance limits shareholder influence: as a public benefit corporation, the board must weigh its mission alongside returns, an independent trust elects a majority of directors, and the co-founders hold 50.1% of the vote," he said.
Granted, Anthropic could alter or scrap its PBC status, and there's precedent for doing so. Shoe-maker-turned-AI-company Allbirds, for instance, dropped its PBC designation as part of a restructuring in June.
The industrial structure of the AI sector is not settled, moreover, so investors should be prepared for further changes as the technology progresses. Large-scale mergers and innovative public-private partnerships have been floated by some of the industry's top executives, and U.S. authorities are considering ways to audit the technology and implement development standards.
"We are dealing with this issue today," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNBC last week. "This is an issue of the moment."

articles.title: Here are five key takeaways from the Fed rate decision and Warsh news conference
articles.text:
The Federal Reserve voted Wednesday to hold its benchmark interest rate steady. At the press conference that followed, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh disclosed some of his thinking about where the U.S. economy stands, and how that affects monetary policy. But for Fed wonks, the big news may have been Warsh's disclosure of some procedural changes ahead.
Here are five key takeaways:
- No surprises: Markets had been widely expecting the Fed to hold, and it did just that. In explaining its decision, the Federal Open Market Committee emphasized a patient approach, saying, "The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal."
- Well, one surprise: If there was one eyebrow-raising moment from the afternoon, it was Warsh's disclosure of changes in how the FOMC will meet. In 2027, the committee will still meet eight times, but one of the meetings will not entail a vote on interest rates, or include a post-meeting statement. The "strategy" meetings will increase to two the next year, leaving just six opportunities to adjust rates — outside of emergency meetings.
- OK, two surprises: The FOMC vote to hold policy where it stands was widely expected. Dissent from multiple members also came as no shock. But one of the "no" votes coming from Governor Lisa Cook was a stunner. Governors rarely dissent from rate votes, and Cook hasn't done so at all since taking her seat in 2022. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack also opposed the decision. Both likely will provide statements explaining their votes before the end of the week.
- The AI impact: Warsh took the opportunity to talk about the impact artificial intelligence is having on economic growth, essentially saying that it was just one of several factors driving an expansion that he said was running strong.
- More musical chairs: The September meeting featured a shortened post-meeting news conference — cut from the usual 45 minutes or so down to half an hour, about the time of Wednesday's event. Moreover, reporters have been limited to a single question, a switch from prior practices when media members would take a two-for-one approach. Finally, Warsh has changed the seating in the room, going from a largely arbitrary approach — with representatives of larger outfits up front — to alphabetical order last month. This month featured reverse alphabetical order, keeping the bearers of the microphone on their toes.
What they're saying:
"The Fed is leaning into patience. It seems they prefer to wait for more information on the appropriate level of rates, as uncertainty reigns supreme in light of recent geopolitical developments." —Phil Camporeale, chief investment strategist, JPMorgan Wealth Management.
"The Fed has time on its side ... But the direction of travel remains clear. The Fed is still taking back some of last year's rate cuts, and the two dissents underline that tightening bias. We expect a hike in December and another in early 2027." — Seema Shah, chief global strategist, Principal Asset Management.
"We hesitate to characterize his communication as particularly dovish or hawkish ... The bottom line is that the Fed policy reaction is not a black-and-white, binary thing ... The market has adjusted to Warsh's communication style, but there might be a ways to go before they are fully on the same page." — Thomas Simons, chief U.S. economist, Jefferies.

articles.title: Tiền thưởng cho nhà vô địch Olympia đã thay đổi ra sao sau 26 năm?
articles.text:
Tiền thưởng cho nhà vô địch Olympia đã thay đổi ra sao sau 26 năm?
Phần thưởng dành cho quán quân Đường Lên Đỉnh Olympia đã trải qua 2 lần điều chỉnh.
- 29-10-2026Dàn MC 4 điểm cầu Chung kết Olympia 2026 lộ diện: 3/4 gương mặt lần đầu xuất hiện!
- 28-10-2026Cuộc sống hiện tại của Quán quân Đường Lên Đỉnh Olympia là Thủ khoa, từ chối việc lương cao ở nước ngoài để về nước
- 28-10-20264 điểm cầu chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026 đặt ở đâu?
Ra đời từ năm 1999, Đường Lên Đỉnh Olympia đến nay đã trở thành chương trình truyền hình gắn bó với nhiều thế hệ học sinh Việt Nam. Bên cạnh sức hút của những màn đấu trí căng thẳng, tiền thưởng dành cho nhà vô địch cũng nhận được nhiều sự quan tâm của khán giả.
Qua hơn 26 năm, chương trình đã có nhiều thay đổi về format, sân khấu và cách tổ chức. Đáng chú ý, giá trị giải thưởng dành cho nhà vô địch cũng được điều chỉnh theo từng giai đoạn, với 2 lần tăng đáng kể vào năm 2020 và 2023.
Trong 19 mùa đầu tiên, từ năm 1999 đến năm 2019, quán quân Đường Lên Đỉnh Olympia nhận suất học bổng du học trị giá 35.000 USD (hơn 900 triệu đồng). Mức thưởng này được duy trì trong thời gian dài, trở thành một trong những dấu ấn quen thuộc khi nhắc đến chương trình.
Bước ngoặt đầu tiên diễn ra vào năm 2020, khi Đường Lên Đỉnh Olympia bước sang mùa thứ 20. Theo đó, trong khuôn khổ thỏa thuận tiếp tục đồng hành cùng chương trình, nhà tài trợ THACO quyết định tăng giá trị các giải thưởng. Trong đó, học bổng du học dành cho quán quân được nâng từ 35.000 USD lên 40.000 USD (hơn 1 tỷ đồng).
Mức thưởng mới được áp dụng ngay tại trận chung kết năm thứ 20, diễn ra ngày 20/9/2020. Nguyễn Thị Thu Hằng, học sinh Trường THPT Kim Sơn A, Ninh Bình, giành vòng nguyệt quế với 235 điểm và trở thành quán quân đầu tiên nhận suất học bổng trị giá 40.000 USD.
Sau lần điều chỉnh này, mức học bổng dành cho nhà vô địch tiếp tục được giữ ở 40.000 USD trong các mùa tiếp theo. Tuy nhiên, đến năm 2023, giải thưởng lại có bước tăng mới. Cụ thể, Quán quân Đường Lên Đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 23 nhận giải thưởng trị giá 50.000 USD (hơn 1,2 tỷ đồng theo tỷ giá hiện tại), cao hơn 10.000 USD so với mức áp dụng trước đó.
Tại cuộc thi năm ấy, Lê Xuân Mạnh, học sinh Trường THPT Hàm Rồng, Thanh Hóa, giành chiến thắng với 220 điểm. Nam sinh trở thành nhà vô địch đầu tiên nhận mức thưởng 50.000 USD, đồng thời được trao vòng nguyệt quế mạ vàng 24K.
Như vậy, nếu tính từ mức 35.000 USD trong 19 mùa đầu đến mức 50.000 USD từ năm 2023, giá trị học bổng dành cho quán quân đã tăng 15.000 USD, tương đương khoảng 42,9%. Riêng lần tăng từ 40.000 USD lên 50.000 USD tương ứng mức tăng 25%.
Những thay đổi về giá trị giải thưởng không chỉ dành cho người giành vòng nguyệt quế. Tại mùa thứ 20, tiền thưởng dành cho các vị trí còn lại trong trận chung kết năm cũng được điều chỉnh đáng kể. Cụ thể, từ năm 2020, thí sinh về nhì nhận 100 triệu đồng, tăng từ mức 20 triệu đồng trước đó. Hai thí sinh đồng giải ba nhận 50 triệu đồng mỗi người, thay cho mức 10 triệu đồng. Như vậy, tiền thưởng cho á quân và mỗi quý quân đều tăng gấp 5 lần so với trước.
Đến năm 2023, mức thưởng tiếp tục tăng khi thí sinh về nhì nhận 200 triệu đồng, trong khi mỗi thí sinh về ba nhận 100 triệu đồng. So với mức áp dụng từ năm 2020, cả hai mức thưởng đều tăng gấp đôi. Tại trận chung kết năm thứ 23, Nguyễn Trọng Thành giành giải nhì với phần thưởng 200 triệu đồng. Nguyễn Việt Thành và Nguyễn Minh Triết đồng giải ba, mỗi người nhận 100 triệu đồng.
Ngoài các giải thưởng dành cho trận chung kết năm, đợt điều chỉnh năm 2020 còn bao gồm việc tăng giá trị giải thưởng ở các cuộc thi tuần, tháng và quý. Điều đó cho thấy thay đổi không chỉ tập trung vào người chiến thắng cuối cùng mà còn mở rộng tới các chặng thi trước đó. Ở thời điểm chương trình đang chuẩn bị khép lại mùa thứ 26 bằng trận chung kết diễn ra ngày 1/11 tới đây, mức thưởng 50.000 USD vẫn là mốc cao nhất cho quán quân trong lịch sử Olympia.
Tổng hợp
Sức khỏe 24h

articles.title: CoreWeave and other neocloud stocks drop after Microsoft capex comes in below expectations
articles.text:
Shares of neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius dropped in extended trading as Microsoft's lower-than-expected capital expenditures figure points to infrastructure partners taking longer to deliver data center capacity.
Microsoft on Wednesday reported $45.2 billion worth of capex and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier, but below the $50.7 billion average analyst estimate, according to StreetAccount.
Microsoft is particularly reliant on neoclouds for capacity as it pours money into its artificial intelligence infrastructure. Microsoft inked a nearly $20 billion deal with Nebius at the tail end of last year for compute through the 2030s. It's also a top customer for CoreWeave.
Those companies and their peers have experienced a rocky few weeks on the market as rising interest rates led to concerns that future debt raises will be too expensive and lenders will start retreating.
In its earnings report, Microsoft said Azure revenue jumped 48% from a year earlier, far outpacing the increase in capex.
"Growth was higher than capital expenditures driven by timing differences between receipt of goods and payment and a lower mix of finance leases," Microsoft said its earnings deck.
CoreWeave and Nebius slid almost 5% after Microsoft's report. IREN fell about 3%.
Alphabet on Wednesday also reported capex numbers that fell short of estimates. The Google parent's capex totaled $51.36 billion, while analysts expected $55.09 billion.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, whose company rents AI infrastructure to Anthropic and Google, predicted over the weekend that more than 200 neocloud companies will collapse, posting on X that "debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers."
And last Monday, analysts at Gartner shared with CNBC its prediction that, by 2030, 80% of neocloud companies will either be absorbed or completely cease operations.
After a steep plunge this month, the neoclouds had been enjoying a modest recovery this week, with CoreWeave up 18% in the past three trading days to pace the gains. Analysts at Wolfe Research wrote in a report on Tuesday that they see the stock rebounding into the mid-$70s. It closed Wednesday at $63.93.
The infrastructure story gained some strength earlier on Wednesday as Oracle issued a strong long-term revenue forecast and said it will return to being free cash flow positive in the second half of next fiscal year. The stock jumped 11% in regular trading before retreating 3% following Microsoft's report.
—CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed to this report.

articles.title: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: Alphabet, Microsoft, Chipotle, ServiceNow, Fortinet & more
articles.text:
Market Insider
Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: Alphabet, Microsoft, Chipotle, ServiceNow, Fortinet & more
Here are some of the companies making headlines in extended trading. Maplebear — The company that owns Instacart gained 3% after sources familiar with the matter told CNBC that DoorDash's deal to buy the delivery service could arrive as soon as Thursday morning. DoorDash fell about 1%. Chipotle Mexican Grill — Shares gained more than 5% after the burrito chain reported same-store sales that beat estimates. Same-store sales in the third quarter grew 2.1%, versus the 1.5% increase analysts polled by FactSet anticipated. ServiceNow — The enterprise software company tumbled 15%. Third-quarter adjusted profit of $1 per share missed the LSEG consensus expectation of $1.02 a share Subscription revenue guidance for the fourth quarter ranged from $4.245 billion to $4.255 billion, while the FactSet consensus called for $4.25 billion. Fortinet — The cybersecurity company plummeted 25%. Non-GAAP gross margin for the third quarter came in at 79.6%, while analysts polled by LSEG sought 80.1%. Separately, top- and bottom-line results beat the Street's expectations. Microsoft – The software giant rose 2% after the company reported a beat on the top and bottom lines for its fiscal first-quarter earnings. Revenue came in at $92.28 billion, ahead of the $90.69 billion expected by LSEG. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings of $4.89 per share was better than the $4.73 expected by analysts. Revenue in the mega-cap's key Azure cloud business grew 48% year over year. Alphabet – Shares of the Google parent are down 9% in extended trading Wednesday after its third-quarter earnings showed the company posted negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion. Its core search revenue of $63.35 billion, missed the $64.96 billion estimate from analysts. Total company revenue of $127.58 billion also missed LSEG expectations of $128.22 billion. Align Technology — The maker of orthodontics and aesthetic dentistry products dropped 1% after fourth-quarter revenue guidance missed analysts' consensus estimates, according to FactSet data. The company also named Procter & Gamble alumna Jennifer Davis as its new CEO, effective Dec. 31. Sprouts Farmers Market — The Phoenix-based grocery chain plunged 18% after third-quarter earnings per share, revenue and same-store sales all trailed analysts' consensus estimates, according to FactSet data. Ford Motor — Shares fell nearly 2% after hours. The company reported third-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street's estimates but slightly missed on revenue. Adjusted earnings of 49 cents a share topped the LSEG consensus estimate of 40 cents per share, while revenue of $46.08 billion narrowly missed the $46.24 billion expected. FedEx — Shares fell almost 2% even as the delivery giant reported third quarter adjusted earnings that beat expectations. FedEx also said expects its full-year revenue growth at 12% year over year, up from the earlier call for an increase of roughly 11%, supported by stronger pricing and improved shipment volumes. Honeywell Aerospace — The aerospace company was down more than 2% even after raising its full-year outlook for pro forma standalone adjusted earnings per share, calling for $7.85 to $8. The company also announced an initial quarterly cash dividend of 40 cents per share. Carvana — The used car dealer climbed 10%. Carvana third-quarter revenue and adjusted EBITDA topped the numbers Wall Street had been expecting, and it said the Securities and Exchange Commission closed a previously disclosed investigation and would not take any enforcement action. CNBC's Paulina Likos, Scott Schnipper, Deena Zaidi and Nick Wells contributed reporting.

articles.title: Đúng 7h sáng nay, sân bay Phú Quốc ghi nhận một máy bay đặc biệt hạ cánh
articles.text:
Đúng 7h sáng nay, sân bay Phú Quốc ghi nhận một máy bay đặc biệt hạ cánh
Chiếc máy bay này có gì mà được nhận xét đặc biệt hơn máy bay khác?
Cảng hàng không quốc tế Phú Quốc, tỉnh An Giang vừa ghi nhận một sự kiện đáng chú ý khi chuyến bay thương mại đầu tiên sử dụng đường cất hạ cánh số 2 được đưa vào khai thác. Chuyến bay mang số hiệu 9G1955 của Sun PhuQuoc Airways được lựa chọn để đánh dấu cột mốc này, với thời gian hạ cánh vào lúc 7h05 ngày sáng 29/10.
Chuyến bay có hành trình từ sân bay Tân Sơn Nhất (TP.HCM) đến Phú Quốc. Điểm đặc biệt của chiếc máy bay không nằm ở việc sử dụng một dòng tàu bay hiếm gặp. Sự kiện đánh dấu việc một hạng mục hạ tầng hàng không quan trọng chính thức bước vào hoạt động sau nhiều tháng thi công, kiểm tra và hoàn thiện các điều kiện kỹ thuật.
Đây cũng là bước tiến trong lộ trình mở rộng Cảng hàng không quốc tế Phú Quốc, hướng tới vận hành đồng thời hai đường cất hạ cánh cùng nhà ga hành khách T2 từ tháng 5/2027, phục vụ Tuần lễ Cấp cao APEC 2027.
Đường băng dài 3.300 m hoàn thành chỉ sau 8 tháng
Đường cất hạ cánh số 2 dài 3.300 m, rộng 45 m, đáp ứng tiêu chuẩn Code E của Tổ chức Hàng không dân dụng quốc tế (ICAO). Công trình được trang bị hệ thống hạ cánh chính xác ILS/DME và hệ thống đèn hiệu CAT II, hỗ trợ máy bay tiếp cận, hạ cánh trong điều kiện tầm nhìn hạn chế theo tiêu chuẩn khai thác được phê duyệt.
Với các thông số kỹ thuật này, đường băng có khả năng tiếp nhận những dòng máy bay thân rộng như Boeing 787, Airbus A350, Boeing 777 và phục vụ tàu bay Code F theo điều kiện khai thác phù hợp.
Đáng chú ý, công trình hoàn thành sau 8 tháng thi công trong điều kiện đặc thù của đảo Phú Quốc. Sun Group phối hợp với hơn 20 nhà thầu, đơn vị tư vấn triển khai dự án giữa những khó khăn về thời tiết, nguồn nhân lực và vận chuyển vật tư bằng đường biển.
Theo chủ đầu tư, hơn 6.000 kỹ sư, công nhân trên toàn dự án làm việc theo ba ca, bốn kíp để bảo đảm tiến độ. Trong thời gian thi công, sân bay Phú Quốc vẫn duy trì hoạt động, với sản lượng chuyến bay tăng khoảng 45% so với cùng kỳ.
Trước khi được chấp thuận khai thác, đường băng trải qua nhiều bước kiểm tra, đánh giá kỹ thuật và bay hiệu chuẩn. Cụ thể theo Tổng công ty Quản lý bay Việt Nam (VATM), hoạt động bay kiểm tra, hiệu chuẩn được triển khai qua hai đợt vào cuối tháng 7 và đầu tháng 9/2026, sử dụng máy bay Beechcraft King Air 350.
VATM cũng xác nhận đã hoàn tất công tác chuẩn bị về dịch vụ bảo đảm hoạt động bay, sẵn sàng phục vụ việc đưa đường cất hạ cánh số 2 tại sân bay Phú Quốc vào khai thác thường xuyên từ ngày 29/10.
Phú Quốc chuẩn bị có đường băng dài 3.500 m, đón được Airbus A380
Việc đưa đường cất hạ cánh số 2 vào sử dụng cũng mở đầu giai đoạn nâng cấp tiếp theo tại sân bay Phú Quốc. Theo kế hoạch, sau khi đường băng mới đi vào khai thác, đường cất hạ cánh số 1 hiện hữu sẽ tạm đóng để nâng cấp, kéo dài từ 3.000 m lên 3.500 m.
Tổng chiều rộng đường băng sau nâng cấp dự kiến đạt 75 m, gồm 45 m mặt đường bê tông và lề đường nhựa rộng 15 m mỗi bên. Công trình sau khi hoàn thành sẽ đủ điều kiện tiếp nhận các loại tàu bay thân rộng Code F như Boeing 747-8F và Airbus A380-800.
Trong đó, Airbus A380 là dòng máy bay chở khách hai tầng cỡ lớn, còn Boeing 747-8F là dòng máy bay vận tải hàng hóa thân rộng. Khả năng tiếp nhận những dòng máy bay này sẽ mở rộng năng lực phục vụ các chuyến bay quốc tế quy mô lớn tại Phú Quốc.
Trong khoảng 6 tháng thi công nâng cấp, hoạt động cất hạ cánh được chuyển sang đường băng số 2 nhằm duy trì khai thác trong mùa bay Đông 2026–2027, khi tần suất chuyến bay được dự báo tăng khoảng 34%.
Đường băng số 1 dự kiến trở lại hoạt động từ tháng 5/2027. Khi đó, sân bay Phú Quốc sẽ có hai đường cất hạ cánh với chiều dài lần lượt 3.500 m và 3.300 m, giúp tăng tính linh hoạt trong điều hành bay.
Cùng thời điểm, nhà ga hành khách T2 cũng dự kiến được đưa vào khai thác. Công trình do CPG Consultants (Singapore) thiết kế, lấy cảm hứng từ hình tượng phượng hoàng lửa, tích hợp các công nghệ như sinh trắc học, xử lý hành lý tự động và quầy làm thủ tục tự phục vụ.
Theo thỏa thuận hợp tác chiến lược ký ngày 21/3/2026, Changi Airports International sẽ tham gia quản lý, vận hành sân bay Phú Quốc, hỗ trợ nâng cao hiệu quả khai thác và phát triển kết nối quốc tế.
Theo dự kiến của doanh nghiệp, năm 2027, sân bay Phú Quốc có thể phục vụ khoảng 13,5 triệu lượt khách, trong đó hơn một nửa là khách quốc tế. Giai đoạn 1, sân bay hướng tới công suất 24 triệu lượt khách mỗi năm và có thể mở rộng lên 50 triệu lượt trong dài hạn.
Việc hoàn thiện hệ thống hai đường cất hạ cánh cùng nhà ga T2 được kỳ vọng tạo nền tảng để Phú Quốc phục vụ Tuần lễ Cấp cao APEC 2027, đồng thời nâng cao khả năng kết nối đảo ngọc với các thị trường quốc tế.
Việt Nam hàng ngày
